In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined:
The principal advised the boy to come to grips with himself if he wanted to do well at the
end of his course.

questions.e: To 'come down heavily on' someone is to punish or criticise them severely, here by imposing a stiff penalty.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined:
The judge came down heavily on the accused person in his judgement

questions.e: A 'white elephant' is a costly possession or project that brings little benefit.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the underlined word or
phrase:
The government should stop white elephant projects
o: projects in which white men kill elephants
projects in which white elephants are used
projects for painting some elephants white
high cost projects with low utility values
low cost projects with high utility values

questions.e: Being 'free' to leave means being 'at liberty' to do so.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
You are free to leave the hall

questions.e: To 'surrender' something is to 'give it up' to authorities.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
The culprit will surrender their loot to the Customs officials

questions.e: An 'animated' discussion is lively and full of energy.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
The discussion became animated

questions.e: 'Niggardly' means stingy, i.e. miserly.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
The rich citizens are often niggardly in their ways

questions.e: To 'decline' is to become less, i.e. to 'wane'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
The musician's popularity is beginning to decline

questions.e: 'Look out for' can mean to protect or take care of someone, which is the meaning the key takes here; it can also mean watch for.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
Olu promised to look out for her next time he is in town.

questions.e: A 'prosecution' witness testifies for the side bringing the case, which in a criminal trial is the government (state).
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word or phrase
underlined:
Thompson was a prosecution witness at the court hearing

questions.e: 'Snowballed' means increased rapidly, like a snowball rolling and growing, so his takings grew.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The beggar's takings snow-belled every hour.

questions.e: To 'nip something in the bud' is to stop it at an early stage, i.e. cut it short.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
His attempts were nipped in the bud

questions.e: To 'make good' a promise is to fulfil it.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The preacher has made good his promise to visit some of his converts today

questions.e: 'Watch it!' is a warning to be careful and alert, i.e. vigilant.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
'Watch it! You could be followed said the robber

questions.e: 'Tell-tale' signs are those that reveal something hidden, i.e. revealing marks.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Look at the tell-tale signs of battering on her

questions.e: To 'come to grief' is an idiom meaning to meet with disaster or a bad end. It does not mean literally feeling grief, so options B and C are too literal.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The armed robbers who raided passengers on the Expressway came to grief when they had
a shoot out with the police today

questions.e: The pun here contrasts 'firing the furnace' with 'had themselves fired', which means they were dismissed from work. Option C is correctly worded; D misuses 'there' for 'their'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Many of the workers hired for firing the furnace had themselves fired as a result of the
unfortunate accident
o: got themselves sacked from their jobs

questions.e: When a system or project 'takes off', it begins or gets started. 'Resumed' and 'continued' wrongly suggest it had existed before.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The new educational system took off this school year

questions.e: To 'buy an idea' is an informal expression meaning to accept or agree with it; no money or trade is involved.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
We will surely buy this idea of introducing an entirely new product

questions.e: 'Surplus' means an amount beyond what is needed, i.e. more than enough. 'Enough for need' misses the excess, and 'limitless' exaggerates.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
This year's harvest is surplus

questions.e: 'Lucrative' means producing a lot of money or profit. Option A fits and agrees with the singular subject; 'quick money' adds a speed idea not in the word.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Many candidates now apply to read Law because it is a lucrative profession.

questions.e: A statement made 'off the record' is unofficial and not meant to be published or quoted, which is option B.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The pressman said that his interview with the Presidents was off the record.
o: not written on government record books
written elsewhere other than the government records

questions.e: To be 'up against' something means to be faced with a difficulty or opponent, here strong competition from the new store.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
She realized that she was up against stiff competition when a new large department store
was opened next to her small provision store

questions.e: To 'go back on one's word' is an idiom meaning to break a promise. The other options interpret 'word' literally.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Finally, I assured him that i would not go back on my word.
o: return to certain word when reading

questions.e: To 'look up to' someone means to respect or admire them. 'Look up at' only describes the direction of looking.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Everybody respects the team leader.

questions.e: 'Hesitant' means unwilling or slow to act because of doubt, which matches 'reluctant'. The driver could start the engine but was unwilling to, so 'unable' is wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The driver, on seeing the traffic warden, was hesitant to start the engine.

questions.e: 'Trivial' means of little importance or value, exactly matching 'unimportant'. 'Incidental' means minor but connected; 'dubious' means doubtful.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
He likes to call attention to unimportant matters

questions.e: To take someone 'down memory lane' means to remind them of past events, so the speaker recalled the past. Memory lane is not a real street.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The speaker took his audience down memory lane before he went to the topic of his lecture
o: Took his audience on a journey through a street called memory lane
told a tale about a place called memory lane
gave an outline of his lecture

questions.e: Holding out an 'olive branch' is a symbol of making peace with opponents, so the leader is seeking peace.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The new religious leader hands out an olives branch.
o: gives out branches of the olive tree
challenges his opponents to a fight

questions.e: To 'lose one's tongue' means to be unable to speak, often from shyness or nervousness. Binta was not literally dumb; she was simply too shy to speak.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
Though a brilliant student, Binta lost her tongue when she was asked to give the vote of
thanks at the end of the Governor's visit to her school.
o: said nothing because she was shy

questions.e: To 'cook the books' is an idiom for falsifying financial records, usually for personal gain, which is why the clerk was jailed.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The accounts clerk was jailed because he cooked the books
o: set fire to the account books
sold the books in his office to get money for food
falsified the accounts to his advantage
destroyed the accounts books by cooking them

questions.e: 'Herculean' describes a task needing enormous strength or effort, like the labours of Hercules, so it means very demanding.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The task was herculean

questions.e: 'Incredible' means hard to believe and describes the story. 'Incredulous' describes a person who does not believe something, so it cannot describe the story.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The story is rather hard to believe

questions.e: To 'administer' a test means to give it to candidates. 'Set' means to prepare the questions, and 'undertake' means to take it oneself.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
It is advisable to administer the test in the morning when students are fresh

questions.e: 'Ostensibly' means apparently or seemingly, describing what appears to be true but is not, as shown by 'although he was actually enjoying the commotion'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
He broke his mallet ostensibly trying to maintain order although he was actually enjoying
the commotion.

questions.e: Being 'entitled to' something means having the right to receive it, which is the sense of 'eligible'. 'Disqualified from' is the opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the Underlined word(s) or
phrase:Ít is very difficult to know who is not entitled to essential commodities these days'
observed the mobbed NNSC officials

questions.e: A 'miniaturized' version is a much smaller copy of the original. 'Abridged' applies to shortened texts, and 'compressed' means squeezed.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:'This is a miniaturized version of your house' remarked the Architect.

questions.e: In geography an 'extinct' volcano is one that is no longer active and not expected to erupt. 'Inactive' best captures this; 'extinguished' refers to put-out fires.
questions.s:
In the question below, choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
It is claimed that there is an extinct volcano near Pankshin.

questions.e: A 'sonorous' voice is deep, full and loud, so 'strong' is closest. It is not high-pitched, and 'beautiful' is too vague.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
Bola has a sonorous voice.

questions.e: To go 'on (the) rampage' means to rush about behaving violently and destructively, so the workers turned violent.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
Some workers went on rampage at a trade-fair.

questions.e: 'Protagonists' of a movement are its main supporters or leading figures. They are not enemies or opponents, and 'believers' is too general.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
We have to identify the protagonists of the new movement

questions.e: 'Stealthily' means moving quietly and secretly to avoid being noticed. 'Boldly' and 'briskly' suggest the opposite manner.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
My nephew came in stealthily through the back gate

questions.e: 'As the crow flies' means measured in a straight line, i.e. by the shortest direct route, not following roads.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
The distance is not more than twenty kilometres as the crow flies

questions.e: To 'infuriate' is to make someone very angry, so 'annoys' is closest. 'Frustrates' means to block or discourage, which is a different idea.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
Your extreme patience sometimes infuriates me

questions.e: 'Audacious' means daring, bold and willing to take risks. It can suggest rudeness but its core meaning is bold.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
I cannot understand how he suddenly became audacious contrary to his nature

questions.e: 'Make-believe' means pretending or imagining things that are not real, which is fantasy.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
He as been a life of make-belief

questions.e: 'Seldom' means rarely, which matches 'hardly ever'. 'Very often', 'always' and 'frequently' are the opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
Our teacher seldom comes late to school

questions.e: To 'put the clock back' means to return to an earlier time; at 80, Musa wished he could go back in time to his youth.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:At the age of 80, Musa wished he could put the clock back.

questions.e: Doing something 'in good faith' means acting honestly and trusting the other person, so the Director left the file in trust.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
The Director left his secret file to the Secretary in good faith

questions.e: 'Disinterestedness' means being impartial, with no personal stake in the matter. It does not mean boredom, which is 'uninterested'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
The Chief approached the issue with convincing disinterestedness.

questions.e: 'Miscellaneous' duties are varied and of different kinds, i.e. assorted. They are not necessarily confidential or unscheduled.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
Nothing irritates the clerk more, than being assigned miscellaneous duties.

questions.e: 'Fundamental' means forming the base or core of something, i.e. basic and essential.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
It is of fundamental importance that one sleeps properly.

questions.e: 'Eavesdropping' means secretly listening to other people's private conversations.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
I know you've been eaves-dropping all along.

questions.e: An 'affected' interest is put on or pretended, not genuine. 'Real' is the opposite of this sense.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
She showed an affected interest in the game.

questions.e: 'Piecemeal' means done gradually in separate small parts, bit by bit, rather than all at once.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
I would not like you to do the work piecemeal

questions.e: To 'reiterate' means to say something again, i.e. to repeat points already made.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
I think i'll like to reiterate the points earlier made.

questions.e: To 'put paid to' something means to bring it to an end, so the king's death terminated the Minister's ambition.
questions.s:
In the question below, choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
underlined:
The sudden death of the king put paid to the ambition of the Minister.

questions.e: 'Strings attached' are special conditions or limitations in an agreement. 'No strings attached' means no conditions.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase
Underlined:
The man insisted on having no strings attached to the agreements

questions.e: 'Fast friends' are close, loyal friends who stick together. Here 'fast' means firmly fixed, not quick or not eating.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
Ngozi and Ekaette were fast friends when we were in the secondary school
o: friends who run very quickly together
friends who go without food for a long time together
friends who are not easily separated from each other
friends who spend too much time and energy on pleasure and excitement together

questions.e: To be 'rusticated' means to be suspended from a university for a period as punishment for misconduct.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:My son has just been rusticated from the university
o: sent home to get his fees
sent home to rest for some time

questions.e: A 'concerted' effort is one made jointly by several people working together. 'Concentrated' is a common confusion but means focused.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
All we need is a concerted effort to combat the epidemic

questions.e: 'Cupboard love' is affection shown only to get something, such as food or money, from the other person.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
Jimoh has cupboard love for Sidikatu
o: love for what he wants from her
love that can fail in time of trouble

questions.e: To know 'which side one's bread is buttered' means to know where one's own advantage or interest lies.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:Yahaya hardly knows on which side his bread is buttered in the matter

questions.e: Being 'under a cloud' means being out of favour or under suspicion. 'Under the weather' means ill.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The preacher is under a cloud among the congregation

questions.e: To 'play to the gallery' means to behave in a showy way to win popular approval, appealing to the tastes of ordinary people.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The politician played to the gallery to win the election
o: sang a good song for the people
went out of his way to appeal to the taste of the people

questions.e: To 'snuff out' a flame or cigarette means to extinguish it completely. 'Put down' only means to lay it aside.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The hefty warder came in and all the prisoners snuffed out their cigarettes

questions.e: To 'wane' means to gradually decrease or decline in strength or popularity.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The popularity of the slogan is beginning to wane

questions.e: 'Dyed-in-the-wool' means firmly fixed in one's habits and unlikely to change, so a hardened convict.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The policeman looked at the face of the robber and saw tell-tale signs of a dyed-in-the wool
convict.

questions.e: If someone 'bears watching', they need to be watched closely, usually because they may be dangerous or untrustworthy.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
'Marcus bears watching; remarked Emperor Nero.

questions.e: To 'carry the can' means to accept responsibility or blame, often for others' faults, as the prefect did by refusing to name the culprit.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The senior prefect had to carry the can because he refused to identify the culprit
o: be made one of the scape goat

questions.e: To 'set the cat among the pigeons' means to say or do something that causes trouble, controversy and confusion.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The senior had the habit of setting the cat among the pigeon whenever matters concerning
his constituency came up for debate
o: illuminating issues that are not clear
making frequent interruptions in the nature of points of correction
introducing elements of controversy and confusion

questions.e: Being 'off colour' means feeling slightly unwell, which explains Adah's absence from lectures. It has nothing to do with skin colour.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:Adah has not been regular at lectures because she has been off colour
o: trying to hide her bleached skin

questions.e: To 'crack up' means to suffer a mental or emotional breakdown, so the grieving man became mentally unstable. 'Broken-hearted' describes sorrow without loss of mental balance.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
When the man lost his two sons in a motor accident, he cracked up

questions.e: 'Crestfallen' means sad and disappointed after a setback, i.e. dejected. 'Elated' is its opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below, choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
underlined:
The news of his performance in the sessional examination has made Okechukwu crestfallen.

questions.e: The idiom is 'cut no ice', meaning to have no effect or fail to influence someone. The son was not moved by the rebuke.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The man rebuked his son severely, but his words seem to have cut on ice

questions.e: The 'nucleus' of something is its central and most important part, i.e. its core. 'Cell' is too literal a biological sense.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The urban environment tends to form the nucleus of a common dialect.

questions.e: 'Presently' in British usage means soon or shortly, i.e. in a moment. 'At present' means now, a common confusion.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
I shall be with you presently

questions.e: 'Superfluous' means more than is needed, i.e. too much or excessive. It does not mean excellent or superlative.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The builder's taste reflected superfluous grandeur

questions.e: To 'make a clean sweep' means to remove completely, so the boss got rid of all the old staff.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The boss made a clean sweep of all old hands in the office

questions.e: 'Apparent' means clearly seen or understood, i.e. visible to everyone. 'Transparent' means see- through, a more literal sense.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
Her anxiety was apparent to everyone present at the ceremony

questions.e: 'Nothing to write home about' means ordinary and not impressive or remarkable.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
Our experience on board the aircraft is nothing to write home about

questions.e: 'Militant' means aggressive and ready to fight for a cause, i.e. belligerent. It does not mean soldiers.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:The rampage was organized and directed by the militant ones among the
students

questions.e: To get 'off the beaten track' means to depart from the usual way of doing things and find new approaches.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The governor advised his people to get off the beaten tracks in their approach to community
matters

questions.e: To 'keep open house' means to welcome visitors at any time, offering them hospitality.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:It was their custom to keep an open house on Sundays

questions.e: A 'passionate' appeal is made with strong feeling, i.e. intense. 'Inflamed' suggests anger, which contradicts an appeal for calm.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The president made a passionate appeal for calm

questions.e: 'Takings' are the money received by a business from sales over a period, i.e. its receipts.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
Mali stole the day's takings from the bakery.

questions.e: To 'stutter' means to speak with involuntary pauses and repetitions, the same as 'stammer'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
You do not need to stutter in order to show your excitement

questions.e: 'Stealthy' means acting secretly and quietly to avoid notice, which matches 'furtive'. 'Boisterous' means noisy, the opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
what embarrasses is the stealthy way in which the new servant goes about his duties in the
house

questions.e: 'Pensive' means deeply or seriously thoughtful, often with some sadness.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined: I have never been accustomed to seeing my brother in such a pensive mood

questions.e: 'Apathy' is a lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern, i.e. indifference. 'Concern' is its opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined: The administrator's apathy was soon noticed by all his subordinates.

questions.e: 'Despicable' means deserving hatred and contempt, i.e. contemptible.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:The way he handled the whole issue was rather despicable

questions.e: 'Authenticity' means the quality of being real or true, i.e. genuineness.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The authenticity of the reporter's claims should be established before taking further actions
on the matter

questions.e: 'No iota of' means not even the smallest amount. 'Grain', as in 'not a grain of truth', has the same sense of a tiny quantity.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
underlined:
After careful investigation, the police found no iota of truth in Ibrahim's allegations

questions.e: 'Jurisdiction' is the official power or authority of a court to hear and decide a case.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word(s) or phrase(s)
Underlined:
The case was thrown out because the court lacked jurisdiction

questions.e: To 'launch' an appeal means to start it off or set it going officially.

a tool or something to sharpen
a bone to pick with someone

questions.e: "Momentous" means of great importance or consequence; it has nothing to do with whether the decision is voluntary.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
He might be compelled to take a momentous decision?

questions.e: "Every cloud has a silver lining" means every bad situation has some good aspect or hope in it.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
The principal advised the students to bear with him in their present situation since every
cloud has a silver lining?
o: every bad situation has something good

questions.e: "Still waters run deep" means quiet people often have deep thoughts or wisdom, so there is wisdom in silence.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
Oche's mother advised him to talk very little because still waters run deep?
o: there is no pride in talking too much
talking too much could lead him into trouble

questions.e: "A dog's breakfast" is an informal idiom for something done very badly and untidily, i.e. a mess.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
Akin made such a dog's breakfast of his home work?

questions.e: "In a spot" is an informal idiom meaning in trouble or a difficult situation, which fits a confused student.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
The confused student found himself in a spot?

questions.e: Speaking "tongue in cheek" means saying something ironically or not seriously, often with hidden humour.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
The man who gave the closing remarks at the party spoke tongue in cheek?

questions.e: "Classified advertisements" are small adverts grouped by category in newspapers; "classified" here does not mean secret.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
New companies in the country always put up classified advertisements in the dailies.

questions.e: "Prophylactic" drugs are given to prevent disease, so they are preventive rather than curative.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
The doctor insisted on giving all of us prophylactic drugs.

questions.e: To "moot" an idea is to raise or suggest it for discussion, so the delegates proposed the transfer.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
The delegates to the Constitutional Conference have mooted that funding of universities be
transferred to states where they are located?

questions.e: Plans that are "in the air" are undecided and uncertain, not yet settled.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
Adebayo's plans for the future are in the air?

questions.e: "Choreography" is the art of designing dance movements, so it refers to a form of dancing.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The group of performers thrilled the audience with its peculiar choreography.

questions.e: "Incisive" means sharp, clear and penetrating in analysis. It does not mean sarcastic or destructive.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
Our local paper is noted for its incisive editorials on local politics?

questions.e: "Not bat an eyelid" is an idiom meaning to show no emotion or surprise at all.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The criminal didn't bat an eyelid when the judge pronounced the sentence.

questions.e: "Apolitical" means not interested or involved in politics; the prefix a- means "not".
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The rally was attended only by people who were apolitical?

questions.e: To "take exception to" something is to object to it or be offended by it.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
Smiling broadly, she explained why she always took exception to being referred to as his
wife?

questions.e: "Putting on airs" means behaving in a proud, showy way to impress others with one's importance.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
In those days, an ordinary school drop-out would come around putting on airs?

questions.e: To "inure" oneself to hardship is to become accustomed to it, so it no longer seems so painful.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
Many Nigerians have inured themselves to hardship?

questions.e: "Venal" describes someone who can be bribed, i.e. corrupt. It is the opposite of honest.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
There are many venal judges in our law courts today?

questions.e: "Nefarious" means wicked or criminal, and such activities are despicable, deserving contempt. "Nocturnal" means active at night.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
He is bound to expose himself by his nefarious activities?

questions.e: "Be in bed by ten o'clock" means at or before ten, i.e. not later than ten.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
In this house, children are supposed to be in bed by ten o'clock?

questions.e: "Don't have to" expresses lack of obligation, not prohibition, so you are free to disagree if you wish. "Must not" would be a ban.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
You don't have to agree with our procedure?
o: may not disagree if you dont wish

questions.e: "You don't have to" means there is no obligation, so the listener may disagree if they wish. It is not a prohibition like "must not".
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
You don't have to agree with our procedure?
o: may not disagree if you dont wish

questions.e: To "tide over" a difficulty is to manage or get through it for a short time until things improve, i.e. to deal with it temporarily.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The new Vice-Chancellor's immediate concern was to tide over the major difficulties of the
moment.

questions.e: "Evasive" answers avoid giving a direct reply. "Equivocal" means deliberately unclear or ambiguous, which matches.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The lawyer gave evasive answers to all the questions?

questions.e: "Staggering" means astonishing or overwhelming, and capacity to reproduce is multiplying power: an overwhelming multiplying power.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
Their strength is their staggering capacity to reproduce?

questions.e: In an auction, the "upset price" is the lowest price at which the seller will sell an item, i.e. the reserve price.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The sales were lively, the upset price in each case was fair?
o: price that was the highest in the sales
price that upset every other buyer
highest amount for a bidder to offer
lowest selling price of each item

questions.e: A "trivial round" is a dull, repetitive series of everyday tasks, so the job had become too routine.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The cleaner resigned from his job which he said had become a trivial round?

questions.e: "Enchanting" means charming and delightfully attractive, so the island becomes more attractive at night. "Lively" describes activity, not charm.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined words.
The island becomes more enchanting at night.

questions.e: "Invulnerable" means impossible to harm or injure. Being hard to catch or indifferent to danger is a different idea.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
For a long time, the robber defied police warnings as if he was invulnerable?

questions.e: An "eclectic" framework draws ideas from many different sources, so it is broad rather than restricted.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The material in the book is presented within an eclectic framework?

questions.e: A "brainwave" is a sudden clever idea, so she had an idea for dealing with the problem.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Ohiokhen had a brainwave as to how she could deal with the problem?

questions.e: "A ball of fire" is an idiom for a very energetic, enthusiastic person, not someone quarrelsome or hot-headed.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Surely, Ahmed is a ball of fire?

questions.e: A "dark horse" is a competitor about whom little is known but who may surprise everyone by doing well.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
This time, she will be competing with a dark horse?
o: a person about whom little is known
a person as strong as a horse

questions.e: "It never rains but it pours" means misfortunes come together in quick succession, so things are getting decidedly worse.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
In answer to the question as to how life is treating him, the stranger said 'it never rains but
it pours?
o: the blessings of life shower on him like heavy rain
he is contented with his improved fortunes

questions.e: To "cut corners" means to do something the easiest or quickest way, skipping necessary steps or effort; the key reads this as avoiding necessary hardships.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
One significant characteristic of the jet is that it encourages people to cut corners?
o: to want to become rich quickly
to want to avoid necessary hardships
not to do the proper thing at the right time

questions.e: "Gait" is a person's manner of walking. "Carriage" means the way a person holds and moves the body, the closest match; "stature" refers to height.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The lady who won the beauty contest had a good gait.

questions.e: A "high flyer" is a person of great ability who is likely to be very successful, so in a university it means an outstanding scholar.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
It would need a high flyer to make a first class degree in the university.

questions.e: To "stew in one's own juice" is to be left to suffer the consequences of one's own actions without help.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Any student found guilty of examination malpractice should be allowed to stew in his juice.
o: taste a repeat of the examination
suffer the consequences of his action
bear the burnt of the disgrace
forfeit the opportunity of further education

questions.e: A "bird's eye view" is a broad overview seen as if from above, so it is a general survey rather than a detailed account.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
What you find in the book is a bird's eye view of the subject?

questions.e: A "minefield" is a situation full of hidden dangers, so a political minefield invites political problems.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
If experience is anything to go by, this action will prove a political minefield?
o: a way out of political trouble

questions.e: A "chequered" career has had both good and bad periods, i.e. a career full of ups and downs.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Hers was a chequered career​.
o: a career full of sorrow and tears
a career full of ups and down

questions.e: When a plan or performance "comes off", it succeeds. "Didn't come off" therefore means the play did not succeed.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
In my view, the play didn't **come off**?

questions.e: "When the chips are down" means when a situation becomes critical or a crisis point is reached.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
When the chips are down, we will know those who have the courage to stand?
o: When we get to a crisis point
When we get to end of the road

questions.e: The phrasal verb "come off" means to succeed or happen as planned, so the underlined phrase is nearest to "succeed".
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
In my view, the play didn't come off?

questions.e: A "pet aversion" (like a pet hate) is something a person particularly dislikes.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
She said boxing is in fact her pet aversion?
o: a hobby she loves to pursue

questions.e: "Perfunctorily" means doing something with minimum effort and no real interest, i.e. without commitment.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The gateman does his work perfunctorily?

questions.e: Working "at cross purposes" means misunderstanding each other or aiming at different goals, so the panel was in disunity.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Members of the panel were working at cross purposes?

questions.e: To "repudiate" someone is to reject them or refuse to be associated with them, i.e. disown them.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The young man who distributed political pamphlets on campus was promptly repudiated.

questions.e: A "die-hard" criminal is stubbornly fixed in his ways and refuses to change or feel sorry, i.e. remorseless.
questions.s:
Choose the most appropriate option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Adayi is a die-hard criminal?

questions.e: "Profusely" means in great quantity, abundantly, so they are bleeding excessively.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
All the accident victims are bleeding profusely?

questions.e: To "obstruct" is to block or get in the way, i.e. to hinder justice. "Retarding" only means slowing down.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The prosecutor was accused of obstructing justice?

questions.e: Egalitarianism is the view that everyone is equal and should enjoy the same rights, so its closest meaning is equality.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The man preaches egalitarianism without matching it up with action?

questions.e: An "incentive" is something that motivates or encourages people to work harder, i.e. an encouragement.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
The Federal Government approved a new salary structure as an incentive for the Nigerian
workers?

questions.e: A "doting" husband shows great, even excessive, love and affection, so he is a loving husband.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Amina said she married a doting husband.

questions.e: To "hit the jackpot" means to win a large prize or suddenly make a lot of money.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
It was a spending spree for all of us when daddy hit the jackpot?

questions.e: To "take to" someone is to begin to like them, so we formed a liking for the stranger.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
It was surprising how we took the stranger at once?

questions.e: A "feasibility" study checks whether a plan is practical and achievable, i.e. its practicability.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Before embarking on his current research, the professor carried out a feasibility study of
the area.

questions.e: "Credentials" are documents proving one's qualifications or achievements, so the officer asked to see qualifications.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
The college Officer insisted that I show him my credentials before I could be registered?

questions.e: A "restive" atmosphere is uneasy and close to unrest, i.e. tense, even though no riot has broken out.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
Even though there is no obvious riot on the campus, the atmosphere is restive?

questions.e: "Dexterity" is skill in using the hands, which suits playing the piano.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
Mr. Dzokoto plays the piano with great dexterity?

questions.e: To have something "up one's sleeve" is to keep a secret plan in reserve, i.e. to be nursing a hidden agenda.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word (S).
The government is not opening up to the unions in the negotiations; it must have something
up its sleeve.
o: be nursing a hidden a last agenda
be hiding a last minute package
be intending to dissolve the unions

questions.e: Something "on his trail" is following or pursuing him, i.e. giving him the chase, which is why he ran.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Adamu woke up with a start, and he took to his heels, claiming that something was on his
trail?

questions.e: "Double-talk" is deliberately confusing or misleading speech, so he mixed up facts to confuse people.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined world(S).
When he found himself in a difficult situation, he tried to double-talk his way through?
o: talk to two people to help him
mix up issues to sound nervous
mix up facts to confuse people

questions.e: To "circumvent" is to find a way around a rule or obstacle, i.e. to bypass it, not openly confront it.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
They have tried to circumvent the restriction on the importation of the commodities.

questions.e: A "routine" tour is a normal, regular one done as part of usual duties, not a surprise or special visit.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The Governor told the chief that he was only on a routine tour.

questions.e: "Several" means more than two but not very many, used with countable nouns such as pints, so "many" is closest.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The boy was told that he would need several more pints of blood if he was to survive.

questions.e: To "browbeat" is to intimidate someone with harsh words or threats, i.e. to bully them.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The principal told the teacher to stop browbeating the children.

questions.e: To "alienate" people is to make them feel estranged or distant, and those who were "sympathetic" were well disposed towards the youth.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
Some actions of the Nigerian youth have alienated them from those who were sympathetic
to their cause.

questions.e: "Nebulous" means cloudy or unclear, i.e. vague. "Distinct" and "clear" are opposites.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The essay topic is nebulous.

questions.e: "Wilful and obstinate" describes someone stubborn who insists on her own way, i.e. unyielding and obdurate.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The man was able to persuade his willful and obstinate daughter to follow the career he
chose for her.

questions.e: An "eagle-eyed" person notices small details quickly, so an eagle-eyed editor is quick-sighted, spotting errors at once.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
Mr. Okon has been described as an eagle-eyed editor.

questions.e: 'Pleasantries' are light, friendly or joking remarks made in polite conversation, so the nearest meaning is 'jocular remarks'. Condolence messages express sympathy and are not pleasantries. The correct option is D.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
In spite of her grim situation, the young widow smiled dutifully at the visitor's pleasantries.

questions.e: "Impassioned" means full of strong feeling, so she is emotional. Note that "impassive" means showing no emotion, the opposite.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
I have always believed that my mother is a very impassioned woman.

questions.e: "Euphoria" is a state of intense happiness and excitement, as after an election victory.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The party gathering was thrown into a state of euphoria after the election result was
announced.

questions.e: To "nail a lie to the counter" is to expose it publicly as false, as traders once nailed fake coins to the counter.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The family discussed the crime committed and resolved to nail the lie to the counter.

questions.e: The "apogee" is the highest point or peak, so he retired at the height of his career.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
My father was at the apogee of his career when he was retired.

questions.e: "Serious" here means grave, i.e. causing concern because it is dangerous. "Nasty" is too informal, and "hypertensive" refers to blood pressure.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
Though David's condition is serious, his life is not in immediate danger.

questions.e: "Fatal" means causing death, i.e. deadly.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
That punch by the young boxer proved to be fatal.

questions.e: "Respite" is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult, i.e. temporary relief.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The presence of the security men in the area will provide a moment of respite for the
residents.

questions.e: To "pick to pieces" is to examine something closely and critically, i.e. to analyse it critically.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
It is time for all concerned to first pick to pieces the strike action before proffering
solutions.

questions.e: A "big-hearted" person is kind and generous to others.
questions.s:
Choose from the options **nearest** in meaning to the word underlined.
The new ruler is big-hearted in his dealing with people

questions.e: "Moribund" means dying or in terminal decline, i.e. crumbling.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
I cannot understand why Ali should serve in that moribund administration.

questions.e: "Transients" are people who stay only briefly, i.e. temporary guests.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The conference Centre caters for transients only.

questions.e: "Coalescence" is the coming together of separate parts into one whole, i.e. union.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The coalescence of the groups created additional problems.

questions.e: A "reverse" in a military context is a setback or defeat.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
As the triumphant rebels were returning to their base they met with a serious reverse.

questions.e: "Sumptuous" means splendid and costly-looking, i.e. expensive.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The village girl wore sumptuous clothes.

questions.e: "Radical changes" are fundamental new reforms, which the key equates with innovations.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Any chief executive of an organisation would find radical changes blocked at every turn.

questions.e: "Belligerent" means hostile and eager to fight, i.e. combative.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Ugo has often been described as belligerent.

questions.e: "Tardy" means slow or late in acting.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The men were tardy in offering help.

questions.e: Being "facetious" is joking about serious matters in an inappropriate way, i.e. being unserious.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Funmi is just being facetious about her marrying a soldier.

questions.e: "Abstruse" means difficult to understand, obscure. "Esoteric", known only to a few specialists, is the closest match.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The professor discussed a number of abstruse topics.

questions.e: A "pilferer" is someone who steals small items, i.e. a petty thief.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Bose was angry because her friend called her pilferer.

questions.e: To look on "complacently" is to be self-satisfied and unconcerned about a problem, i.e. contentedly rather than sorrowfully.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
While the hooligans exchanged blows, we looked complacently.

questions.e: "Timorous" means showing fear or lack of confidence, i.e. nervous.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Tade became timorous when she was asked to give the valedictory speech.

questions.e: "Gamely" means bravely and with determination despite difficulty, i.e. courageously.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
The player kept on gamely to the end of the match.

questions.e: "Creative power" here refers to each person's capacity to create, i.e. their potential.
questions.s:
Choose the option **nearest in meaning** to the word underlined.
Art lies in cherishing the initiative and creative power of each person.

questions.e: "Think" here means to suppose or believe without proof, i.e. to assume. "Know" implies certainty.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Practicing medicine is not as lucrative as many people think?

questions.e: A "stringer" is a part-time journalist paid per story rather than a staff member, i.e. a freelancer for a newspaper.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
He is a stringer for a newspaper?

questions.e: "Adamant" means refusing to change one's mind (unyielding), and a "reprisal" attack is one made in retaliation (retaliatory).
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
I wish the commander were less adamant about his proposed reprisal attack on the enemy?

questions.e: To "hibernate" is to spend a cold season in a deep, dormant sleep.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Tortoises need cool climates and must have places where they can hibernate?

questions.e: "Disparaging" remarks belittle or criticise someone, i.e. they are derogatory. "Rude" lacks the sense of belittling.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The manager made disparaging remarks about the retiring officer?

questions.e: "Eerie" means strange and frightening, i.e. scary, which explains why the man ran.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The man outran his wife when they heard the eerie sound?

questions.e: "Therapeutic" means having a healing effect on body or mind.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Teachers of music believes in its therap.eutic effect?

questions.e: "Puerile" means silly and immature, i.e. childish.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
Adigun's jokes are always puerile?

questions.e: "Extraneous" material is irrelevant or not needed, i.e. superfluous. "Relevant" is the opposite.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
I wonder what will be left of his essay when the extraneous material is deleted?

questions.e: A "Pyrrhic victory" is won at such great cost that it is hardly worth winning, i.e. a costly victory.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
His success may be described as a Pyrrhic victory?

questions.e: To "misconstrue" is to understand wrongly, i.e. to misinterpret. "Misquoted" refers to wrongly repeating words.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The teacher's apparent nonchalant attitude was misconstrued by his students?

questions.e: "Luminaries" are people who are eminent and inspiring in their field, so legal luminaries are respected legal experts.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
They are considered to be legal luminaries

questions.e: To "assume office" is to formally take up a position, usually after being sworn in.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The Executive Secretary has just assumed office.

questions.e: To "parley" is to hold talks or discussions, especially between opponents.
questions.s:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s).
The warring tribes have been told to parley with each other.

questions.e: "Recrimination" means answering an accusation with a counter-accusation.
questions.s:

questions.e: To bequeath is to leave property to someone, usually in a will, so "left" is nearest in meaning.
