questions.e: To "accumulate" wealth is to build it up; to "squander" it is to waste it. Gather, amass and pile up are synonyms.
questions.s:
**Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.** 
Where is the wealth the rich man accumulated in his lifetime?

questions.e: To "admire" is to regard with approval; to "scorn" is to regard with contempt, the opposite.
questions.s:
**Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.**
The cleaner admires the girls for their neatness.

questions.e: A plan that "falls through" fails to happen; the opposite is to "succeed".
questions.s:
**Choose the option that is opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.**
The commissioner thought that the proposal would fall through.

questions.e: "Vehemently" means with strong feeling and passion; doing something "coldly" means without feeling, the opposite. Emphatically and strongly are synonyms.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
Musa vehemently opposed his son's political ambition.

questions.e: "Natives" are people born in a place; "foreigners" come from another country. "Indigenes" is a synonym of natives.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
The natives were allowed to stay.

questions.e: "Meticulous" means very careful and attentive to detail; its opposite is "careless".
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
The scientist conducted a meticulous experiment.

questions.e: To anger the gods is to provoke their wrath; to "appease" them is to calm and satisfy them, the opposite in this religious context.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
In the past, anyone who angered the gods would be killed.

questions.e: To be "chastised" is to be severely scolded or punished; to be "honoured" is to be praised and rewarded. "Rebuked" is a synonym.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
Despite their efforts at the last Nations Cup fiesta, the team was chastised by their
employers.

questions.e: A "facile" generalisation is too simple and shallow; its opposite is "complex", taking full account of an issue's difficulty.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
He made a facile generalisation.

questions.e: "Flexible" means willing to change or adapt; "rigid" means unwilling to bend or change.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
The manager became flexible on critical matters.

questions.e: "Immanent" means existing within something; "transcendent" means existing beyond or above it.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
The gear is immanent in a car.

questions.e: The "protagonist" is the main character; the "antagonist" is the character who opposes the protagonist.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
Andrew is the protagonist in the play.

questions.e: "Porous" security has holes that let things through; "impermeable" means letting nothing through. "Pervious" is a synonym.
questions.s:
For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in italics. 
The robbers gained access to the bank because of their porous security network.

questions.e: A "leisurely" pace is slow and unhurried; its opposite is "rushed". Relaxed, slow and calm are synonyms.
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase**
**underlined.**
The old man walked at a leisurely pace.

questions.e: "Ecstatic" means overwhelmingly happy; its opposite is "sad". "Elated" is a synonym.
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase**
**underlined/in italics.**
She remained ecstatic despite the chaos around her.

questions.e: "Concise" means short and to the point; its opposite is "lengthy". Brief and succinct are synonyms.
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase**
**underlined.**
The manager gave a concise summary of the report.

questions.e: "Capricious" means unpredictable and given to sudden changes of mood; "methodical" means orderly and systematic, the opposite.
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase in**
**italics.**
Known for his capricious behaviour, no one was surprised when Obinna was arrested by the
police.

questions.e: 'Lay' is the past tense of the intransitive verb 'lie' (to recline); 'laid' is from 'lay' (to put something down), and 'lied' means told lies.
Before a gerund ('leaving'), a possessive form is used: 'He did not like our leaving the class early.'
The past perfect 'had long decayed' fits a past reporting verb ('found'), showing the decay happened before the discovery.
The subject is 'The employer'; the phrase 'not the salesman and his representative' is parenthetical, so the singular verb 'is' is needed.
A child born to unmarried parents is legally 'illegitimate'; 'illegal' and 'illicit' describe acts that break the law.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
The boy was born before his parents actually got married and so the court has declared him
....

questions.e: To 'lend' is to give money temporarily; 'borrow' is to receive it, and 'loan' is mainly used as a noun in standard usage.
questions.s: As he was still owing me two naira, i was careful not to .... him any more money

questions.e: People gathered to watch a performance at a theatre are an 'audience'; a 'congregation' gathers for worship.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space:
Last week, the .... at the theatre was the largest I had ever seen.

questions.e: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so it takes no article and no plural 's'.
'Contemporary' describes people who lived at the same period; 'contemporaneous' usually describes events, and 'contemptible' means despicable.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space.
Tennyson and Browning lived about the same time and are therefore .... poets

questions.e: 'Camouflage' is natural colouring that helps an animal blend into its surroundings, as a green snake does in green grass.
To 'exhume' is to dig a buried body out of the grave, usually for examination.
'Between' is used for two people, and a preposition takes the object pronoun 'me', not 'I' or 'myself'.
The fixed expression is 'with a view to' + gerund, so 'with a view to finding'.
'Had just ... when' is the standard pattern for one action happening immediately after another in the past.
'Used to' + base verb expresses a past habit: 'They used to receive visitors.' 'Are used to' would need a gerund.
'Beside the point' is an idiom meaning irrelevant, which explains why the suggestions cannot be accepted.
'For as long as' introduces a condition lasting over time: while he remains secretary, the minutes will be wrong.
'Fast' is both adjective and adverb; 'fastly' is not standard English, so 'as fast' is correct.
Letters are commonly closed with 'Yours ...'; the possessive pronoun 'yours' never takes an apostrophe.
A second conditional pairs the past simple ('If I went') with 'would' + base verb ('would return').
An 'appendix' is extra material added at the end of a book, which suits folktales attached to it.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space
The traditional folktales form an .... to the book.

questions.e: To 'wipe out' means to destroy completely, which suits an explosion destroying a whole wing.
For an aircraft, the correct phrasal verb for leaving the ground is 'take off'.
An aircraft 'touches down' when it lands on the runway.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
As luck would have it, the weather brightened almost immediately and after six hours flight
we .... at Heathrow Airport

questions.e: One 'fills in' a form by writing the required details in the spaces provided.
'Smell' is the neutral or unpleasant word; 'aroma' and 'scent' suggest a pleasant odour, which does not fit 'cannot bear'.
questions.s:
**Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that most suitably**
**fills the space;**
My father cannot bear the .... of the concoction that emanates from my mothers soup pot

questions.e: The perfect infinitive 'to have broken' shows the offence happened before the appeasing, explaining why he had to appease the policeman.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
I would not have condescended to appeasing the traffic policeman, but I happened .... traffic
regulation.

questions.e: A negative statement takes a positive question tag; 'did not pay' is past simple, so the tag is 'did he?'.
'Mastery of' means thorough knowledge or command of a subject, which fits 'improve his mastery of French'.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space:
Although he is in all respects a poor student, he has managed to buy a tape recorder to
improve his .... of French.

questions.e: To 'order someone around' is an idiom meaning to keep giving them commands in a bossy way.
The invention of the locomotive engine was a key milestone of the Industrial Revolution; locomotion itself and the engine were not single 'discoveries'.
o: The invention of the locomotive engine

questions.e: 'Than' requires a comparative, and 'many more' (with countable 'cheers') shows the loser was strongly favoured by the crowd.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
Because the referee was partial and his opponent rough, the loser of the wrestling match
received .... cheers than the winner

questions.e: One is rated or praised 'for' a quality, so 'rated for his doggedness'.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;The boxer was highly rated .... his doggedness and ability to absorb heavy
punches

questions.e: 'Owing to' means 'because of', giving the cause of the deaths; 'resulting in' would wrongly reverse cause and effect.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
Many lives are lost on Nigerian roads .... lack of consideration for other road users by many
crazy drivers

questions.e: The idiom is 'well disposed towards' someone, meaning friendly or favourable to them.
questions.s:
Complete each of the following sentences by choosing the option that **most suitably** fills
the space;
The man no longer feared his opponent after their spokesman had assured him that they
were well disposed .... him

questions.e: 'Prone' takes the preposition 'to': prone to accidents means likely to have them.
Something irritating 'jars on' one's nerves; this is the fixed expression.
Speed is expressed with 'at': 'at full speed'.
A third conditional pairs 'had happened' with 'would have' + past participle: 'what would you have done?'.
The past simple 'ended' describes a completed action at a definite past time ('when it did').
'In case' introduces a possible future event we prepare for: take care in case the robbers come back.
'By the time' + past event takes the past perfect for the earlier completed action: 'had doubled'.
'So many ... that' introduces a result clause, and 'feed' needs an object: 'that she couldn't feed them all'.
o: that she couldn't feed them all
that she could feed them all
more than she could feed them all

questions.e: After 'it is high time', the past tense is used to show something should already be happening: 'you left'.
'Incidence' means the rate or frequency of occurrence of a disease; an 'incident' is a single event.
The past perfect 'had started' shows the play began before the arrival at the hall.
The perfect participle 'Having played' shows an action completed before the main one (deciding to join another team).
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
....for the team for six years, he decided to join another

questions.e: To 'blow up' a bridge is to destroy it with explosives.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
The bridge connecting the two cities was .... by the enemy

questions.e: In English one 'suffers from' an illness.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
My little boy is suffering .... jaundice

questions.e: Adjective order is size, then colour, then material: 'a big brown leather bag'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
They went to the market and bought a suitcase and .... bag

questions.e: 'By the end of this year' points to a completed span up to a future time, requiring the future perfect 'I'll have lived'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
By the end of this year, .... in this town for eleven years

questions.e: A third conditional: 'If he had left ... he would not have been late'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
If he had left home earlier, he .... late

questions.e: In reported (indirect) questions, normal statement order is used and the tense follows the past: 'where you were going'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
I saw you walking in that direction but i did not know exactly ....

questions.e: 'So steep that ...' introduces a result clause, and 'on' needs its object 'it': 'that no man could find a foot-hold on it'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
The hill behind the town was so steep ....
o: that no man could find a foot-hold on
that any man could find a foot-hold on it
for no man to find a foot-hold on
that no man could find a foot-hold on it
for any man to find a foot-hold on

questions.e: The participle 'Walking down the street' must refer to the subject that follows; only 'the boy' could be walking, avoiding a dangling modifier.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
Walking down the street ....
o: the boy was knocked down by a car
a car knocked the boy down
the boy was knocked down by car
a car collided with the boy

questions.e: A plan that 'falls through' fails to be completed.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
The project which seemed very near realization .... because of lack of funds

questions.e: The adjective 'sympathetic' takes the preposition 'to' (or 'towards').
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentence:
The chairman of the company was very sympathetic .... his staff

questions.e: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' with statement word order: 'if she could meet him later'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
Jane asked James ....
o: whether could she meet him later
if she could meet him later
that she could meet him later

questions.e: 'Hypocritical' means pretending to have feelings one does not have, which fits pretending to still regard him.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
After our series of quarrels, it would be ....to pretend that i have any more regard for him

questions.e: The idiom is 'of one's own making', meaning caused by oneself.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
If the company had any delay at the customs office, it was .... their own making

questions.e: To 'ward off' means to prevent or fend off an attack or danger.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
There is an obvious need to ward .... enemy attacks

questions.e: 'Exposure to' something means experience of it, which helps a person mature.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
David can only become more mature through .... to life outside his home

questions.e: Policies are 'formulated', i.e. carefully drawn up; 'fabricate' means invent falsely, and 'develope' is misspelt.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
Many of those who .... the country's educational policy have taught for many years

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'at great length', meaning for a long time and in detail, with no article.
questions.s:
From the options lettered A-E, choose the option that best fills the gap in the following
sentence. 
Mr. Thomas talked .... about the successes of his institute in the past year.

questions.e: 'Humanitarian' services are those that promote human welfare and relieve suffering.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
The governor commended the society's .... services to the nation

questions.e: 'Discuss' is transitive and takes a direct object, so no preposition is needed: 'discussing it'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
The member of the panel were ....

questions.e: 'Masterly' is an adjective, not an adverb, so it is used in the phrase 'in a masterly way'.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
This writer analyses the evil society ....

questions.e: A 'task force' is a group set up to deal with a particular problem; a 'tribunal' judges disputes and an 'inquest' investigates a death.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
The Nigerian society of Engineers has set up .... to study the nation's problems

questions.e: To learn something 'by heart' means to memorise it.
questions.s:
Choose the expression or word which **best complete** each sentences:
It was a long poem but he learnt it ....

questions.e: The teacher's surprise suggests the inspector is usually strict, i.e. hard to please; the other options would make approval expected.
questions.s:
Choose the correct option that completes the following sentence:
The young teacher was surprised that his promotion was approved by the old inspector who
is generally known to ....

questions.e: 'Would you mind ...?' asks if there is an objection, so a willing reply is 'No, I don't (mind)'.
questions.s:
Complete the following with the **appropriate answer** to the question:
John would you mind lifting this box?

questions.e: 'Legacies' are things handed down from an earlier period or system, here the lasting results of colonial rule.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The giant hydro-electric project is among the .... of colonial rule in Southern Africa.

questions.e: To 'review' activities is to look back over and assess them, which suits looking at four years of government.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
During the inaugural address, the president .... the activities of his government for the past
four years

questions.e: To 'forecast' is to predict a future condition, especially in economics; 'prophesied' suggests religious prediction.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The world bank team which visited the land-lock country .... a bleak economic future for it.

questions.e: 'Arrive at' is used for a specific point or building such as a motor park; 'arrive in' is for towns and countries.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
We travelled all night and arrived .... the oyo motor park at six o'clock in the morning

questions.e: 'In case' introduces a possible event we take precautions against: stay away in case the robbers return.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
We ought to stay away .... the robbers come back

questions.e: 'In case' introduces a possible event we take precautions against: stay away in case the robbers return.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
We ought to stay away .... the robbers come back

questions.e: To 'take over' is to assume control or responsibility from someone else, as the vice principal does in the principal's absence.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The principal will be going away on leave. In his absence, the vice president will .... the
school.

questions.e: To 'carry out' intentions or plans means to put them into action.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The new leader has a good intentions, but he is unable to ....

questions.e: Time distance is expressed with a possessive: 'an hour's drive'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
Ikorodu is not far from here, it is only an ....

questions.e: The present perfect with 'yet' asks whether something has happened up to now: 'has arrived yet?'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
Do you know if the new teacher .... yet?

questions.e: 'Had he known' is an inverted third conditional, so the main clause takes 'would have' + past participle: 'would have gone'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
Had he known he .... away

questions.e: After 'it is time', the past tense is used to mean the action is due now: 'It is time we went'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
It is time we ....

questions.e: 'So that' introduces purpose: he sent them out in order to be alone.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
He sent the children out to play .... he might be alone.

questions.e: 'For' is used with a length of time: 'for an hour or two'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
He played the piano .... an hour or two

questions.e: If a solution 'eludes' someone, they have failed to find it; 'avoided' suggests deliberate action.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The solution to the problem has so far .... the scientist

questions.e: Reported speech after past 'asked' shifts the tense back to the past perfect: 'if she had seen'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The teacher asked if she .... seen her boyfriend recently

questions.e: 'Be supposed to' means be expected to; the passive needs the past participle 'supposed' after 'are'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
You .... to know better than an illiterate farmer

questions.e: To 'influence' is to affect someone or their situation, which fits how a decision might affect you.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
How will the committee's decision .... you?

questions.e: The subject is the singular 'The benefit', and general truths take the present tense, so 'is'.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The benefit one gets from watching plays .... comparable to that found in taking a university
course in drama.

questions.e: 'Look' here is a linking verb describing a state, so it takes an adjective ('unhappy'), not an adverb.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :The candidate looked
.... after finishing the examination

questions.e: 'Result in' introduces the effect of an action: the boycott resulted in closure.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The boycott of classes last year by under-graduates resulted .... the temporary closure of
Nigerian Universities

questions.e: 'One another' is traditionally used for more than two people, here all Nigerians.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The head of state in his new year broadcast to the nation emphasised the need for
Nigerians to regard .... as member of the same family

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'in recognition of', meaning as an acknowledgment of.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The executive President honoured the messenger with the Grand Commander of the Niger
award .... his industries and meritorious services to the nation

questions.e: 'Noise' here is uncountable, and 'make a lot of noise' is the standard, idiomatic expression.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The neighbour's children always make ... when she is not at home

questions.e: A group 'comes to power' when it takes control of government; the other phrases are not idiomatic.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
In 1966, the Military .... because of the tragic failure of the civilian politicians

questions.e: 'Consists of' is correct; 'comprises' takes no 'of', and 'is constituted of' is non-standard.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
A society .... individuals each of whom has his attributes and distinct characteristics

questions.e: 'The Miss Sanda of the Central Bank' identifies a different, particular person of the same name, so the definite article is used.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
Biliaminu sent the expensive present to one Miss Sanda of the United African Organization
and not to .... of the Central Bank of Nigeria

questions.e: Since large estates are kept, the decree does not aim at equal ownership, so 'equality' fits the contrast.
questions.s:
Choose the word/expression which **best completes each** sentence :
The Land Decree does not concern itself with achieving .... in landed property ownership,
since those who already own large estates can keep them for good

questions.e: A completed action at a definite past time ('in the nineteenth century') takes the simple past passive 'was invented'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five option:
The telephone .... in the nineteenth century and is now used in most countries in the world

questions.e: A deadline in the future ('By the end of the next semester') calls for a perfect form showing completion; the key accepts 'would have completed', though 'will have completed' is the stricter standard form.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five option:
By the end of the next semester he .... his University education

questions.e: The present simple 'goes' expresses a present habit, contrasting with the past habit 'used to walk'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five option:
In the past his father used to walk but nowadays he .... to work by bicycles

questions.e: The past continuous 'were making' shows an action in progress over a period in the past, during which the lecturer walked out.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options
The students .... so much noise while the lecturer had to walk out of the class

questions.e: 'Used to' + base verb describes a past habit or state that no longer exists, contrasting with 'now he is a driver'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options
Olukayode .... as a mechanic when he was young, but now he is a driver

questions.e: 'From his point of view' means 'as he sees it', which fits the idea of how the proposition might look to him.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options
...., it might not look such a rosy proposition.

questions.e: 'Like' introduces an example, meaning 'such as': any European country like Britain.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options

money to pay our way

questions.e: 'You can take my word for it' is the idiom meaning 'you can believe me', used to assure someone.

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options

o: you can take that from me
you can say i say so
you can take my word for it
it is my word against theirs
you may or may not believe it

questions.e: A third conditional: 'If he had entered ... I would have seen him'.

questions.e: 'Consideration for' others' feelings is the correct collocation, meaning thoughtfulness towards them.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options

questions.e: 'This year' is a time period still continuing, so the present perfect passive 'has been repaired' is used.

questions.e: One 'quotes' a price when stating how much something will cost.

Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:

questions.e: A method is something one 'recommends' (suggests as good); the other verbs do not fit 'method'.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:

questions.e: Things already existing in nature, like oxygen, are 'discovered'; things newly created are 'invented'.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:

questions.e: Without any support, the bird would 'fall down', i.e. drop to the ground.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:
Why does a flamingo stand on one leg? Because if it lifted the other one, it would ....

questions.e: To 'see someone off' is to accompany them to their point of departure and say goodbye.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:
I am travelling by the 6:30 train tomorrow morning. Will you .... me ....?

questions.e: 'So' + auxiliary + subject agrees in a short addition: 'I am ... so is Musa; I left ... so did Musa'.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:

questions.e: To 'make up for' something is to compensate for it, such as lost time.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:
You have been absent from classes for four months. How can you .... for the lost time

questions.e: 'Out of order' means not working, which is why the telephone cannot be used.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:
I am afraid you cannot use this telephone; it is ....

questions.e: One 'makes an effort' to do something, meaning one tries; 'effect' means a result.
questions.s:
Choose the **best option** to fill the gaps in the following sentences:

questions.e: The fixed collocation is 'tell lies' and 'tell the truth'; we do not 'say' or 'speak' lies in standard usage.
questions.s:
From the options lettered A-D, select the option that best fills the gap(s) in the sentence
below:

questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
.... listening to the news when i came in

questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
They said that ....about 20 candidates for the job of a shorthand typist

questions.e: 'Go on' + gerund means continue doing something: 'go on working'.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
He told me to go on .... till seven

questions.e: 'Such as' introduces examples: goods such as tape recorders and cameras.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
Many goods .... tape recorders and cameras find a ready market in every country

questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
He acts .... he were a general manager

questions.e: 'I'd rather you' + past tense expresses a preference about another person's action: 'I'd rather you visited him'.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
Could i ring him up? I'd rather you ....

questions.e: A negative command in reported speech becomes 'told me not to' + base verb.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
Don't study on the examination day? What did he tell you? He told me .... on the
examination day

questions.e: An action continuing from the past up to now ('for the past three years') uses the present perfect continuous 'have been trying'.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
I .... to gain admission to the college for the past three years

questions.e: 'Recently' with a period up to now requires the present perfect, and plural 'arguments' needs 'There have been'.
questions.s:
complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
.... a lot of arguments for and against car loans in the press recently

questions.e: Reported speech after past 'reported' shifts the present perfect to the past perfect: 'he had never been overseas'.
questions.s:
Complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
He reported to his manager that he .... overseas

questions.e: 'Feel like' is followed by a gerund: 'I do not feel like going'.
questions.s:
Complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
Shall we go to the union meeting? No thank you, i do not feel like .... anywhere

questions.e: Goods cannot buy, so the passive 'will be bought' is needed, matching the future tense of 'will sign'.
questions.s:
Complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
Will they sign any contracts at the Fair?
They will not only sign the contracts but a lot of goods .... as well

questions.e: An action continuing up to a future point ('By 11:00 a.m. ... for three hours') takes the future perfect continuous 'shall have been writing'.
questions.s:
Complete the sentences with the **correct options** from the list below:
I started writing this test at 8 : 00 a.m It is 10 : 00 a.m now. By 11 : 00 a.m. I .... it for three
hours.

questions.e: To be 'laid up' is to be confined to bed or inactive because of illness or injury.
questions.s:
Choosing the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
As a result of the injury sustained on the football field, Segun was .... with a broken leg for
months

questions.e: One 'acts on' advice, meaning one follows it.
questions.s:
Choosing the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
the principal was able to establish a functional language laboratory for school because he
acted .... the advice of experts on the subject

questions.e: The past perfect 'had lived' shows a period of time leading up to a past moment ('when I met her').
questions.s:
Choosing the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Dume .... in Abraka for three years when i met her

questions.e: A second conditional ('If I were') takes 'would' + base verb in the main clause to express what the speaker would choose to do.
questions.s:
Choosing the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
If i were the Head of the English Department in my school, i .... make oral English a
compulsory subject

questions.e: 'Will be' completes the future condition and avoids the agreement problem with 'either ... or', where the verb would otherwise agree with the nearer subject 'I'.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
If Remi perform poorly in her forthcoming examination, then either her mother or I.... to
blame

questions.e: To 'lend' is to give something temporarily; 'borrow' would mean taking the book from Olu.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
I was able to .... Olu my book because he promised to return it the following day

questions.e: The past perfect 'had started' shows the lesson began before the prefect came.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
The prefect came to the class five minutes after the lesson ....

questions.e: A positive statement takes a negative tag, and 'sings' (present simple) uses 'does': 'doesn't she?'.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Bimbo sings beautifully .... ?

questions.e: 'Actually' introduces the real fact explaining the situation: the guide had left.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
We couldn't find the official who was to act as our guide ...., he has left before we arrived

questions.e: 'No sooner' is always paired with 'than': 'No sooner had ... than ...'.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
No sooner had the examination ended .... the students started vacating the halls of
residence

questions.e: 'Wasn't' is already negative, so 'anybody else' is needed to avoid a double negative.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Ogedengbe kept goal for his club team because there wasn't .... to do it

questions.e: 'Allergic' takes the preposition 'to'.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Grace must be allergic .... smoke because any time she sits by someone who is smoking, she
sneezes

questions.e: 'Duplicity' means deceitfulness or double-dealing, which explains why trust cannot be restored.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Now that i realize the full extent of your ... i am afraid it will be impossible for me to ever
trust you again

questions.e: To 'discern' the truth is to perceive or recognise it clearly, a skill legislators need.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
Legislators must be trained to .... the truth

questions.e: A 'voracious' reader reads eagerly and a great deal; 'veracious' means truthful and 'mendacious' means lying.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
He must be a good student because he is a .... reader

questions.e: 'Connotations' are the extra shades of meaning a word carries beyond its literal sense, which are hard to translate.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
It is very difficult to capture the subtle ..... of words when translated from one language to
another

questions.e: The analogy pairs training of a faculty with the person it produces: training the body makes an athlete, training the mind makes a scholar.
questions.s:
Choose the **appropriate option** to fill the gap in the following sentences:
As it holds true that, unless you train your body you cannot be an athlete, so also unless you
train your .... you cannot be a ....

questions.e: 'At' is used with exact clock times: 'at two o'clock'.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
The meeting starts .... two o'clock. Please be punctual

questions.e: The verb 'insist' takes 'on': insist on being given a receipt.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
Every time you pay a bill you must insist .... being given a receipt

questions.e: Elections 'into' a body refer to being elected to membership of it, e.g. elections into the Senate.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
The elections .... the Senate were held in July

questions.e: 'Around the corner' means just past or near the corner.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
There is a filling station .... the corner, to your right.

questions.e: For public transport such as planes, trains and buses, English uses 'on': a seat on the plane.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
It is difficult these days to get a seat .... the plane in spite of a confirmed booking

questions.e: Means of transport without an article use 'by': 'by train'.
questions.s:
Choose the **correct word** to fill the space in the following sentences:
He travelled to Jos .... train when he came last

questions.e: 'Coup' (coup d'état) is the correctly spelt word for a sudden seizure of power; the other forms are misspellings.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
For their part in the unsuccessful .... the mutineers were court - martialled

questions.e: To rule a speaker 'out of order' is to declare that he has broken the rules of the meeting.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
The Chairman ruled the impertinent speaker .....

questions.e: 'Different from' is the standard, preferred construction.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Your approach to the problem is different .... ours

questions.e: To 'gag' the press is to stop it from publishing freely; the other words refer to physical restraint.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
The way to stop some frivolous publications is to .... the press

questions.e: 'Received' follows the spelling rule 'i before e except after c'; 'receipt' is a noun.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
They .... our donation with thanks

questions.e: 'Some' is used in offers and questions expecting 'yes', and 'milk' is uncountable, so 'a milk' is wrong.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
You surely want .... in your tea don't you?

questions.e: An adverb is needed to modify 'done', and the comparison pattern is 'as quickly as'.
questions.s: The exercise must be done .... possible

questions.e: The idiom 'with a view to' is followed by a gerund: 'with a view to learning'.
questions.s: He bought a typewriter with a view .... to type

questions.e: After 'It is time we', the past tense shows the action is overdue: 'expelled'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
It is time we .... this irresponsible member

questions.e: 'Had he known' is an inverted third conditional, so the main clause takes 'would have prepared'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Had he known in advanced, he ....
o: was going to prepare for the interview
would have prepared for the interview
will have been preparing for the interview
may be preparing for the interview

questions.e: The perfect infinitive 'to have assaulted' shows the reported act happened before the report and that he did the assaulting.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
He was reported .... the policeman

questions.e: A possessive ('Peter's') is followed by a gerund acting as a noun: 'Peter's catching a cold'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Peter's .... a cold upsets our plans

questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Although he was invited .... he was not welcome.

questions.e: After a past reporting verb ('remarked'), the tense shifts back: 'he was a responsible boy'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
When John reported the incident, the teacher remarked that he .... a responsible boy.

questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
They tried to cash in .... the people's ignorance

questions.e: 'Founded' is the past tense of 'found' (establish); 'found' as past of 'find' would mean discovered.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
A pioneer, he .... the institution from his own resources

questions.e: 'So well ... that' introduces the result clause.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
He passed so well .... he was awarded a scholarship

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
I told him .... he had no chance

questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
He looked .... everyone in authority as an enemy

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
As .... of you that can come are welcome

questions.e: 'Bid' takes an object and a bare infinitive or complement: 'bade them welcome'.

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
He bade them .... to his house

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
If .... one day, we would talk about it for weeks.
o: a lion would be coming into this room
a lion was coming into this room
a lion came into this room
a lion is coming into this room
a lion is going to come into this room

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:

questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
The house will look all the better .... this new coat of paint

questions.e: 'Without mincing words' means speaking frankly and directly, without softening what one says.

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:

Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Asmau, did you see the snapshop of ....

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five option

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:

questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
.... Several bad air-crashes recently.

questions.e: Country names with 'States' (the U.S.A.) and names of oceans take 'the', while continents such as Europe take no article.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
Visitors…. Pass beyond this point. It is forbidden

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

questions.e: 'Devote oneself to' takes a gerund, since 'to' is a preposition here: 'devoted himself to helping'.

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
We talked quietly _________ wake the baby.

questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
These six employees ........ absent from work since new year’s day.

questions.e: 'I wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish I had learnt to swim'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
I wish I …. to swim when I was younger.

questions.e: 'By the end of June' marks completion before a future time, so the future perfect 'shall have taken' is used.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
By the end of June, i …. six examinations this year.

questions.e: 'Used to' is past, so the tag uses 'did': a positive statement takes 'didn't we?'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
We used to go to that club on Saturday night ….?

questions.e: 'Farther' refers to physical distance, which suits walking; 'further' is preferred for abstract extent.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
It was a blind alley. I could not walk any ....

questions.e: To 'put someone up' is to give them a place to stay for the night.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
Maimuna wrote to ask if I could put her …. for the night

questions.e: To 'bring off' a deal is to succeed in achieving it; 'fell through' would mean it failed.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
After weeks of bargaining they …. a deal worth millions.

questions.e: To 'watch' is to observe someone attentively over a period, which suits policemen keeping an eye on a man.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
The policemen stood …. the man at the corner.

questions.e: A percentage of the population fits an abstract noun, 'unemployment', not a word for people such as 'employees'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
.... reached 18.7% of the U.S population.

questions.e: 'At least' introduces a minimum fact that is still reassuring: he won't sleep here, even if he eats here.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

questions.e: The fixed collocation is 'say hello'; we 'say' words or greetings.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
I was in such a hurry, I didn’t have time to …. Hello.

questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
My younger brother looked ill last night, and was evidently …. this morning

questions.e: 'Which' is the relative pronoun for animals and things, introducing a clause about the snake.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
The schoolboy screamed loudly when he saw a snake …. looked terrifying.

questions.e: 'By the time the bus arrives' refers to a future point, so the future perfect 'will have finished' is used.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences, making use of the best of the five options
:
The guests ...... breakfast by the time the bus arrives.

questions.e: A comparison needs 'more ... than': more lawyers enrolled last year than in the year before.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
…. Lawyers enrolled at the Nigerian bar last year …. the year.

questions.e: 'As little ... as possible' with the uncountable 'fuss' means the smallest possible amount.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
They promised to cause …. fuss …. possible.

questions.e: A comparative needs 'more ... than': many people have more money than they need.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
From one’s daily experience,one can see that many people have ..... money ..... they really
need.

questions.e: 'Traffic' is uncountable, so 'a lot of traffic' is correct; 'many traffic' and 'plenty traffic' are wrong.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :
Eko bridge, linking Lagos Island to Surulere, has ….

questions.e: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun and never takes a plural 's'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options :

questions.e: 'Point-blank' means flatly and bluntly, without explanation or politeness.
questions.s:
Choose the word or phrase from A to E which has the **nearest meaning** to the underlined
word or words in each sentence :

questions.e: 'Easily the ... of the lot' compares one with a group, so the superlative is needed. 'Brightest' is correct, and 'most brightest' is a double superlative.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
He is easily the ...... of the lot

questions.e: After a negative statement, 'neither' with inversion adds another person: 'I am not attending, neither is my wife.'
questions.s:
fill in the blank space in the following sentence making use of the best of the five options: I
am not attending ...... is my wife.

questions.e: In compound nouns like 'parent-in-law', the plural goes on the main noun: 'parents-in-law'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Some people think that ...... are potentially a nuisance

questions.e: Nouns ending in consonant + 'o' like 'hero' form the plural with '-es': 'heroes'.
questions.s:
fill in the blank spaces in the following sentences making use of the best of the five options:
Shakespearian ...... are generally the victims of circumstances.

questions.e: 'Since the beginning of this term' marks an action continuing to now, requiring the present perfect continuous 'has been working'.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
Monisola is sure to pass in September. She .... hard since the beginning of this term.

questions.e: 'A close friend' is the correct collocation; 'tight friend' is non-standard and the shoemaker is not a customer.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
The old shoemaker at the corner of our street is .... so i hope you will patronize him

questions.e: A comparison with 'than' requires the comparative form, and the keyed 'more brilliant than' expresses better performance than last year.
questions.s:
Fill in the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
The students in my junior class seem to have performed .... they did last year

questions.e: 'Assist them' fits helping flood victims; 'respond' would need 'to', and the other verbs do not suit the context.
questions.s:
Fill the blank spaces with the most appropriate of option A - E:
After the 1980 Ogunpa floods, our association received many letters from those adversely
affected and we resolved to ....

questions.e: 'Each other' is used for two people, Jane and Jarawa, showing a mutual action.
questions.s:
Fill the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
Jane and Jarawa love …. Very much.

questions.e: The correct phrases are 'by air' and 'by road', with no article.
questions.s:
Fill the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
I shall travel to Lagos by …. Next week.

questions.e: To 'get away with' something is to escape punishment for it.
questions.s:
Fill the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
You can never get …. With stealing the presidential jet. You will be caught.

questions.e: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it has no plural 's'; 'the advice given by her friends' is correct.
questions.s:
Fill the blank spaces with the most appropriate of options A-E:
She got into trouble because she refused to listen to the …. given by her friends and
relatives.

questions.e: One is stabbed 'in' a part of the body: 'in the back'.

From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
