I am sure that my mother will not find out. She is so .... that she will accept anything i tell
her

questions.e: The statement uses 'have started' (positive), so the tag is negative with 'have': 'haven't they?'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The boys are very naughty. They have started fighting again ....

questions.e: 'If only' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'If only I had been insured'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
If only i ..... insured! But i wasn't. Now i have to pay a lot of money

questions.e: 'I'd rather you' + past tense expresses preference about another person's action: 'I'd rather you called'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Do you mind if i wait for the reply? I'd rather you ..... again tomorrow

questions.e: Reported questions use statement order, and after 'I was asking' the tense shifts back: 'how you wanted the money'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
appropriately completes the sentence:
Olu: How do you want the money in cash or in traveller's cheques? Ali: Beg your pardon?
Olu: I was asking you how .... the money?

questions.e: To 'make out' something is to understand or decipher it.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The young man looked carefully at the long document, but he couldn't make .... what it
meant.

questions.e: 'Offhand' means without time to think or check, which fits being unable to remember immediately.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Give me a minute to think i can't remember the answer ....

questions.e: A 'setback' is a reversal or check in progress, such as losing by-elections.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The government suffered a .... when they lost two by-elections.

questions.e: 'Be worth' is followed by a gerund without an object pronoun: 'will be worth seeing'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Our Literature Master said that he would show us a film on Macbeth. The film will ....

questions.e: 'Nearly lost his life' means he almost died but survived.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The driver of that lorry .... lost his life during the collision

questions.e: To 'catch a glimpse' of someone is to see them briefly; this is the fixed collocation.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Wherever the leader went people struggled to catch a .... of him

questions.e: 'Mean' (intend) takes a to-infinitive, and 'no one to sell' means no one available to sell: 'to buy / to sell'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
I meant ... a pencil but there was no one .... there.

questions.e: 'Since 1975' marks a period up to now, so the present perfect continuous 'has been teaching' is used.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Mrs. Okoro .... in this school since 1975.

questions.e: 'Broadcast' has the same form in the past participle; 'broadcasted' is non-standard.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The Governor has .... to the people on many occasions

questions.e: 'Could not have taken' expresses a deduction about the past: she obviously did not take the right route. 'Cannot have taken' is also possible, but the past form matches the narrative.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Paulina arrived late, she ..... the right route

questions.e: The perfect participle 'Having bought' shows that buying was completed before he asked his daughter.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
.... the medicine, he asked his daughter to take it according to the doctor's prescription.

questions.e: A perfect form shows completion by a future deadline ('By the end of this year'); the key accepts 'would have read', though 'will have read' is the stricter standard.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
By the end of this year i ..... twenty books

questions.e: 'Couldn't have had' expresses disbelief that something was possible in the past, given the low price.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Leonard: We went to a hotel and had a very good dinner for N1.00.
Geoffrey: You .... a very good dinner if you paid N1.00

questions.e: 'Needn't have submitted' means the action was done but was unnecessary, since three copies were enough.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Evelyn: I've submitted eight copies. Joseph: You .... eight. Three would have been enough

questions.e: The subject 'display' is singular, and the present continuous fits an ongoing situation ('present'): 'is affecting'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the question below select the one which most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The present wanton display of riches .... morality of our society

questions.e: 'Whose' shows possession (the women's profit), and 'make life difficult' is the correct idiom.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The market women ... profit ranges from thirty fifty percent are making .... difficult for the
ordinary people

questions.e: 'To prevent' expresses purpose; 'prevent people rushing ... and dashing' uses parallel gerunds.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Town authorities have put up a railing in front of the exits .... people .... out of the stadium
and ... straight across the road

questions.e: 'Since 6 p.m.' requires the present perfect continuous 'has been playing', and 'I wish he would' expresses annoyance at a continuing action.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Someone .... the radio cassette since 6 p.m. I wish he .... turn it off

questions.e: A third conditional ('would have been lynched') needs the past perfect in the if-clause: 'had been caught'.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
If the armed robbers ... caught, they would have been lynched.

questions.e: 'Had he known' is an inverted third conditional, so the main clause takes 'would have taken'.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Had he known that it would rain, he .... his umbrella with him.

questions.e: To 'break loose' is to escape from restraint; 'lose' is a misspelling here, and 'break even' means no profit or loss.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Omeime was taking his dog for a walk when the dog suddenly .... from its chain and escaped

questions.e: 'News' is uncountable and singular, and the past participle of 'broadcast' is 'broadcast', so 'was broadcast'.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
I was still sleeping when the national news ... this morning

questions.e: 'Each of' takes a singular verb, and 'has a chance' is the natural collocation.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
Each of the contestants .... a chance to win

questions.e: 'I think' is a parenthetical insertion, and the pronoun is the subject of 'works', so the subject form is needed: 'the library attendant who I think works in the evenings'. 'Whom' is an object form. The correct option is D.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
I gave the book to the library attendant ... I think works in the evenings

questions.e: 'The course events have taken' means the direction in which events have developed; 'coarse' means rough.
questions.s:
From the alternative provided in the question below select the one which is most
**appropriately** completes the sentence:
The politicians are responsible for the .... events have taken in this country

questions.e: 'Equipment' is an uncountable noun, so it has no plural form: 'some equipment'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the questions given, select the one which **most**
**appropriately** completes the sentence. The principal went to buy some ..... for the physics
laboratory.

questions.e: Both words have double letters: 'committee' (mm, tt, ee) and 'accommodation' (cc, mm).
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the questions given, select the one which **most**
**appropriately** completes the sentence. The ..... should make .... for them as soon as
possible.

questions.e: 'Can't help' or 'couldn't help' is followed by a gerund. The past narrative needs 'couldn't help laughing'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the questions given, select the one which **most**
**appropriately** completes the sentence. It was a funny episode, so I ......

questions.e: The standalone possessive pronoun is 'theirs', with no apostrophe, meaning 'their share'.
questions.s:
From the alternatives provided in the questions given, select the one which **most**
**appropriately** completes the sentence. After we have taken our share we shall give ....... to
them

questions.e: A means of transport without an article takes 'by': 'by bus'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Mary goes to school ..... bus

questions.e: The verb 'stare' takes the preposition 'at'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The loud noise in the neighbourhood attracted people who stared .... the thief

questions.e: 'Result in' introduces the consequence: the unrest resulted in the expulsion.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The students unrest resulted .... the expulsion of the ringleaders

questions.e: 'Insist' takes the preposition 'on'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The lawyer insisted .... the full payment of his charge

questions.e: The adjective 'afraid' takes 'of'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Little children are usually afraid .... thunder,

questions.e: 'To' shows movement towards a destination: rushed to the market.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
On the orders of the steward, the cook rushed .... the market

questions.e: To be 'taken in' is to be deceived, which fits being fooled by Ada's lies.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The principal advised that we pursue this case cautiously, otherwise we are bound to be
taken .... by Ada's lies

questions.e: 'Sorry for' + gerund apologises for something one did or failed to do: 'sorry for failing to attend'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
I am very sorry .... to attend the meeting yesterday

questions.e: To 'keep one's mind on' something is to concentrate on it.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
When you are faced with an examination of this nature, endeavour to keep your mind .... the
job and not be distracted for one moment

questions.e: Embedded questions use statement order, and the tense follows the past 'depended': 'what he wanted'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
It all depended on what ....

questions.e: The present continuous 'I'm working' describes an action in progress now, explaining why John is busy.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Samuel: would you please come here. John? John: No I'm busy .... in my farm

questions.e: The past perfect 'had started writing' shows the action began before the speaker arrived.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
My colleagues .... before i arrived

questions.e: The simple past 'began to wane' describes what happened next, after the earlier past perfect event ('had conceded').
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
After the team had conceded two goals, their enthusiasm ....

questions.e: 'Cost' meaning 'estimate the cost of' is regular, so its past form is 'costed'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The Government .... the initial value of the hotel complex at ten million naira

questions.e: The singular subject 'James' takes 'needs', and 'needs reminding' has a passive meaning (needs to be reminded).
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
James .... reminding that not all that glitters is gold.

questions.e: 'Any more ... than' is used in a negative comparison: not any more dangerous than riding a bicycle.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The boy thought that driving a car was not .... dangerous than riding a bicycle

questions.e: After the negative 'don't want', 'any' is used, and uncountable 'advice' takes no plural: 'any more advice'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
I don't want .... from such a friend as Jimoh

questions.e: 'Accommodation' is spelt with double c and double m.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Very few students have satisfactory .... these days because the student population has
increased tremedously

questions.e: To 'cash in on' something is to exploit it for one's own advantage.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The old politicians were discredited because they tried to .... the people's ignorance

questions.e: A plane overshoots the 'runway' when it fails to stop before its end.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The plane overshot the .... in a minor accident.

questions.e: 'Occurrence' is spelt with double c and double r, ending in -ence.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The single .... was enough to spoil a whole lifetime of good living

questions.e: To 'run out of luck' is to have one's good fortune end.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The thief ran .. luck when the policeman running after him caught up with him and knocked
him down

questions.e: To 'rob' people is to steal from them; 'rubbing' means applying friction and 'robing' means dressing in robes.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Whilst the thief was .... the passengers, he kept apologizing for the inconvenience he was
causing them

questions.e: 'Desist' takes 'from': desisted from rumour-mongering.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Your brigade would be better for it, if you desisted .... rumour - mongering, observed the
Chief of Staff

questions.e: 'Damage' meaning harm to the car is uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded by a court.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The court ordered the lorry driver to pay for the .... to my car

questions.e: 'Information' is uncountable and takes no article or plural form.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
Journalists always collect and publish ....

questions.e: The idiom is 'a pat on the back', meaning praise for an achievement.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
He received a pat .... the back for his brilliant success in the examination

questions.e: A 'break-in' is a noun for illegal entry into a building to steal. 'Break into' is a verb phrase and cannot follow 'the'; 'break out' refers to escape or sudden starts.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Jibril found that thieves had entered his house in his absence. He went to the police to
report the ....

questions.e: A 'plea for mitigation' asks the court to reduce a sentence after a guilty verdict. 'Litigation' means taking legal action, which does not fit this stage.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
After the accused was found guilty by the court, his counsel .... before sentence was passed.

questions.e: The correct spelling is 'trafficking', with a 'k' added before -ing to keep the hard 'c' sound, as in panicking.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Four persons accused of currency ..... are being held by the security agents

questions.e: The main clause 'I don't suppose you enjoyed the journey' is negative and in the past, so the tag is the positive past form 'did you?'. The tag follows 'you enjoyed', not 'I suppose'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
You had to stand in the corridor all the way? Poor you! I don't suppose you enjoyed the
journey .... ?

questions.e: 'Few' with a countable noun like oranges means hardly any, which explains why the speaker cannot give any. 'A few' would mean some are available; 'little' is for uncountable nouns.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Í'm sorry I can't give you any of the oranges; I have .... left'.

questions.e: The present perfect 'haven't had' links a past period ('for ages') to the present result (the plants are dying now). 'Hadn't' alone lacks the main verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
No wonder those plants are dying. They .... any water for ages!

questions.e: To 'put up with' means to tolerate or endure something unpleasant, like the children's noise. 'Make do with' means to manage with something inadequate.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
'Darling, do send the children to bed. I can't .... their noise any longer' he said to is wife

questions.e: 'Each other' is used for a mutual action between two people, here husband and wife. 'One another' is traditionally used for more than two, and 'met ourselves' is wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
My wife and i met .... on a ship going to Liberia.

questions.e: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb, so 'Is there any news'. 'Their' is a possessive, not the adverb 'there'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
..... yet about the principal?

questions.e: To be 'entitled to' something means to have a right to it, here an extra week of holiday earned by hard work. 'Due' would need 'for', and 'qualified' takes 'for'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
I am .... to another week's holiday this year after such a tedious job.

questions.e: To know or recite something 'off by heart' (or 'by heart') means from memory. 'Off hand' means without preparation or casually, which is different.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
I can quickly recite the National Anthem .... now.

questions.e: 'Assent' means official approval or agreement, which the Chief withheld. 'Accent' is a way of speaking, 'access' is entry, and 'ascent' is a climb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
The committee was frustrated because the Chief withheld his ....

questions.e: 'Used to' expresses a past habit or state that no longer exists, matching 'gone are the days'. 'Would' needs 'when he would enjoy' and suits repeated actions less well with a state.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Gone are the days when he ... enjoy patronage.

questions.e: 'Rites' are ceremonial acts, as in burial rites. 'Rights' are legal or moral entitlements, a different word that sounds the same.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
He did not attend the final burial ....

questions.e: 'Seize', meaning to take by force or authority, is the correct spelling and an exception to the 'i before e' rule. 'Cease' means to stop.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
The officer was compelled to .... the suspects's car.

questions.e: To take a statement 'literally' means to understand the words in their exact, basic sense, missing the intended point. 'Literary' relates to literature.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
He missed the point because he took the statement ....

questions.e: 'Morale' means the confidence and spirit of a group, which can be high and give an advantage. 'Moral' and 'morality' relate to right and wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Their high .... was an advantage

questions.e: To 'defuse' a bomb means to remove its fuse to prevent an explosion. 'Diffuse' means to spread out, which is wrong here.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
The brave officer .... the time bomb.

questions.e: Suspects are paraded 'before' (in front of) someone for identification. 'In front' would need 'of' to be complete.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
A number of suspects were paraded .... the victim of the robbery

questions.e: 'Had better' is followed by the bare infinitive, so 'had better get prepared'. 'Have better' is not standard and 'had better got' uses the wrong verb form.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
If you want peace, you .... prepared for war

questions.e: 'If only' expressing regret about the past takes the past perfect: 'If only we had persevered'. This matches the past result 'we could have overcome'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
If only we .... we could have overcome the difficulty

questions.e: 'Getting to the end' is the natural idiom for gradually nearing the end. 'Approaching' would not take 'to', and 'arriving' takes 'at'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
'We are gradually .... to the end of the programme this afternoon', remarked the chairman
of the wedding reception

questions.e: After 'saw him', the -ing form 'leaping' shows the action in progress as it was observed. The bare form 'leap' would show the completed action; the past forms are wrong after an object of 'see'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
We saw him ... over a wall as the police approached

questions.e: The gerund 'working' follows the preposition 'to' in 'disposed to'. Since the statement is negative ('not so well disposed'), the tag must be positive: 'are they?'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
A number of doctors are not so all well disposed to .... in government hospitals these days
.... they?

questions.e: The subject is 'set', which is singular, so it takes 'is'. 'Of loud speakers' only describes the set and does not change the verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
The only set of loud speakers available .... to be connected according to the instruction

questions.e: The past perfect 'had held' shows the earlier meeting was held before the time of 'discovered'. Present perfect forms do not fit a past narrative.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
We later on discovered that some members .... another meeting before the one advertised.

questions.e: 'Luggage' is uncountable, so it has no plural and goes with 'a lot of', not 'many' or 'too many'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
He decided to wait for the bus because he had  ______________

questions.e: 'Enjoy' is transitive and needs an object; with no other object, the reflexive 'ourselves' completes it: 'we really enjoyed ourselves'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Thank you for the party, we really ....

questions.e: Lights 'go off' when power fails. 'Came off' means became detached, and 'quenched' is used for fire or thirst, not electric light.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
We are trying to study for the examinations last night when the light .....

questions.e: 'Hang' meaning to suspend an object has the past tense 'hung'. 'Hanged' is used only for executing a person by hanging.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
When he had arranged the furniture, he .... the picture on the wall

questions.e: You 'lend' something to someone, and you 'borrow' from someone. The speaker wants the listener to give a pen temporarily, so 'lend me yours' is correct.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
I forgot to bring a pen with me. Would you, please ... me yours

questions.e: 'Come with you' is the natural way to ask to accompany someone. 'For follow you' is non- standard and 'come by you' means to pass near you.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
If you are going to the market, may I .... please?

questions.e: 'Lay' (to produce eggs) has the past tense 'laid'. 'Lied' is the past of 'lie' (tell a falsehood), 'lain' is the past participle of 'lie' (recline), and 'layed' is a misspelling.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which **best fills** the gap:
Wada said that two of his chickens .... eggs yesterday morning

questions.e: 'Within hearing distance' means close enough to hear, inside the range. 'Within' is the preposition used with ranges and limits.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
I was .... hearing distance of the speaker.

questions.e: To 'take on' someone means to accept a challenge from them or fight them, which fits a confident boxer.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
Peter was such a skillful boxer that he was not afraid to take ...... anybody.

questions.e: To 'shoot at sight' (or on sight) means to shoot as soon as one is seen. 'In sight' means visible, and the other forms are not idioms.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
Owing to the constant harassment of the populace by armed robbers, all night guards have
been instructed to shoot .... every moving things

questions.e: A 'fateful' day is one with important, often disastrous, consequences, like a death on an anniversary. 'Futile' and 'fruitless' mean useless.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
My wife and i were to celebrate our silver wedding anniversary last Sunday. Unfortunately
on that ....day, my father-in-law died mysteriously

questions.e: The idiom 'all walks of life' means all occupations and social classes.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
The first graduation ceremony of the university was attended by men from all ..... of life

questions.e: 'All the guests' fits the plural noun and verb. 'Every' needs a singular noun ('every guest'), and 'the whole' is used with singular nouns.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
..... guests enjoyed joy's birthday party

questions.e: The negative perfect infinitive is formed as 'not to have' + past participle: 'wish not to have missed'. 'To have not' is less standard.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
One would wish .... missed that opportunity to be present at the graduation ball

questions.e: To 'round off' an event means to bring it to a close or finish it. 'Round up' means to gather together.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
The ceremony was rounded .... very late.

questions.e: 'Elder' is used for the older of siblings in the same family, especially before a noun ('my elder brother'). 'Older' is used for general comparison.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
My ..... brother intends to get married in December.

questions.e: In compound titles the first noun acts like an adjective and stays singular, as in 'Student Affairs Officer'. A possessive form is not used in this title.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
The ..... Affairs Officers is expecting all of us in the dining room

questions.e: The plural subject 'many candidates' takes the plural verb 'fail'. 'Fails' and 'is failing' are singular, and the general truth calls for the simple present.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase which best fills the gap(s):
Many candidates ..... to realise the difference between written and spoken English

questions.e: To 'allude to' something is to refer to it indirectly without stating it openly. Chinyere only hinted at it rather than calling the Cabinet irresponsible directly.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Chinyere has not really described the Cabinet as irresponsible; she only ..... it in her speech.

questions.e: To 'tune in' means to set a radio or TV to a station to listen or watch, the phrase broadcasters use. 'Switch on' does not take 'at 9:30 for more news' as naturally.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
'.... at 9:30 for more news',said the announcer.

questions.e: A 'sadist' takes pleasure in causing others pain, matching bullying 'with relish'. 'Bully' merely repeats the action, and a 'pugilist' is a boxer.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The way that big boy bullied his sister with relish make me think he could be a ....

questions.e: In the idiom 'all is well', 'all' means everything and takes the singular verb, so 'All is not well with Peter'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
All .... well with Peter

questions.e: The third conditional pairs 'if + had + past participle' with 'would have + past participle': 'Ore would have said so if she had thought it necessary'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Ore .... so if she had thought it necessary

questions.e: The idiom 'might as well' means there is no good reason not to do something, so having done three quarters, we might as well finish.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
We have done three quarters of the journey already; we .... as well see the end of it

questions.e: 'Defective' sight is faulty or imperfect sight, the kind corrected with glasses. 'Blurred' describes a temporary effect, and 'diminutive' means very small.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
My little daughter has .... sights; hence she now wears glasses

questions.e: The phrasal verb 'lead to' means to cause or result in. Bassey's evidence resulted in Okon's life imprisonment.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Bassey's evidence led .... Okon being imprisoned for life

questions.e: 'At times' is the correct two-word phrase meaning sometimes or occasionally. 'Atimes' is a common misspelling.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
My boss is usually a charming man but ... he can be very irritable.

questions.e: 'Alternative' means another possible option or backup plan. 'Alternate' means occurring by turns, and 'alternating' means switching back and forth.
questions.s:
In the question below, choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
We surely ought to have an .... arrangement in case somebody discovers the present
strategy.

questions.e: 'Into' shows movement penetrating the inside of something, as a needle entering a baby's body. 'In' shows position rather than movement.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The nurse kept apologizing to mothers as she stuck her needle .... every baby at the clinic

questions.e: 'Who' refers to 'ladies' (plural), so 'who sell'. The main subject is 'One', which is singular, so 'has been asked'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
One of the ladies who .... in the premises .... been asked to withdraw.

questions.e: A title, though it contains a plural word ('cities'), names one book and takes a singular verb and noun: 'is the novel'. The present tense fits 'we are studying'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
A tale of two cities .... the .... we are studying for examination

questions.e: 'That' refers back to 'feelings', which is plural, so the verb must be 'were'. 'Those were' would make a separate clause and is ungrammatical here.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
We must not take with us the feelings of inadequacy .... experienced during preparations for
the debate

questions.e: The past perfect 'had started' shows the exams began before another past action, his arrival. Reported speech also shifts the tense back.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Omogbai reported that the examinations .... before he arrived in the hall

questions.e: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the coach', which is singular, so 'deserves'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
In my opinion, neither the player nor the coach .... praise for the result of the match.

questions.e: 'May' expresses possibility when the speaker is unsure, which fits 'no one has said anything yet'. 'Must' would show certainty.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
no one has said anything yet, but i think i .... be getting a salary increase next month

questions.e: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary, the correct negative answer to 'must we...?'. 'Mustn't' would mean it is forbidden.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Student: Excuse me sir, must we complete the assignment before lunch? Teacher: No you
....

questions.e: To 'break through' a line means to force a way past a barrier or defence. 'Break down' means to collapse or fail.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
During demonstration, the mobile police were instructed to break .... the students defence
line

questions.e: 'Too' means more than is acceptable, leading to a negative result, which explains why Roli failed. 'So' would need a 'that' clause.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Roli failed because the examination was .... difficult for her

questions.e: The noun 'flair' (natural talent) takes the preposition 'for': a flair for mathematics.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
My brother does not have a flair .... mathematics.

questions.e: The idiom is 'down with' an illness, meaning ill with it: 'down with fever'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The poor little kid has been down .... fever these few days

questions.e: In an indirect (embedded) question, the normal statement order is used, subject before verb: 'why he should do such a thing'. Inversion belongs to direct questions.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
He did not stop to ask himself why .... such thing.

questions.e: To 'intervene' means to come between quarrelling parties to settle a dispute. 'Interfere' and 'intrude' suggest unwanted involvement.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The quarrel has got to a stage where someone has to ....

questions.e: To 'look up to' someone means to respect them and see them as a model, matching 'for good examples'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The villages looked ..... their leader for good examples.

questions.e: 'Live' (pronounced to rhyme with 'five') is the adjective used before a noun for a living animal: 'a live antelope'. 'Alive' is not used before a noun.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The hunter brought home ..... antelope.

questions.e: In a conditional with 'unless', the present tense 'have' states the condition. 'Had got' is the wrong tense, and 'have' is not used in the continuous here.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Do not take my books out of this office unless you .... my permission to do so

questions.e: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun, so it has no plural. 'Advise' is the verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The man insisted on giving unsolicited ....

questions.e: Culture is 'transmitted', meaning passed on, from one generation to the next. 'Transposed' means changed in order, and 'translated' means put into another language.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Culture patterns are modified as they are .... from one generation to the next

questions.e: 'Very many more' is the correct intensified form for a countable plural noun like 'books'. 'Much more' is used with uncountable nouns.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
We discovered at the end of last term that we had to read .... books before we could
confidently go for our final examination

questions.e: 'In case' referring to a past situation takes the simple past: 'in case it rained'. 'Would rain' is not normally used after 'in case'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Chinedu took his umbrella with him in case it ....

questions.e: To 'get off' means to leave a bus or train. 'Get by' means to manage, and 'get of' is not a phrasal verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The train was to slow so i decided to .... at the next stop

questions.e: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural. 'Some useful information' is correct; 'piece of' would need 'a' or 'pieces'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Dapo has made good use of some useful .... on the chemical composition of chalk

questions.e: 'Too tired to do' expresses that he was so tired he could not do more. Only 'too' combines with an infinitive this way to show an impossible result.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Tonye said that he was going to bed because he was .... to do any more work.

questions.e: To 'revert to' means to go back to a former state or habit. 'Reverse' means to turn backwards and does not take 'to his old habits'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The child's recent training has not been very effective, he is likely to .... to his old habits

questions.e: 'In defiance of' means openly resisting or ignoring authority, which fits whispering despite the teacher. 'Disobedience' does not combine with 'in ... of'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The students went on whispering in .... of the teacher

questions.e: 'Elusive' means difficult to find or catch, like Okwu. 'Illusive' and 'delusive' relate to illusions and false impressions.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
You can never find Okwu; he is a very .... person.

questions.e: The adverb 'honestly' modifies 'give', and the adverb 'completely' modifies 'honestly', so 'completely honestly'. Adjectives like 'honest' cannot modify a verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
You could see that Akpan did not give his evidence ....

questions.e: 'Unsuspecting' victims are those who do not suspect any trickery. 'Unsuspected' means not suspected by others, which describes the fraudster, not the victims.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The suspect defrauded his ..... victims of large sums of money

questions.e: In compound nouns where the adjective follows the noun, the main noun takes the plural: 'Auditors General', like 'Attorneys General'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The ... of the participating countries will hold a preconference on the eve of the conference.

questions.e: Excited dancers 'kicked' and 'stamped' the ground, both natural actions of feet in dancing. 'Licked' and 'stroked' do not fit the energetic scene.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The drummers struck their drums with great efforts and the surging crowds of dancers ....
and .... the grounds around the palace.

questions.e: 'With no intention to' means without the purpose of doing something. 'Intent' usually follows 'with intent to', and 'intend' is a verb.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The chairman's daughter's laughter was with no .... to ridicule the applicant

questions.e: 'Contaminated' means made impure or unsafe by contact with something harmful, like a rotting carcass. 'Infested' refers to pests swarming in a place.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The water is not good for drinking; it's been .... by the dead rabbit

questions.e: 'Circumspect' means cautious and careful in considering consequences, fitting careful spending in hard times. 'Misely' is not a word.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The austerity of the times has made people to be more .... in their spending

questions.e: 'Prefer' takes 'to' for comparison: 'prefer a horse ride to taking a walk'. 'Prefer ... than' is incorrect.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
Are you sure he prefers a horse ride .... a walk?

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'with regard to', meaning concerning. 'With regards' (plural) is used for greetings, not this phrase.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
.... to your request, we have decided to provide the necessary information

questions.e: With 'up' already after the gap, the idiom is 'shot up', meaning rose suddenly and sharply. 'Risen up' is redundant here because 'rise' already means go up. The correct option is B.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The price of everything seems to have ... up in the last few months.

questions.e: To 'put in an appearance' means to attend briefly, mainly to be seen there. The other forms are not standard idioms.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
Just to convince you about my commitment to the project, i shall .... at the office before i
leave for Kano tomorrow.

questions.e: A 'flight of steps' (or stairs) is a series of steps between floors, the standard collective expression.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
There was a .... of steps.

questions.e: To 'iron' clothes means to remove creases with a heated iron. 'Press' can mean this too, but 'iron' is the common everyday term.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
Many young men of nowadays do not know how to properly .... their cloths.

questions.e: The idiom is 'in high spirits' (always plural), meaning cheerful and lively.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The dancers were all in .... before their departure

questions.e: To 'fall off' means to drop from the edge or surface of something, like a cliff. 'Fall down' means to drop to the ground from standing.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
Ebun .... the edge of the cliff after his shoes had failed to grip.

questions.e: 'Prefer' with gerunds follows the pattern 'prefer doing X to doing Y', so 'prefers baking bread to making clothes'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
That old lady prefers .... bread .... clothes.

questions.e: After 'I wonder', the question is indirect and keeps statement order: 'how much these earrings cost'. Inverted order like 'do these earrings cost' is for direct questions.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
I wonder how much .....

questions.e: In an indirect question after 'I wonder', normal statement order is used, so 'how much these earrings cost'. The 'do' auxiliary is dropped.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
I wonder how much .....

questions.e: To 'call on' someone to do something means to formally ask or urge them, here to end the strike. 'Call for' takes a thing, not a person plus infinitive.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The college authorities have .... the students to end the strike.

questions.e: 'For' is used with a length of time (five days), while 'since' is used with a starting point (since Monday).
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
I have been trying to locate you .....

questions.e: In formal English, a possessive is used before a gerund: 'insisted on my accepting'. 'Me to accept' is wrong after 'insisted on'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The host insisted on ... what he called 'a little gift'

questions.e: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: 'looked forward to visiting'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The whole class looked forward to .... Kainji Dam at christmas.

questions.e: The noun 'efforts' is followed by an infinitive of purpose: 'efforts to obtain the release'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
A government spokesman announced that efforts .... the release of hostages are continuing

questions.e: 'In time' means eventually or after a while. 'On time' means punctually, which is not the sense here.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
I know you will think I am talking nonsense, Shehu, but .... you'll realize that i was right.

questions.e: 'Worn down' means exhausted and weakened over time by difficulty, like the bad road trips and fever. 'Worn off' means faded away.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The Inspector of Education who made several trips on bad road returned yesterday
completely .... by fever

questions.e: To 'look up' information means to search for it in a book or reference source, such as recommended textbooks.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s).:
The vice principal asked the students to always .... their answer only from the textbooks
recommended for the course

questions.e: After a negative statement in the future ('will not accept'), agreement is shown with 'neither' + auxiliary + subject: 'neither will you'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
I know that your friend will not accept the proposal ....

questions.e: To have 'an eye for' something means to be good at noticing or attracted to it; in this sense, he was always noticing pretty girls.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Mark is a very handsome fellow who informs me that he was .... for pretty girls

questions.e: To 'draw on' something means to use it as a source, as a writer uses life experience to create characters.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
Wale Agun, in creating his characters, draws freely .... his experience in life

questions.e: 'Hate' can be followed by a gerund, and the passive gerund 'being kept waiting' shows that someone else makes the speaker wait.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
When i have an appointment with someone, i hate .... waiting

questions.e: 'It's no good' is followed by a gerund: 'it's no good worrying'. 'For worring' is misspelt and ungrammatical.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
It's no good .... about the result until you have sat for examination

questions.e: 'Lose' is the verb meaning to have something taken or to fail to keep it. 'Loose' means not tight, and 'loss' is a noun.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
If you don't want to .... your car to robbers, then don't travel in the night

questions.e: Plans that 'fall through' fail to happen or are abandoned. 'Fall out' means to quarrel.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The beautiful plan made for the expansion of the business fell .... as soon as the manager
died.

questions.e: 'Recent' is an adjective and follows 'are' directly: 'they are recent'. 'Are of recent' is a non- standard expression.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The event reported in the newspaper did not happen years ago; they ....

questions.e: To 'take something in one's stride' means to deal with problems calmly without being upset.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
There is no point getting upset by problems; I take them ....
o: on the spur of the moment

questions.e: To 'stand on ceremony' means to behave very formally; 'no need to stand on ceremony' means formality is unnecessary.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
There is no need to stand .... ceremony in matters of this nature

questions.e: To 'pick up' passengers means to collect them in a vehicle. 'Pick' alone means to choose or pluck.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The driver will .... all the students interested in going to Lagos tomorrow at 7 a:m outside
the Main Building

questions.e: To 'cite' means to quote or refer to works as evidence. 'Sighted' means saw, and 'sited' means located.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
What bothered me about the lecture was that the speaker ... too many irrelevant works

questions.e: 'Undisciplined' is the standard English adjective for people lacking discipline. 'Indisciplined' is a common Nigerian usage that standard dictionaries do not accept, and 'disciplinary' means relating to punishment. The correct option is B.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The students were suspended because they were ....

questions.e: 'Screeching' is the harsh, high-pitched sound made by brakes when a vehicle stops suddenly, matching the crash that followed. ('Breaks' in the sentence should be 'brakes'.)
questions.s: We heard the .... of breaks which was followed by a crashing noise

questions.e: 'On the spur of the moment' means suddenly, without planning or thinking beforehand, which fits 'had not given the question a thought'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
I had not given the question a thought before my answer came ....
o: on the spur of the moment

questions.e: 'Cleverer' is already comparative, so it cannot take 'more'. 'Much' is used to intensify a comparative: 'much cleverer'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
The small girl is.... than her elder sister

questions.e: The subject of the verb 'are' needs subject pronouns, 'he' and 'I'. Courtesy places 'I' last: 'He and I are good friends'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills** the gap(s):
.... are good friends

questions.e: The past perfect 'had seen' covers the period up to a point in the past (yesterday's meeting). Present perfect would link to now, which does not fit.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
When I met Amadi yesterday, it was the first time I .... him for six months.

questions.e: A 'determining' factor is one that decides or strongly influences the outcome. 'Determined' means resolute, and 'determinate' means fixed.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
A student's natural ability should be a .... factor in his choosing a course of study at the
university.

questions.e: 'In the course of' means during. 'Coarse' means rough, 'cause' means reason and 'curse' is a spell or swear word.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
Many unrelated issue were touched upon in the .... of the discussion.

questions.e: To run 'fast' means quickly, and to 'catch' a train means to get on it before it leaves. 'Cash' (money) and 'first' are sound-alike traps.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
The traveller had to run .... in order to .... the train.

questions.e: The idiom is 'run for dear life', meaning run as fast as possible to save oneself. It is a fixed phrase without a possessive.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
When the driver lost control of his vehicle, the pedestrian began to run for ....

questions.e: 'One of the' must be followed by a plural noun, so 'elites' fits. 'Elitist' describes a person who believes in rule by an elite, not a member of one.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
My uncle is one of the ..... of the society.

questions.e: The 'outskirts' of a town are its outer edges or suburbs. The word is always plural; 'outskirt' and 'outskates' are wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
The new singlet factory is built on the .... of Aba township

questions.e: The third conditional (if + had not + past participle) is completed by 'would not have' + past participle: 'wouldn't have fallen'. 'Fell' is the simple past, not the participle.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap(s):
If Kaka hadn't tried to stand up in the boat, he .... into the lake

questions.e: 'Arms' (weapons) is always plural in this sense, while 'ammunition' is uncountable and has no plural, so 'arms and ammunition'.
questions.s:

questions.e: With 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the leader of the farmers' (singular), so 'is'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Either the chief of the village or the leader of the farmers .... to be held responsible for the
revolt.

questions.e: The subject is 'most of the support', and 'support' is uncountable, so it takes the singular 'has yielded'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
We must observe that most of the support by other states .... only marginal returns

questions.e: 'Mind' is followed by a gerund, and reported speech after 'asked' takes the past: 'whether I minded posting'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
She asked me whether i .... the letter for her

questions.e: The subject is 'the effort' (singular), so 'is appreciated'. The phrase 'made by the principal...' does not change the subject.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The effort made by the principal to get the students to be serious in their studies .....

questions.e: 'Wish' about a past event takes the past perfect: 'I wish I had heeded'. It shows regret over something not done.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
How i wish i .... my mother's advice

questions.e: The subject 'observers' is plural, so 'are allowed'. 'From the Ministry of Works' only describes them.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Only observers from the Ministry of Works .... allowed into the conference room

questions.e: The subject is 'a panel' (singular), so 'is yet to sit'. 'Set up to probe...' only describes the panel.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
A panel set up to probe the organization's activities .... yet to sit

questions.e: Schools 'break up' when the term ends and holidays begin. 'Break out' means to start suddenly or escape.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The school will .... for Easter in another six weeks

questions.e: Power supply is 'cut off' when it is disconnected, often for non-payment.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
His power supply was .... from the mains because he did not pay his electricity bill

questions.e: To 'hang up' means to end a telephone call by putting down the receiver.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
When you've finished using the telephone, please hang ....

questions.e: To 'put in an appearance' means to attend an event briefly, just to be seen. The other forms are not standard idioms.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
I do not intend to stay long at the function. i only want to ....

questions.e: 'Sheer' means pure or nothing but, as in 'sheer hard work'. 'Shear' means to cut, and 'cheer' and 'share' are unrelated.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The man rose to an important position as a result of ________ hard work

questions.e: 'Acquired' is spelt with 'cq' followed by 'uired'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Ebun Ojo .... international fame as an actress

questions.e: 'Unbelievable' keeps 'ie' from 'believe' and drops the final 'e' before '-able'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The story on the lost jewel was quite .....

questions.e: 'Rheumatism' is spelt with 'rh' at the start, from Greek, followed by 'eumatism'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The patient is suffering from .....

questions.e: 'Pronunciation' drops the 'o' of 'pronounce': pro-NUN-ciation. 'Pronounciation' is a very common error.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The attitude of my students to .... baffles me

questions.e: The past perfect 'had left' shows he left before the past time when they arrived and were told.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
When we got to the president's house, we were told that he .... two days earlier

questions.e: 'Hanged' is the past tense used for killing a person, including oneself, by hanging. 'Hung' is used for objects.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Atuk, without giving any hint as to what he intended to do, went and ... himself

questions.e: 'Provided' introduces a condition and takes the simple present for a future meaning: 'provided you go'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Provided you .... to the market very soon, we shall be able to eat enough

questions.e: 'Must have arrived' expresses a confident deduction about the past based on evidence, the people shouting.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
He .... by now, i can hear all the people shouting

questions.e: This calls for a perfect form showing the duration completed by a future point. Of the options, 'would have been' supplies the perfect duration; standard English would use 'will have been'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
By the time the plane reaches Harare, it .... in the air for twelve hours.

questions.e: 'If only' expressing regret about the past takes the past perfect: 'If only Adoyi had known', matching 'could have avoided'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
If only Adoyi .... what was good for him he could easily have avoided the tragedy

questions.e: After verbs of perception like 'saw', the bare infinitive 'smash' describes a complete action that was witnessed.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
We saw Ifueko .... an egg on the wall

questions.e: The idiom 'stand in need of' means to need. The simple present 'stand' states a current general situation and agrees with plural 'streets'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Many streets in the town .... in need of lights at night

questions.e: This is a third conditional about a past party: 'if you had invited' pairs with 'would have been' + past participle.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
I did not enjoy the party. If you had invited Tariere, it ..... better organized

questions.e: The present perfect continuous 'has been reading' shows an activity that started in the past ('since she came home') and continues now.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
sibi .... novels since she came home

questions.e: 'Since 1954' marks a period from the past up to now, so the present perfect continuous 'has been teaching' is used.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Asabe is overdue for retirement as she .... in this college since 1954

questions.e: To 'give someone away' means to betray them or reveal their identity or secret to others.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The boy who stole the mango was given .... by an eye witness

questions.e: To 'touch off' means to cause something to start suddenly, like a trivial argument sparking a serious quarrel.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
After listening to the statement from two students, the headmaster realized that it was a
trivial argument that .... a serious quarrel between them

questions.e: 'Disappointed at' is used for one's reaction to an event or result, such as a son's performance.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Mr and Mrs Akoka were sad and disappointed .... the performance of their son

questions.e: To lie or throw oneself 'on one's stomach' is the idiom for lying face down.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
when the transformer blew up, Saka threw himself down .... his stomach

questions.e: To 'run into' someone means to meet them unexpectedly. 'Run across' is used more for things found by chance.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
I ran .... an old friend of mine on Broad Street and brought him home

questions.e: To 'give in to' demands means to yield or surrender to them. 'Give up' means to stop trying.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
The spokesman confirmed that government would not give .... to the demands of trade
union leaders

questions.e: A noun used as a modifier stays singular: 'the revival movement'. 'Revivalist' would also work as an adjective, but the plural and possessive forms are wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
Many students have joined the .... movement

questions.e: The third conditional (if + had not jumped) takes 'would have' + past participle: 'would have perished'. 'Perish' is intransitive, so it cannot be passive.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fills(s)** the gap(s):
If they had not all jumped out of the car just in time, they ....

questions.e: 'However' introduces a contrasting point, and it fits after a comma at the start of a new clause. 'But' would also contrast but is less formal in this position.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Many people believe that nuclear power will solve our energy problems, .... this has not
been proven to be true

questions.e: 'In conclusion' is the standard signpost phrase used to introduce a final summary. 'Conclusively' means decisively, which is a different meaning.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
...., sign post words are used to readers

questions.e: Two singular subjects joined by 'and' but preceded by 'every' take a singular verb and pronoun: 'has its limitations'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Every programming language and software package .... limitations

questions.e: To 'fight off' an illness means to resist it successfully.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
A programme of good exercise may help a person fight .... cold

questions.e: As part of the subject of 'participated', the subject pronoun 'he' is needed: 'Baba and he'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Baba and .... participated in the tournament

questions.e: After 'It was', formal English uses the subject pronoun: 'It was they who fought'. 'Them' is common in speech but not formally correct.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
It was .... who fought the civil war

questions.e: 'Their' is the possessive form for 'the physicians', and 'they' is the subject in the comparison 'than they (have)'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
The physicians have more people in ..... waiting rooms than ....

questions.e: 'Wring' (to twist and squeeze) has the past tense 'wrung'. 'Wringed' and 'wrang' are not standard.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Before mechanization, workers ... water out of fabric with their hands.

questions.e: 'Since March' indicates an action begun in the past and still continuing, so the present perfect continuous 'have been working'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Four engineers .... on this system since March

questions.e: The participle phrase 'Having worked all night' describes an earlier action, and the main verb in a past narrative is the simple past 'felt'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Having worked all night, the security man .... a sense of accomplishment

questions.e: With fractions, the verb agrees with the noun after 'of'. 'The Physics class' is treated as a single unit here, so 'is improving'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Three quarters of the Physics class .... dramatically.

questions.e: 'A number of' + plural noun means 'several' and takes a plural verb: 'have missed'. ('The number of' would take a singular verb.)
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
A number of students .... missed the opportunity to re-register

questions.e: 'Well thought-out' means carefully planned and considered in detail.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
It seems to be a well thought .... scheme.

questions.e: A 'showdown' is a final, decisive confrontation, fitting a rematch after last season's defeat. 'Show- off' is a boastful person.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Adekunle is prepared for a .... with his opponent following his defeat last season

questions.e: Being 'frustrated' means feeling discouraged after repeated failure; Tosin refused to give up despite three attempts.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Tosin refused to be .... though he has written the same examination three times

questions.e: The 'assumption of office' is the act of taking up an official position. 'Ascension' is used for rising to a throne or to heaven.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
On his ... of office, the new presidents announced some drastic measures

questions.e: A legal 'suit' (lawsuit) is filed 'at' a particular court, the place where it is lodged.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill in the gap with the appropriate option:
The .... was filed .... the Ilorin Magistrate Court.

questions.e: In legal language, a plaintiff 'prays' the court, i.e. formally requests it to grant an order.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
The plaintiff .... the court to restrain the defendants from further action

questions.e: The idiom 'nothing to write home about' means not impressive or not worth mentioning. The fixed phrase ends with 'about', which follows the gap.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
My experience in Lagos last week was .... about

questions.e: 'Had I seen him' is the inverted form of 'If I had seen him', a third conditional matching 'I would have informed you'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
.... him around, i would have informed you

questions.e: In 'one of the boys who...', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'boys', not to Ahmed, so the verb must be plural: 'one of the boys who always do good work'. The correct option is C.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
Ahmed is one of the boys who always .... good work

questions.e: 'News' is uncountable; to count it, we say 'an item of news' or 'a piece of news'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
I sent .... news to the press yesterday

questions.e: 'Equipment' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so 'sporting equipment'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
The university has a large collection of sporting ....

questions.e: 'Surroundings' (always plural in this sense) means the area around a person or place. 'Premise' means an assumption; 'premises' would be needed for a building.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
He keeps his .... clean always

questions.e: 'A set of' requires a plural noun, and the correct spelling is 'earrings'.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
She has a set of gold ....

questions.e: The simple past 'heard' refers to the specific past moment he learned the news, which caused him to stop writing.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
I have stopped writing letters application because i .... that all the vacancies are filled

questions.e: The subject is 'a survey' (singular), so 'has been carried out'. 'Of opinions on how pupils feel...' does not change the subject.
questions.s:
In question below fill the gap with the appropriate option:
A survey of opinions on how pupils feels about their teachers .... carried out

questions.e: Adjective order is number, then size, then colour: 'two big black cars'.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
The police are looking for ....

questions.e: 'Contemptuous' takes the preposition 'of': contemptuous of dishonest people.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
Adaobi is contemptuous .... dishonest people

questions.e: Animals graze 'in' a field, since a field is seen as an enclosed area.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
My goats are grazing ..... the field

questions.e: The second conditional pairs a past-tense if-clause ('if he told us') with 'would be' for a present or future hypothetical.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
It .... easier if he told us himself

questions.e: 'Our principal and chairman' refers to one person holding both roles (only one 'our'), so the singular 'has' is used.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
Our principal and chairman of the occasion ... just arrived

questions.e: 'Is kept busy serving' means he is occupied with serving; 'busy' is followed by an -ing form, not an infinitive. The present tense fits a daily routine.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
From 7 a.m to 9 a.m, he .... hot chocolate, often not having time for his own breakfast

questions.e: After 'one of the', the noun is plural ('schools of thought'), but the verb agrees with 'one', so 'suggests'.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
One of the ... selective marking of errors

questions.e: To 'face up to' something means to accept and deal with a difficult reality.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
You avoid facing .... the reality of life.

questions.e: 'Deeper' is already comparative, so it cannot take 'more' or 'most'. 'Much' intensifies a comparative: 'a much deeper sense'.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
In .... we, as politicians, are identified with the masses
