questions.e: 'So' introduces a result: because the comments are vague, students find them difficult. 'Them' refers to the plural 'comments'.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
In addition, their comments are vague and abstract, .... difficult to interpret

questions.e: 'Happy to receive' and 'in good health' form a standard letter-writing expression. 'Swimming in good health' is not idiomatic.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
we are .... to receive your letter and to know that you are ....

questions.e: 'Live by themselves' means live alone; 'themselves' is the reflexive for 'people', and the plural verb 'know' agrees with 'people'.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
People who live by .... what loneliness is like

questions.e: A confirmed future event is expressed with 'will be held'. The other options refer to the present or are ungrammatical.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
It has been confirmed that the election .... held in July

questions.e: 'Yours' is the possessive pronoun used alone and never takes an apostrophe.
questions.s:
In the question below fill the gap with the appropriate option :
The choice to go to the university or not is ....

questions.e: 'Too complicated' describes people who are difficult to understand or deal with, explaining the lack of respect. 'Compliance' is a noun and cannot follow 'too'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
I have no respect for individuals who are too ....

questions.e: To 'connive at' something means to secretly allow or ignore wrongdoing, like letting a robber escape.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
the policemen who were to keep watch connived .... the robber's escape

questions.e: 'Not only ... but also' must be balanced: 'not only anxious to acquire knowledge, but also eager to display it'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Kaka is .... to acquire knowledge, but also eager to display it
o: not only that she is anxious

questions.e: 'Unless' means 'if ... not': Wudu will come only if she is asked.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Wudu will not come .... she is asked

questions.e: A possessive is used before a gerund in formal English: 'forbid his coming'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
You must forbid .... coming

questions.e: The fixed phrase is '(all) other things being equal', meaning if nothing unexpected happens. 'Other things being equal' completes it correctly.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Oche should leave for New York on Friday .... being equal

questions.e: To 'keep company with' people means to associate with them. After 'not to', the bare infinitive 'keep' is used.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Th woman warned her daughter not to .... with bad boys

questions.e: A 'road accident' is the standard term for an accident involving vehicles on a road.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Ali is crying because his mother was killed in a .... accident

questions.e: To be 'cut out for' something means to be naturally suited to it. Otokpa is not bold enough for a rough life.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Otokpa is not very bold. He's not .... a rough life

questions.e: With 'some of', the verb agrees with the noun after 'of'. 'Food' here is uncountable, so the singular 'is' is used.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Some of the food .... spoilt

questions.e: In compound nouns like 'sister-in-law', the main noun takes the plural: 'sisters-in-law'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
They spent the last holiday with their ....

questions.e: 'Need' + -ing has a passive meaning, so 'need telling' means 'need to be told'. 'To tell' would wrongly make 'you' the teller.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
You should not need .... twice

questions.e: 'The length of the story' correctly expresses the story's length. 'Story's lengths' is wrongly plural, and 'stories length' lacks the apostrophe.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The .... discouraged me from reading it

questions.e: An 'affront to' one's dignity is an insult that hurts pride. 'Insolence' and 'disrespect' do not take 'an ... to his dignity' naturally.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
When the teacher asked him to join the queue outside, he considered it .... to his dignity

questions.e: Duties are 'assigned to' someone, meaning given as their responsibility. 'Detailed' is used for people sent on a task, not duties given to someone.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
When he joined the staff of the school, he had various duties .... to him

questions.e: One is 'blamed for' something: the secretary was held responsible for the untidy office.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The secretary was blamed .... the untidy state of the office

questions.e: To 'exonerate' is to clear someone officially of blame. 'Vindicated' means proved right, which suits a claim more than the accused boys.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
After a long talk with the police, Baba confessed his guilt and so the other boys with whom
he was accused were ....

questions.e: 'Quite a few' means a fairly large number, contradicting the idea that she has no friends. 'Few' would mean hardly any, and 'friends' is countable, so 'much' is wrong.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
You think she hasn't got any friends? Of course she's got ....

questions.e: 'Each other' expresses a mutual action between two people, the landlord and his wife. 'Theirselves' is not a word.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
He moved out of the house because the landlord and his wife were always fighting ....

questions.e: 'Vermin' is treated here as a collective singular, so 'makes'. 'Make' as a causative verb takes the bare infinitive 'look', not 'to look'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The vermin on his body .... hideous

questions.e: 'Information' is uncountable and singular, so it takes 'this' and 'is'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Do you think all .... not enough to help the investigator?

questions.e: 'Prefer' with gerunds follows the pattern 'prefer doing X to doing Y': 'prefer going on foot to taking my car'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Do you prefer ..... my rickety car?
o: to go on foot to taking
to go on foot than to take

questions.e: 'No sooner' is followed by inverted past perfect and completed with 'than': 'No sooner had we set out than the rain started'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
No sooner .... to fall
o: did we set out when the rain had started
had we set out than the rain started
were we setting out than the rain started
we had set out when the rain started

questions.e: A 'breach of contract' is the legal term for failing to honour the terms of a contract.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The company was charged with a .... of contract

questions.e: 'Arms' (weapons) is always plural, while 'ammunition' is uncountable with no plural: 'arms and ammunition'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The army ran short of ....

questions.e: 'The helpless' (the + adjective) refers to helpless people as a group and takes a plural verb: 'require'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The helpless .... our sympathy

questions.e: 'Decent' manners are polite and respectable. 'Gorgeous' and 'attractive' describe appearance, not manners.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
My brother got married to a woman with .... manners

questions.e: To be 'disguised as' someone means to dress or act so as to look like them. 'Concealed' and 'veiled' mean hidden, not impersonating.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The thief we caught yesterday was .... as an official of the company

questions.e: A compound adjective with a number before a noun is hyphenated and its noun stays singular: 'fifteen-centimetre nails'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The carpenter asked for ten packets of .... nails

questions.e: The fixed expression is 'shake hands with' someone, always with plural 'hands'.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The president refused to shake .... with the visiting Prime Minister

questions.e: In reported speech after the past 'complained', the robbery happened earlier, so the past perfect passive 'had been robbed' is used.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The trader complained that he .... robbed

questions.e: To 'corroborate' a story means to confirm it with further evidence. 'Collaborate' means to work together, a common confusion.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
How can we believe this witness when no one will .... his story?

questions.e: 'Derision' means mockery and scorn, the likely response to unpopular views. 'Admiration' is the opposite.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
The journalist's unpopular views made him the subject of much ....

questions.e: 'Turned' is almost certainly a misprint for 'tuned': an engine taken to a mechanic needs to be tuned up, that is, adjusted to run well. Turning an engine on needs no mechanic. The correct option is C.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Idubor has gone to see his mechanic because his car engine needs to be turned

questions.e: To 'leave' something somewhere means to forget to take it with you. 'Forgot' does not take a place phrase like 'in the car' in standard usage.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
I was anxious to arrive early for the lecture that i .... my note in the car

questions.e: To 'educate' means to develop the whole person, beyond merely teaching facts, which is the contrast the sentence draws.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Good schools don't just teach their students they ....

questions.e: 'Had he come' means he did not come, and 'would still not have been solved' means his presence would have made no difference.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
Had he come that day, the problem would still not have been solved
o: He came that day, but the problem was not solved
He did not come that day, but the problem was solved
He did not come that day, and the problem was not solved
He did not come that day, but his presence would not have solved the problem

questions.e: A 'megaphone' of a group is someone who speaks loudly on its behalf, so he is now the oppressors' spokesman.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
He is now the megaphone of the people's oppressors
o: He now speaks on behalf of the oppressors
He now carries the megaphone when the oppressors speaks
He is now the oppressor with loudest voice
He is the oppressor who no speaks with megaphone

questions.e: 'Shall' in formal documents and rules expresses obligation, so it is required that one of the guarantors signs here.
questions.s:
In the question below, fill the gap with the most appropriate option:
One of the guarantors shall sign here
o: It is desirable that on e of the guarantor signs here
It is reasonable that one of the guarantors signs here
It is obligatory that one of the guarantors signs here
It is advisable that one of the guarantors sign here

questions.e: The accepted name of the body is "Parent-Teacher Association", where the nouns act as modifiers and so stay singular without apostrophes.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
When I was in the secondary school, my parents were active members of the ..........

questions.e: For a name ending in -s, the possessive is commonly formed by adding only an apostrophe: Charles'. "Charle's" and "Charless'" are misspellings.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The pen which you have just picked up is.......?

questions.e: Agreeing with a negative statement needs a negative reply: "No, I won't" confirms that the speaker will not visit. "Yes" would contradict the negative.
questions.s: It is clear to me that you won't visit Okoro this holiday, will you?...

questions.e: "As well as the maids" is a parenthetical addition, so the verb agrees with the singular subject Sa'adatu: "likes". "Like" is a stative verb and is not used in the progressive.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Sa'adatu as well as the maids....?

questions.e: Names of diseases ending in -s, such as measles, take a singular verb, and the present tense suits "these days": "Measles is".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Measles....no longer impossible to manage these days

questions.e: "Tricky" is the standard adjective for a deceitful, crafty person. "Trickish", "tricking" and "trickful" are not acceptable forms here.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
People dislike Jobe because he is a......young man?

questions.e: 'If' with the simple past ('arrived') forms the second conditional, which takes 'would' plus the base verb: 'the match would be played'. 'Would have been played' needs 'had arrived'. The correct option is D.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
If the boys arrived early enough, the match ....?

questions.e: The correct expression is "at times", two words meaning occasionally. "Atimes" and "attimes" are not English words.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
She usually works hard, but....... she could be very lazy?

questions.e: "Police" is a plural noun, so it takes the plural verb "say" and the plural pronoun "they": "The police say they are happy".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The police ........... happy about the dwindling crime rate.

questions.e: The verb sting is irregular: sting, stung, stung. The passive needs the past participle, so "are stung"; "stinged" and "stang" do not exist.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The keepers themselves are sometimes........ by the bees?

questions.e: "Now realize" places the speaker in the present, and the present perfect "have met" links a past experience to that present moment.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I now realize I ........ you before?

questions.e: Surgery is described with the phrasal verb "operate on" (a patient), so the passive is "was operated on".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The patient was ....... by a group of surgeons last week?

questions.e: The expression "cannot help" is always followed by a gerund (-ing form): "couldn't help laughing".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The old man couldn't help ...... at his grandson's babbling?

questions.e: With "a range of + plural noun", the verb often agrees with the plural idea of the options (notional concord), and the past suits "recently concluded": "were made".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
A range of options ......available to the political parties during the recently concluded
elections

questions.e: Money claimed as legal compensation is "damages", always plural in this sense. "Damage" means physical harm.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
He claimed that Mr. okoli's utterance was tantamount to defamation of character, so he
sued for .......

questions.e: A question tag repeats the auxiliary of the main clause with reverse polarity. "I don't think he can" is negative in sense, so the tag is positive: "can he?"
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I don't think he can .......?

questions.e: To "get through to" someone means to succeed in reaching them by phone. "Get at", "get over" and "get on to" carry other meanings.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The handset was faulty and so it was impossible to ..... them on phone?

questions.e: The past progressive "was leaving" shows an action already in progress when another past event (the riot) started.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The president of the union ....... for the airport by the time the riot started?

questions.e: "Extravagant" describes spending or using things wastefully, beyond what is necessary or sensible. Being rich or luxurious is not the same as wasting.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
To be extravagant is to be ....... ?

questions.e: The idiom is "pride oneself on" something, meaning to be proud of it.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Until his recent experience, Onimisi used to pride himself....... his fearlessness?

questions.e: At a trade fair, goods are put on show for public viewing, which is to "exhibit" them; the word fits the formal setting of a fair.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The trader ...... his wares at the trade fair.

questions.e: The fixed expression is "have no alternative but to", meaning there is no other choice.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Based on the facts before me, i have no alternative ..... to terminate your appointment?

questions.e: The idiom "put in an appearance" means to attend briefly, often out of obligation.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Despite the pressure of work during the week i shall endeavor to ...... at your wedding?

questions.e: The keyed phrase expresses being together with someone. Note that "accompanied with" is wrong because a person is "accompanied by" another.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The expected guest eventually arrived ....... his wife?

questions.e: "Hard drinks" are strong alcoholic spirits such as whisky and brandy; "soft drinks" are non- alcoholic.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
When we visited him, he offered us a variety of ....... drinks such as whisky and brandy?

questions.e: To "pool resources" means to combine them for a shared purpose. Adding "together" is redundant, and "pull" is the wrong verb.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The exercise will be easily accomplished by the team if members ....... their .......?

questions.e: To "give up" a habit means to stop doing it. "Abandon", "discard" and "jettison" are not used idiomatically with a habit like drinking.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I have decided to ...... drinking alcohol for health reasons?

questions.e: To "accompany" someone is to go somewhere with them as a companion. "Follow" means to go behind, and "escort" suggests protection or guarding.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I would like to ....... my father to Kaduna?

questions.e: The idiom "one can't be too careful" means it is impossible to be overcautious, which fits the warning that "walls have ears".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
One ..... be too careful these days; times are uncertain and walls have ears?

questions.e: The correct pattern is 'so + adjective + as not to', giving 'I shall never be so tired as not to be able to write to you'. 'So tired such that' mixes two structures. The correct option is A.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I shall never be so tired ..... to write to you?
o: such that i will be unable

questions.e: "You'd better" (you had better) gives advice and is followed by the base verb: "you'd better lead the way". "You would better" is wrong.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
As you have been here before..... lead the way?

questions.e: The past perfect "had not seen" shows that the not-seeing happened over a period before the past meeting last week.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
My friend ....... me for many years when I met him last week.

questions.e: The buildings were constructed in the past, so the passive needs the past participle "were built". The plural subject "buildings" then takes "are" for their present state.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
School buildings that ...... in 1950...... now uninhabitable?

questions.e: With a percentage, the verb agrees with the noun after "of": "workers" is plural, and "yearly" shows a habit, so the present passive "are retained" is right.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Sixty percent of the unskilled workers...... yearly by the company?

questions.e: "Defects" is plural, so the demonstrative must be "these", and the plural subject takes the plural verb "call".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Defects like ...... in government's development plans..... for extra vigilance?

questions.e: "One of the most..." must be followed by a plural noun: "centres". "Electronics" (the industry) is the correct noun modifier, not the adjective "electronic".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Tokyo is one of the most developed ...... of the world?

questions.e: The verb "liaise" takes "with" for the person or body, and matters discussed take "on": "liaise with the management on corporate matters".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The director is to liaise ..... the management ...... corporate matters?

questions.e: To "shuttle between" two places is to travel back and forth between them regularly, which suits a route linking Sokoto and Kano.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Some motorist ..... Sokoto and Kano.

questions.e: "Since" introduces a reason clause that makes a complete sentence with the main clause: "Since the cold war is over, we can now start..."
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
...... we can now start meaningful development?
o: Since the cold war is over
That the cold war is over

questions.e: Both gaps follow a determiner ('my', 'the'), so both need the noun 'advice': 'My advice is for you to refuse the advice of the wicked'. 'Advise' is a verb, so D cannot be a correct answer. The correct option is B.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
My ...... is for you to refuse the ....... of the wicked?

questions.e: A "turning" is a side road leading off the one you are on, the usual word in giving directions: "take the third turning on the left".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Go straight down the hill and take the third ........ on the left. you can't miss it?

questions.e: To "affirm" is to state formally that something is true, the word used in sworn declarations. "Confirm" means to verify, and "conform" means to comply.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I hereby declare and ...... that, to the best of my knowledge, this statement is true in all
respects?

questions.e: To "turn to" the law means to seek help from it. A citizen correcting an injustice would go to the courts for redress.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
A citizen in a democracy can ...... the law if he or she wants to correct an injustice.

questions.e: We speak of working "under the sun", meaning exposed to its heat. "Underneath" suggests something physically covering.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The workers suffered a lot, toiling ..... the sun?

questions.e: A "delusion" is a false belief a person holds about themselves, such as wrongly believing she is intelligent. "Allusion" is an indirect reference, and "elision" is omission of sounds.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
She has the .... of being intelligent when in fact she is not?

questions.e: With "either...or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject (proximity rule). "You" is nearer and takes "are".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
Either Ekaette or you .... to go.

questions.e: A compound adjective before a noun is hyphenated and its noun stays singular: "a 90-year-old woman". Of the options, only "90-year" correctly uses the singular "year".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
........ woman was attacked by a group of bandits

questions.e: The preposition "for" gives the reason for an emotion: angry with someone for doing something.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
He was angry with me ...... being treated nonchalantly?

questions.e: "With his wife" is an added phrase, not part of the subject, so the verb agrees with the singular "teacher": "was".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The teacher with his wife ..... here?

questions.e: "Would have been convicted" is the third conditional, which requires "if" + past perfect: "if he had done this".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
....... he would have been convicted.

questions.e: The verb cling is irregular: cling, clung, clung. "Clinged" and "clang" are not correct forms.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
What saved her was that she ...... to the side of the boat?

questions.e: "For" is used with a length of time (the past three years); "since" is used with a starting point.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
She has been here ....... the past three years?

questions.e: The pattern "so + adjective + that" expresses result: so weak that he could not climb. "Too" pairs with "to", not "that".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
He was ...... weak .... he could not climb the stairs.

questions.e: In compounds with man or woman, both parts become plural: "women doctors".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The hospital can now boast of more.....

questions.e: In "one of those who", the relative pronoun "who" refers to the plural "those", so the verb is plural: "teach".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
He is one of those who ....... in my school?

questions.e: "No less than his workers" is a parenthetical addition, so the verb agrees with the singular subject "director": "is".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The director, no less than his workers ....... to blame?

questions.e: In reported questions the word order becomes a statement (subject before verb) and the tense shifts back: "what my name was".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The principal asked me ......?

questions.e: "Neither" adds a second negative statement after a negative one, with inverted order: "...neither did she".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
He did not explain what happened ..... did she?

questions.e: When the subject and object refer to the same people, a reflexive pronoun is needed: "enjoy themselves". "Theirselves" is non-standard.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
Did the boys enjoy ..... when they went on vacation?

questions.e: After "It's time", the past subjunctive (simple past form) is used for the present: "It's time the room was redecorated".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
It's time the room ...... it looks awful?

questions.e: "Would rather" + a different subject takes the past (subjunctive) form even for present or future time: "I would rather you cooked the dinner now".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
Her mother said to her 'I ...... the dinner now?

questions.e: "Admit" is followed by a gerund, and the negative is placed before it: "admitted not having a licence".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The driver of the car admitted ......a licence?

questions.e: "Credulity" is readiness to believe things. Saying it was "stretched to the limit" means what they heard was very hard to believe. "Credibility" is the quality of being believable.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The panel's ...... was stretched to the limit by what they heard.

questions.e: Adjectives follow a fixed order: opinion/age (old), then other description (discarded), then material (rubber) right before the noun. "Old" begins with a vowel sound, so "an" is used.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The poor man was pleased to find ..... tyre?

questions.e: A "prior engagement" is the standard phrase for an earlier commitment that prevents someone from accepting a new one.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The minister can't come today because he has ...... engagement?

questions.e: A "discrepancy" is a lack of agreement between two things that should match, such as two accounts of one incident.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The policeman pointed out a ...... between Mr. Ogene's two accounts of the incident?

questions.e: A "site engineer" supervises work at a construction site. "Cite" means to quote, and "sight" means vision; these are homophones.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The ...... engineer was unhappy with the shoddy work done by the contractors?

questions.e: "Request" is a transitive verb and takes a direct object without "for": "requested more answer sheets". The past tense matches "During the examination".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
During the examination, a student ...... more answer sheets?

questions.e: "Opportune" (well-timed) is an adjective with no -ed form, and "privileged" means honoured to have a special opportunity: "an opportune moment... to be privileged".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
It was an .... moment for us to be ..... to welcome the new Vice - Chancellor?

questions.e: The expression "a subject of ridicule" means someone people laugh at or mock.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
You must study hard this semester in order to avoid being made ...... ridicule?

questions.e: The idiom "have an edge over" someone means to have an advantage over them.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The fact that Olu able to guess correctly some of the questions that were asked, made him
....... the other candidates?

questions.e: To "stand down" means to withdraw from an election or position, especially in someone else's favour.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
One of the three candidates contesting the union election was obliged to ...... in favour of
his friends?

questions.e: The idiom "more power to your elbow" is an expression of encouragement and good wishes for further success.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
This is to congratulate you on your success in the last examination and wish you ...........?

questions.e: "One of" must be followed by a plural noun ("vice presidents"), while the verb agrees with the singular "one": "acts".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
One of the vice...... in an interim capacity?

questions.e: The idiom is "at the helm of affairs", meaning in control or in charge; "helm" is singular and "affairs" plural.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
A very popular ruler is at the ......?

questions.e: The standard form is "grassroots", meaning the ordinary people at the local level of society.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap(s) with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap(s).
The development is to be carried to the....... level?

questions.e: To be "duped" is to be tricked or deceived, which is exactly what a trickster does. "Cajoled" means coaxed by flattery.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
He was ....... by the trickster

questions.e: "Futile" means useless or pointless, which explains why the soldiers stopped fighting. "Inadequate" and "inefficient" do not imply giving up.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
When the soldiers saw that resistance was ....... they stopped fighting?

questions.e: "Brochures" are booklets with pictures and information advertising holidays and travel. A "prospectus" usually describes a school or company.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
You should read all the ...... carefully before you decide where to go on holiday?

questions.e: "The Emir and conqueror" refers to one person (a single article before both nouns), so the verb is singular. The simple present can show a scheduled future event: "arrives".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The Emir and conqueror of the enemy territories .......next week?

questions.e: The tag repeats the modal "ought" in the negative: "We ought to have visited..., oughtn't we?"
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
We ought to have visited the Governor ......?

questions.e: To agree that he did not sense her presence, the answer stays negative throughout: "No, he didn't". Mixing yes/no with the opposite verb is wrong.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
He didn't sense Obi's presence in the room, did he?

questions.e: "As long as" means provided that, introducing a condition: you can stay as long as you are quiet.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
You can stay here ....... as you are quite?

questions.e: "Buses" is plural, so it takes the plural demonstrative "these" and the plural auxiliary "do", followed by the base verb "go".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Where ...... buses ...... ?

questions.e: "Ours" here refers to a single venture, so it takes the singular "is". "A resource based venture" is a compound modifier with the noun "resource".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Ours ..... based venture

questions.e: To "reverse into" something means to drive backwards and hit it. "Reversed back" is redundant, since reversing already means going back.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The accident occurred when the driver of the car..... the lorry?

questions.e: "Would have helped" is the third conditional, which needs "if" + past perfect: "If you had asked me".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
...... i would have helped you?
o: Has it been that you asked me
Had itbeen that you asked me

questions.e: The idiom is "take the law into one's own hands", meaning to punish someone yourself instead of using the legal system. "Law" is singular and "own" is required.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The principal warned the students not to take the....... hands.

questions.e: After the verb "helped", the pronoun is an object, so "me" is correct. "Myself" is reflexive and needs "I" as the subject.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Those men helped Duped and ......?

questions.e: The past perfect needs the past participle of "lie" (to recline): lie, lay, lain. So "had hardly lain down". "Laid" belongs to "lay" (to put).
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I had hardly ...... down to sleep when I heard the gunshot.

questions.e: A "cobbler" repairs shoes. A tanner treats animal hides, a grocer sells food and a hosier sells socks and stockings.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
My shoes are worn out; I must see my ...... ?

questions.e: The subject is "a sterile range" (singular); the phrase about ravines is parenthetical. A mountain range covering a state needs the singular "encloses" in the key.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
A sterile range of mountains, broken at intervals by deep ravines ...... almost the whole of
this small state?

questions.e: The sentence gives two causes of Kunle's bad mood, joined by "and": arriving late, and Kemi's rather insolent manner also put him out of temper.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Kunle was annoyed for arriving late ..... put him out of temper?
o: and Kemi's rather insolent manner also
and Kemi's is also insolent which

questions.e: To "wrench" something is to pull it off with a violent twisting movement, which suits protesters tearing a statue from its fixtures.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The protesters, unable to pull down the statue,.... it from its fixtures.

questions.e: "There's" is the contraction of "there has" here: "There has been no official reaction". "Theirs" is a possessive pronoun.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
...... been no official reaction to your request yet?

questions.e: "News" is uncountable, so "a news" is wrong. "The news" refers to the specific news his looks suggest is coming.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
His looks portend that ....... would be unpleasant?

questions.e: "Should have been" with "By January 1999" expresses an expected completed period at a future point: by then I should have been ten years in service.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
By January 1999, I ..... ten years in the service of this institution?

questions.e: The accused is hopeful because no witness exists to "contradict" (deny or oppose) his story. "Corroborate" would mean to support it.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The accused is optimistic of regaining his freedom because there is no witness to ..... his
story?

questions.e: To "prevaricate" is to avoid giving a direct answer or delay a decision, which the leader is telling the listener not to do.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Don't ...... said the leader 'I want a decision now?

questions.e: Lost items that are found and returned are "recovered". "Found" lacks the sense of getting back stolen property.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Most of the missing jewelry were___________ by the police?

questions.e: "Cattle" is always plural, so it takes "are". In a compound adjective the noun is singular: "tick- free".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
All the cattle on Lamidi's farm ...... ?

questions.e: "So" + auxiliary + subject adds a matching positive statement, repeating the auxiliary implied in "saw" (did): "so did she".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
He saw the play and so ....... ?

questions.e: "Aroma" is the pleasant smell of food being cooked. "Fragrance" and "scent" are usually used for flowers or perfume.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The ..... of what she was cooking filled the whole compound?

questions.e: To "encroach on" someone's time is to take more of it than is right. "Invaded" and "trespassed" do not collocate with "time" here.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
I hope i have not ...... too much on your time?

questions.e: "Plain sailing" and "smooth sailing" both mean easy progress; the key takes "smooth sailing", contrasting with the earlier problems.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The exercise presented us with a lot of problems but later it was all ...... sailing?

questions.e: To be "inclined to" do something is to tend to do it. "Propensed" is not a word, and "disposed to" is more formal for willingness.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
In moments of serious economic hardship, many people are ....... to turn to God?

questions.e: Since the goal was allowed to stand, the striker was not offside; he was very well positioned, as "consequently" suggests.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
That centre-forward was....... consequently the goal was not disallowed?

questions.e: People cannot all buy expensive shoes because their incomes differ, i.e. because of differing purchasing power.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
We cannot all wear expensive shoes in situation of......?

questions.e: The pattern is "so + adjective + a + noun": "so deadly a disease". "Such" would need "such a deadly disease".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
AIDS is ..... disease that kills slowly but surely?

questions.e: When "hardly" begins a clause, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: "hardly had the talk begun when...".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
We had a dull evening because ......?
o: hardly the talk had begun when the lights went off
hardly had the talk begun when the light went off
the talk had hardly begun when the lights had gone out
the lights had hardly gone out when the talk began

questions.e: "Evocation" is bringing a feeling or memory vividly to mind, which suits recreating his childhood atmosphere. "Invocation" is a call for help, especially in prayer.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Soyinka's masterful ....... of the atmosphere of his childhood helped to make his book, Ake,
an ought success?

questions.e: The main clause uses the positive auxiliary "will", so the tag is the negative "won't they?"
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Students will always blame their teachers when examination results are unfavorable .......?

questions.e: To "eat one's words" is to take back what one has said. A stubborn man would never do that.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Okonkwo is a stubborn man, he will never ...... his words?

questions.e: "Lend" means give for a time, so "Kindly lend me your book". "My friend has borrowed mine" shows the friend took mine for a time.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Kindly .... me your book because my friends has ..... mine?

questions.e: With fractions, the verb agrees with the noun after "of": "the church" is singular, and "the previous day" needs past tense, so "was".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Three-quarters of the church....... painted by the members the previous day?

questions.e: "Neither" is used for two people and takes a singular verb: "neither of them has". "None" is for more than two.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Two young boys have been caught with parts of the stolen machine but....... admitted
stealing it?

questions.e: To "dart" is to move suddenly and quickly, typical of fish. Fish do not crawl, and "dotting" makes no sense.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Watching carefully, i could see the fish ...... along the bottom?

questions.e: "Mature" is both the adjective ("a mature student") and the verb ("to mature"). "Matured" is only the past form of the verb.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Emeka is now a ..... student but it took him years to .......?

questions.e: "Inform on" is not the sense here; the key reads "informed on their rearmament", i.e. their gathering of weapons again, which fits rebels about to fight back.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The rebels will soon fight back. We have been informed ...... their ....?

questions.e: "Temperament" is a person's nature, and drink "loosens the tongue", making someone talk freely. "Temperature" is about heat.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
Ali was honest and quite as a schoolboy, but too much drinking has now changed his ..... and
..... his tongue?

questions.e: A hospital "closed off" stops admitting people, and patients are put "on" beds.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The hospital was closed ...... because there were no beds to put patients ..... ?

questions.e: "With his son" is an added phrase, not part of the subject, so the verb agrees with the singular "judge": "is travelling".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The judge with his son ..... travelling to Lagos now?

questions.e: "Academic" as a noun means a university teacher or scholar. "Academia" is the academic world, and "academics" is plural.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
A university teacher is an ......?

questions.e: "Deer" has the same form in singular and plural: "many deer". "Dear" is a different word.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The adventurers run into many ..... in the forest?

questions.e: "Comprise" means consist of and takes no "of". The singular "class" takes "comprises".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The class ....... more girls than boys this session?

questions.e: Adjective order is size, colour, origin, material, then noun: "a small brown Nigerian earthen pot".
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
The tourist bought ...... ?
o: a brown small Nigerian earthen pot
a small brown Nigerian earthen pot
an earthen brown small Nigeria pot
a Nigerian small brown earthen pot

questions.e: A conference does not hold itself; it is held by organisers, so the passive is needed: 'the conference being held at Ibadan'. 'Conference holding' is a Nigerian usage, not standard English. The correct option is C.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gaps with the appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Most of us will attend the conference .... at Ibadan later this year.

questions.e: "Hang" meaning to suspend an object has the past participle "hung". "Hanged" is used only for executing people.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
I have already ..... the picture on the sitting-room wall?

questions.e: "Make a distinction" is the keyed collocation for achieving a distinction grade in an examination.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the the gap.
I shall work hard so that i can ..... a distinction in English?

questions.e: "Than" must follow a comparative, so the gap needs "more troublesome"; "much" intensifies the comparative.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the gap.
The baby was rather ..... than i could bear?

questions.e: "Forbid" can be followed by "from + -ing": "forbidden from joining". "In joining" and "on joining" are wrong.
questions.s:
Fill each of the gap with the appropriate option from the list following the gap.
Students were forbidden ...... any secret society.

questions.e: The present progressive "is marrying" shows a planned future arrangement, with Jide as the active subject who marries Ngozi. "Marry" takes a direct object, not "to" in the active voice.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
After two years of courtship, Jide is finally ....... Ngozi next Sunday?

questions.e: "Seek" is a transitive verb meaning to look for, so it takes its object directly: "seeking admission". Adding "for" is redundant.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
I am ...... admission to the university this year?

questions.e: "Seek" already means "try to obtain", so it needs no preposition: "I am seeking admission".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
I am ...... admission to the university this year?

questions.e: A "spontaneous" prayer comes naturally and immediately, without planning, which suits sudden gratitude. "Spasmodic" means occurring in fits and starts.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
The freed robber expressed his gratitude in a ..... prayer of thanksgiving?

questions.e: The correct spelling is "airborne", meaning carried in the air or in flight. It is an adjective and takes no -ed ending.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
By twelve midnight, we will be..... en route for Britain?

questions.e: "Querulous", meaning complaining and peevish, is the correct spelling; the other options are misspellings.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
They were all behaving like a bunch of ..... children?

questions.e: Numbers come first ('the first two'), and an opinion or quality adjective such as 'enlightened' comes before an age adjective such as 'young'. This gives 'the first two enlightened young ladies'. The correct option is A.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Mrs Ojo was one of ...... in my village?
o: the first two enlightened young ladies
the two first enlightened young ladies
the two first young enlightened ladies
the first two young enlightened ladies

questions.e: "Finesse" is skill and delicacy in handling people or situations, the quality lacking in his dealings with customers.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Ndem was suspended from work because he showed no ...... in dealing with the customers?

questions.e: The idiomatic adjective for a nose producing mucus is "runny", as in "a runny nose".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
The visitor was very uncomfortable because of his ..... nose?

questions.e: Students breaking rules "time and again" (repeatedly) and his not knowing how to stop them explains his "frustration".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
The principal expressed his ...... when the students broke the rules ....... and he didn't know
how to stop them?

questions.e: To "detect" a smell is to notice or discover it. "Smell the smell" is repetitive, and one does not hear or feel a smell.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Immediately I entered the house, I could ........the smell of gas from the kitchen?

questions.e: An adjective is needed before the noun "driving": "negligent" means careless. "Negligence" is a noun, and "negligible" means very small.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
The accident was due to ..... driving by the defendant?

questions.e: "Redress" is the remedy or compensation that a wronged person seeks through the courts. "Acquittal" is for an accused person.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Aggrieved persons are free to seek ...... in the court of law?

questions.e: The subject "chances" is plural, so it takes "have", and the passive present perfect is "have been jeopardized".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
His chances in the games ..... seriously jeopardized?

questions.e: The expression "you would be well advised to" means it would be sensible for you to do something.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
You would be well ........ to listen to what the teacher says?

questions.e: The passive participle "rooted" is needed, and the noun "commitment" requires an article and adjective: "rooted in a deep commitment".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Our economic programme is .....commitment to Nigeria's economic growth?

questions.e: "Shoulder to shoulder" means standing very close together side by side, which made him hard to identify in the crowd.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided
We found it difficult to identify him as the crowd was ......... around him.

questions.e: "Covert" means hidden or secret. Since the group could not act openly, their hostility was covert; "overt" means open.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
The group never felt strong enough to act in the open ....... hostility was the hallmark of
their resistance?

questions.e: The fixed expression is "on the alert", meaning watchful and ready for danger.
questions.s: Some robbers are on the prowl, we must be ..... ?

questions.e: "Although" sets up a contrast: the officer wanted a genuine report but got a ridiculous account instead.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
Although the officer wanted a ..... report on the matter, he got ....... account?

questions.e: The idiom is "grind to a halt". Grind is irregular (grind, ground, ground), so the present perfect is "has ground".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
My friend's car has ..... to a halt?

questions.e: To "sneer at" something is to show contempt for it, which matches a boastful person mocking others' efforts. "Scorn" does not take "at".
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
He boasts so much about his high scores and he ...... at the efforts of others?

questions.e: The pattern "so + adjective + that + clause" shows result: so credulous that he believes my ghost story.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
He is so credulous ...... my story about the ghost?

questions.e: To "make it up" means to become friends again after a quarrel.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
My friend and I have been quarrelling since yesterday and we haven't ....... yet.

questions.e: We "get off" public transport such as a train or bus. "Get out of" is used for a car.
questions.s:
Fill in the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided?
It was late when we decided to get ...... the train?

questions.e: A past hypothetical result uses "might + have + past participle", with "never" placed after the modal: "might never have been".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Without our relentless campaigns we might ....... sure of victory in the race for the National
Assembly.

questions.e: Trees able to withstand drought are "drought-resistant", the standard compound adjective for this quality.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
To check desertification in the arid zones ...... trees should be planted.

questions.e: A "turncoat" is a person who deserts one party or cause to join the opposing side. The other spellings are wrong.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
I like the character that played the role of a political ....... at the last convention of our party.

questions.e: "From the outset" means from the very beginning. "Onset" is the start of something unpleasant, such as an illness.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The man declared his intention from the -----

questions.e: Only a "swift-footed" (fast-running) athlete could win a race; flat-footed suggests clumsiness.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The Team Manager told us that the race could only be won by the .......

questions.e: "Several" requires a plural noun, and "sheep" has the same form in the plural. Ewe, lamb and goat would need -s.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
There are several ........ in the farmyard.

questions.e: "Elder" is used before a noun for the older of family members: "his elder brother". "Older" is typically used in comparisons with "than".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Audu fought with his ........ brother.

questions.e: An "epithet" is a descriptive name or phrase given to a person or place, such as "the Dark Continent" for Africa.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The Dark Continent was an ...... for Africa.

questions.e: "In time" means early enough to do something, here to see his family before they left.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
He arrived ....... to see his family leave for the countryside.

questions.e: The tag repeats the modal "can" from the statement, in the negative: "You can travel on your own, can't you?"
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
You can travel on your own, ......?

questions.e: To "cut in" means to interrupt someone who is speaking, which many cultures consider rude to elders.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Our culture does not allow one to ........ when an elderly person is speaking.

questions.e: After the article "a", a noun is needed: "a loss". "Lose" is a verb, "lost" its past form, and "loose" means not tight.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Raffle draws, like gambling, often end in a ....... for me.

questions.e: "Equipment" is an uncountable noun, so it never takes a plural -s or "an": "enough equipment".
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The new school is not provided with .......for science practicals.

questions.e: A "turn-out" is the number of people who attend an event. "Turnover" relates to business sales or staff changes.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
llesa witnessed the largest ..... of writers at any convention in recent times.

questions.e: The press is known for criticising or mocking politicians, so they were "ridiculed". "Ostracized" means excluded from society.
questions.s:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The politicians were ....... by the press.

questions.e: No sane person would act in a "cruel" manner. "Rational" and "composed" describe how a sane person would behave.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
I do not think any sane person would have acted in such a ....... manner.

questions.e: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "parents" (plural), and "now" needs present tense: "attend".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Neither Agbo nor his parents ...... the meetings now.

questions.e: Dancing that is "scientific" needs careful design of movements, i.e. some choreographic skill.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Modern dancing has become rather scientific and so requires .......

questions.e: "Had he considered..." is an inverted third conditional, so the main clause is "would have + past participle": "would have stepped down".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Had he considered his public image carefully, he ..... from his office in the election.

questions.e: "The government" acting as one body takes the singular verb "was" and the singular possessive "its", keeping agreement consistent.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The government which .....recruiting ....... workers suddenly stopped doing so.

questions.e: After verbs of perception like "see", the bare infinitive describes a complete action: "saw the culprit approach and hit the man".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Of course, we all saw the culprit ....... and hit the man on the head.

questions.e: "Precocious" describes a child who develops abilities or maturity unusually early. "Premature" means happening too soon.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
A child that shows mature characteristics at an early age may be described as .......

questions.e: A "prototype" is a first model of a design. The key treats it as a model of the proposed building shown to the contractor.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The company Director showed the contractor a ....... of the proposed office complex.

questions.e: "Should you come early" is an inverted conditional meaning "If you come early". "Should in case" is a redundant mix.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
....... you come early to the new house, clean up my flat.

questions.e: "Cost" is irregular, and its past tense is also "cost". "Costed" is used only for estimating costs.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
This imposing edifice ....... a fortune to build.

questions.e: "In respect to" in the key is meant as "out of respect for" his age, i.e. they released him in consideration of his age.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
They let him go in ....... to his age.

questions.e: To "replicate" is to make an exact copy, as in scientific cloning of human beings. "Fabricate" suggests making something false.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Some scientists are trying to ...... human beings in their laboratories.

questions.e: "He does not seem" is a negative statement, so the tag is positive: "does he?"
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
He does not seem to know how to solve the problem ...... ?

questions.e: "Used to + verb" describes a past habit no longer true: "These villagers used to grow rice". "Are used to" would need "growing".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
These villagers ....... to grow rice.

questions.e: To "obliterate" is to wipe out completely, so Ade tried to erase all memory of his father. "Recall" and "eulogize" would keep the memory alive.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Ade tried to ...... all memory of his dead father.

questions.e: A comparison requires a comparative adjective followed by 'than', so the sentence becomes 'less appealing for Jos residents than for foreigners' — option C, less / than.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The weather is probably ..... appealing for people who live in Jos ..... for foreigners.

questions.e: To "reconcile" divergent views is to bring them into agreement, the purpose of such a meeting.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The meeting was called to ...... divergent views on the subject of a national conference.

questions.e: To "defuse" a bomb is to remove its fuse so it cannot explode. "Diffuse" means to spread out, and "detonate" means to explode it.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The police came early enough to...... the bomb planted by the rioters.

questions.e: The perfect participle "Having been told" shows an action completed before the main action: having been informed, I prepared.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
..... told of his impending arrival, I worked hard to make his short stay very comfortable.

questions.e: "More power to your elbow" is the idiom expressing encouragement and good wishes.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
More ...... to your elbow as you campaign for press freedom.

questions.e: An "estranged" husband is one who no longer lives with or is on good terms with his wife, which explains her wish to reconcile.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
When Ajike met her ..... husband at the party, she felt like reconciling with him.

questions.e: To "fall back on" something is to use it as a reserve when the usual thing fails, as with a generator during a power cut.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
They had to ...... the generator when the electricity failed.

questions.e: To be "hemmed in" is to be surrounded and restricted, unable to move or act freely.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
The editor was not happy that the Nigerian press was hemmed .......

questions.e: With fractions the verb agrees with the noun after "of": "the hostel" is singular (has), while "the students" is plural (have).
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
Three-quarters of the hostel ........ been painted and three-quarters of the students ......
moved in.

questions.e: In formal concord, the head noun "range" is singular, so it takes "was", with the past tense matching "recently concluded".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided. 
A wide range of options ....... made available to the political parties during the recently
concluded elections.

questions.e: The correct spelling is "guerrillas", with "gue" and a double r and double l.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The army officer said that more ...... would be needed to prosecute the war?

questions.e: When "one" is the subject, the formal pronoun repeating it is also "one": "If one perseveres, one will succeed".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
If one perseveres ....... will surely succeed?

questions.e: "Intricate" means very complicated and detailed, which pairs well with "elaborate" rules that are hard to master.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
Musa has lived here for five years but he does not seem able to get over the
enormously........ and elaborate rules that govern the society?

questions.e: A party losing members who have "defected to" other parties becomes "vulnerable" as elections approach.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
As election day draws near, the party looks ...... because many of its members have.......
other parties?

questions.e: The gerund "riding" works as the subject, and "harmful" takes the preposition "to": harmful to your health.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
....... a motor cycle can be harmful ..... your health.

questions.e: "Though" signals contrast: the company's future is "rosy" (bright) even though many seem "pessimistic" about it.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The future of the company is ...... though many seem .....about it?

questions.e: "By this time next year" points to a state completed before a future time, so the future perfect "will have been" fits.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
By this time next year, I ...... twenty years old?

questions.e: "Amnesia" is loss of memory, so once cured he no longer suffers from it.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
Ali has been cured of his amnesia, he no longer suffers from ...... ?

questions.e: "Operations" is plural, so it takes "do", followed by the base verb "cover".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The operations of the bank ........ not ...... cottage and small-scale industries?

questions.e: "Agree with" is used for agreeing with people or opinions, which is the sense the key takes here; terms of a contract would usually take "agree to" or "on".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The members of the team agree ........ all the members of the contract?

questions.e: Adjective order puts opinion (good) before size/length (long): "a good long talk together".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
Whenever we have ....... we feel better?

questions.e: "Prowess" is great skill or ability, especially in sport, which a match lets a team display.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The match gave the team a chance to show their ........?

questions.e: "These" requires the plural "analyses", and after "must have" the past participle "attracted" is needed.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
These ........ must have ........ the World Bank officials.

questions.e: After "elect" with an object, the title follows directly without an article: "elected Baba chairman".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The members elected Baba ....... of the committee?

questions.e: The idiom is "on a common footing", meaning on an equal basis or level.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
One advantage of the English language in Nigeria is that it puts everyone ........ a common
........ ?

questions.e: "Ludicrous" means so absurd as to be laughable, which fits comments described as very amusing.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The officer described the comments as ........ because it was very amusing?

questions.e: "Solicit" is transitive and takes its object directly: "solicit financial support". "Support" is uncountable, so "a" is wrong.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
You are free to solicit ....... support from the board?

questions.e: An appreciative audience acts as individuals clapping "their" hands, and "encomiums" are expressions of high praise. "Invectives" are abusive words.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The highly appreciative audience clapped ........ hands and showered ......... on the lecturer?

questions.e: When an event "comes off", it takes place or succeeds as planned. Despite preparations, the wedding did not happen.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
Despite all preparations, the wedding did not ....... ?

questions.e: The relative clause refers to the plural "questions" (which have attracted attention), while the main subject "the quality" is singular (has never been).
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
The quality of your questions which ....... always attracted attention ....... never been in
doubt.

questions.e: "In" is used for being within a city (in Kaduna), and "on" is used for a duty or task: "on an official assignment".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
He is ....... Kaduna ......... an official assignment?

questions.e: "Assault and battery" is a fixed legal phrase for threatening and then physically attacking someone.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
We did not understand what the magistrate said about ........ and battery?

questions.e: In negative questions and statements, "anyone" is normally used rather than "someone": "Didn't anyone draw your attention...?"
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
Didn't ......... draw your attention to the entry requirements?

questions.e: "Barring" means except for or unless there are: barring any problems, I shall travel.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the lists provided.
....... any problems, I shall travel to London tomorrow on a business trip?

questions.e: A determiner and quantity come first, then the colour adjective: "a dozen white eggs".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
He put .......... in a basket?

questions.e: In "course material writers", the nouns act as modifiers before "writers" and stay singular without an apostrophe.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Course ......... writers are to reflect local colour

questions.e: After "The reason why... was", a "that"-clause is used. "Because" repeats the idea of reason and is redundant.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The reason why he was not offered admission was ...... his results could not be found?

questions.e: "If" + simple past ("saw") is the second conditional, so the main clause uses "would": "would you be able to identify him?"
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
If you saw the photograph of the man ....... you be able to identify him?

questions.e: "Some kind" with a singular verb ("will put him up") requires a singular noun: "some kind man".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
As Obande does not know anyone in this city, he hopes that some kind ........ will put him up
for the night?

questions.e: In reported questions the word order is subject + verb and the tense shifts back after "asked": "what the problem was".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The doctor asked the patient what .......?

questions.e: "Elite" is a collective noun for a privileged group, used here as "one of the elite". "Elitist" describes an attitude.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The woman is one of the ........ of the society?

questions.e: With fractions the verb agrees with the noun after "of": "people" and "huts" are both plural, so "were" in both gaps.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
