Three quarters of the people in the village ....... killed but only half of their huts .........
affected?

questions.e: With "woman" as a modifier of a plural noun, both become plural: "women occupants".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The armed robbers went into the house and robbed the three .......?

questions.e: The idiom is "take the law into one's own hands", which requires "into" and "own".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
It was a free-for-all and the students were blamed for taking the law ....... ?

questions.e: "Determining" means deciding or having a strong influence on the result. "Determinate" means fixed or definite.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The candidate's charisma should be a ....... factor in winning the election?

questions.e: "I can't stand..." is a negative statement, so agreement is expressed with "Me neither". "Me too" agrees with a positive statement.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
I can't stand people prying into my private life; Ladi said '......' agreed Agbenu?

questions.e: A period of time treated as one unit takes a singular verb: "Four weeks is enough".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Four weeks ....... enough for the police to conclude their investigation?

questions.e: The possessive goes at the end of the whole phrase: "someone else's property".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
It is bad to take ........ property without permission?

questions.e: "Whom" is needed because the pronoun is the object of "seen": I haven't seen him (whom).
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
My classmate ....... I haven't seen for years, wrote to me last week.

questions.e: A polite request with "if you would" is answered with "I would be very grateful", in the conditional.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
If you would do me this favour, I ......... be very grateful?

questions.e: "The" is used before musical instruments when talking about playing them: "plays the violin".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Ali plays ...... violin with remarkable skill?

questions.e: The correct spelling is "privilege": p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e, with no d.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
I have the ....... of meeting the President?

questions.e: "Coarse" means rough and rude in manner. "Course" is a path or subject, "coerce" is a verb, and "causal" relates to cause.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
The sergeant spoke to me in a...... manner?

questions.e: "Lest" (for fear that) is followed by "should" + base verb or the subjunctive: "lest he should miss the train".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Idankwo ran ...... miss the train?

questions.e: To "get on with" work is to make progress with it; "how is he getting on with...?" asks about progress.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
How is the new editor ...... on with his work?

questions.e: After "to", the base verb "lose" (to misplace) is needed. "Loose" means not tight, and "loss" is a noun.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Be careful not to ..... this money?

questions.e: The statement is negative ("are not well disposed"), so the tag uses the positive form of the same auxiliary: "are they?"
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Nowadays, many graduate are not well disposed to teaching ........?

questions.e: "Regularly" shows a habit, which uses the simple present, and the singular subject Adika takes "receives".
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
Adika ....... a message from the club regularly?

questions.e: The passive "It is often said that" introduces a general claim, and the singular "inflation" takes "results" in the present.
questions.s:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
It is often ....... that inflation ....... from too much money chasing very few goods?

questions.e: A 'pastime' is a hobby, spelt as one word with a single 's'. 'Get through with' means to finish a task.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I shall find time for my ..... when I get ....... with this difficult assignment?

questions.e: 'Not' is already negative, so a positive pronoun is needed: 'not afraid of anybody'. 'Nothing', 'nobody' and 'no one' would create a double negative.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Agbo says he is not afraid of .......?

questions.e: A possessive determiner is needed before the noun 'responsibility', so 'their' is correct. 'Theirs' stands alone without a noun, and 'their's' and 'theirs'' are never correct.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
It is ...... responsibility to look after parents in old age?

questions.e: 'Exemplify or demonstrate' pairs two words of similar meaning: to show by example or illustration. The other verbs don't mean to illustrate.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
One needs to exemplify or ....... the aspect of the subject being discussed?

questions.e: In careful standard usage, 'due to' is adjectival and follows a noun or a form of 'be', as in 'His absence was due to illness'. An opening adverbial phrase takes 'owing to': 'Owing to his illness, ...'. The correct option is C.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
....... his illness, Muhammad could not come to school?

questions.e: 'Pay off' means to succeed or bring good results after effort. 'Paid up', 'paid for' and 'paid out' relate to money.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
After so many trials, the experiment ....... ?

questions.e: The correct adjective for someone who is cunning or deceptive is 'tricky'. 'Trickful', 'trickish' and 'tricker' are not standard English words.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
People dislike Mariam because she is ...... ?

questions.e: After a preposition ('to'), the object form of the relative pronoun is needed: 'the one to whom the job was given'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Actually, he forgot the one to ...... the job was given?

questions.e: A negative statement takes a positive question tag. 'You may not have heard…' therefore takes a positive tag, and 'have you?' is the only positive option offered.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
You may not have heard the last word on the matter ...... ?

questions.e: 'Commission' is spelt with double 'm' and double 's'. Here it means a solemn task or duty.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
All God's prophets were given the great ...... to preach salvation to people?

questions.e: 'For months' describes a period continuing up to now, so the present perfect is needed. Singular 'he' takes 'hasn't been'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Ali goes to stadium regularly, but he ...... to the church for months?

questions.e: 'Each' is singular, so 'each of the houses' takes the singular verb 'has'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Each of the houses ..... a new look?

questions.e: 'Morale' means confidence and spirit, which a speech can boost. 'Moral' and 'morality' relate to right and wrong, and a 'mural' is a wall painting.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The minister addressed the workers to boost their ......?

questions.e: Agreeing with a negative statement in English takes 'No', so the answer is 'No, he isn't'. 'Yes' would contradict 'he isn't'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He isn't coming home, is he? ....... he isn't

questions.e: The correct spelling is 'harassment', with one 'r' and double 's'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
No teacher of honour would subject his student to any form of ......?

questions.e: A producer places a value on a product by considering its 'worth', meaning its value. The other words don't describe value.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Each producer is able to place on his product by considering its ........ ?

questions.e: 'A number of' means 'several', so it takes a plural verb. Since the cars have just been recovered, 'have been' is correct.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The police claim that a number of stolen cars ....... recovered?

questions.e: The fixed expression is 'shake hands with someone', with plural 'hands' and no possessive.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The chair man refused to shake ........ with the secretary.

questions.e: You spin wool into 'yarn', the thread used for weaving or knitting. 'Was seen' is followed by the - ing form 'spinning'. 'Yards' are units of length.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The poor widow who could not buy the clothes was seen ....... her wool into ....... yesterday?

questions.e: The correlative pair is 'not only … but also'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He not only looked after the children when their parents died, ...... sponsored their
education to university?

questions.e: Supporters rally round a leader in times of 'crisis', meaning difficulty or danger. 'Critism' and 'disilusionment' are misspelt.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
His supporters railed round him in moments of ........ ?

questions.e: A 'literal' translation is word for word and can miss the intended meaning. 'Literary' relates to literature, and 'lateral' means sideways.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The interpreter was wrong because he gave the congregation a ....... translation of the
pastor's statement?

questions.e: In reported speech after a past reporting verb, the tense shifts back and the word order becomes that of a statement: 'asked me if I was tired'. No question mark or inversion is used.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
Yesterday, my mother asked me......

questions.e: The correct idiom is 'with regard to', meaning concerning. 'With regards to' and 'as regard to' are non-standard.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The Bank Manager assured us that there was nothing to worry about ...... ?

questions.e: Adjectives follow a set order: opinion, then process or type, then material. That gives 'an attractive carved wooden tray', with 'an' before the vowel sound.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The first prize was ....... tray?

questions.e: The fixed expression is 'step by step', meaning gradually, one stage at a time.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
Tsadu always cautions that difficult jobs should be done .......?

questions.e: We are angry 'with' a person, and one person can differ 'with' another, meaning disagree with them.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
I was often angry ....... Oche since he differed ....... me often?

questions.e: 'Several' is a determiner that can come directly before 'reasons'. 'Plenty' needs 'of', 'myriad of' needs 'a', and 'concerned' doesn't fit the sense.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
I am writing to you for ....... reasons?

questions.e: We sit 'in' silence. Eyes that 'roam' a room move slowly around it, which is the natural pairing.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
As we sat ....... the silence, my eyes ....... the room?

questions.e: The question asks about a completed action before a past moment, when the gates were closed, so the past perfect 'had returned' is needed.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
Is it true that Okoro ........ when the gates were closed?

questions.e: A library 'lends' books, giving them out temporarily. Readers 'borrow' them. 'Renting' and 'loaning' imply payment or are less idiomatic here.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The public library has stopped ........ books to readers?

questions.e: In a time clause referring to the future, English uses the simple present, not 'will': 'until it stops raining'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
We won't leave until it ........ raining?

questions.e: 'Historic' means very important or significant in history, which fits an event that marked a new beginning. 'Historical' simply means relating to the past.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The ...... event marked the beginning of a new life for the entire cabinet?

questions.e: The train's departure happened before another past action ('I arrived'), so the past perfect 'had left' is needed.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The train ...... before I arrived?

questions.e: A positive statement with the auxiliary 'can' takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary: 'can't you?'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
You can travel on your own ....?

questions.e: In 'with a view to', the 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: 'with a view to selling it'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The man is refurbishing the flat with a view to ......it?

questions.e: When a noun is used as a modifier it is normally singular, so the phrase is 'child soldiers'. 'Childish' means immature.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
The Secretary-General was shocked at the number of...... ?

questions.e: 'Unkempt' means untidy or uncombed and is the standard word for messy hair. 'Unkept' is a misspelling here.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
In spite of Shade's good looks, her hair is always ...... ?

questions.e: 'By the end of …' points to an action completed before a future time, so the future perfect 'will have known' is needed.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
By the end of the football match today, we ...... the best player?

questions.e: 'Deference' means polite respect and submission, which is what African custom expects the young to show elders.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
It is African for a younger person to show ...... to elders?

questions.e: In a relative clause, the verb agrees with the antecedent of 'who'. Here that is 'you', so the clause needs 'are': 'You, who are convicted, should appeal.'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(S).
You, who ...... convicted, should appeal.

questions.e: 'A number of' means 'many', so it takes a plural verb: 'a number of stolen cars have been recovered'. 'Being' cannot follow 'have' here.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The police claim that a number of stolen cars ....... recovered?

questions.e: 'He's been' is the contraction of 'He has been', the present perfect needed with 'several times'. 'He is been' is ungrammatical.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
....... been there to look several times without success?

questions.e: An adverb ('dangerously') modifies the adjective ('low'), which modifies 'level'. 'Lowly' means humble in rank.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The old man was rushed to hospital when his blood pressure dropped to a ....... level?

questions.e: Hoping that continued up to a past event, losing the election, needs the past perfect continuous: 'had been hoping'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Until he lost the election, agbo ....... to be Student Union president?

questions.e: 'Would succeed' in the main clause shows a second (hypothetical) conditional, which takes the simple past in the if-clause: 'If he applied…'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
If he ....... for admission, I am sure he would succeed?

questions.e: 'Ruthless' means having no pity or mercy, which matches 'showed no mercy'. 'Benevolent' is the opposite.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The ....... robber showed no mercy during the attack?

questions.e: The British spelling is 'diarrhoea', with double 'r' and 'oea'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Did you have ....... when you went to visit the medical doctor?

questions.e: This first conditional uses the simple present in the if-clause. In British English the verb is spelt 'practise' ('practice' is the noun).
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
your performance will improve if you ..... hard?

questions.e: Adjectives follow the order size, then colour, then type or purpose: 'big black spitting cobra'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The brave hunter killed the ...... in the forest?

questions.e: 'Wrote' is simple past with no auxiliary, so the tag uses 'did': 'didn't he?'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He wrote to you, .......?

questions.e: To be 'founded on' something means to be established on it as a basis. 'Funded' relates to money, and 'found' is the past of 'find'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The clubs were not ...... on a solid ethical base?

questions.e: 'Watched' sets the narrative in the past, so the past tense 'dug' is needed. 'Dugged' is not a word.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I watched him as he ....... the hole?

questions.e: A 'portable' radio is easy to carry around. 'Potable' means safe to drink.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
His father hardly misses the news because he goes about with his ....... radio?

questions.e: Formal written requests or complaints submitted to a commission are called 'petitions'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The investigation Commission has treated all the ......submitted to it by the warning
factions?

questions.e: 'Those of his elder brothers' means the clothes belonging to his elder brothers. The 'of' already shows possession, so no apostrophe is needed. In standard English the term is 'elder', not 'senior', brother.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Olu brought his clothes and those of his ...... ?

questions.e: An 'aroma' is a pleasant smell, especially of food cooking. 'Stench' is a bad smell, and 'flavour' is taste.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Our neighbour was attracted by the ....... from my mother's cooking?

questions.e: To 'air' one's views means to express them publicly.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Everybody is allowed to ....... his view on state matters?

questions.e: To 'come off' means to take place or happen as planned. Despite the preparations, the wedding did not happen.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best best completes the gap(s).
Despite all preparations, the wedding did not ...... ?

questions.e: To 'beat up' someone is to attack them violently. 'Rusticated' means suspended from a university as punishment.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
For beating...... his coursemate, Agbo was ..... from the university?

questions.e: 'Occasionally' (from time to time) fits a generally peaceful life disturbed by rumours now and then.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
We have been living peacefully here but ....... hear rumours of war?

questions.e: A 'pliable' person is easily influenced or persuaded, which is why Ayo could be tricked. 'Uncompromising' would make him hard to trick.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Because of his ........ nature Ayo was tricked out of his wristwatch?

questions.e: 'To see the writing on the wall' is an idiom meaning to recognise signs that trouble is coming. The steward missed the warning signs.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
The idle steward could not see ...... on the wall, and he lost his job.

questions.e: 'Says' is present tense, and the coordinate 'but will accommodate me' refers to now and the future, so the present 'is not able to' fits. 'Cannot be able to' is redundant.
questions.s:
Choose the option that completes the gap(s).
He says he ...... find me a job, but will accommodate me

questions.e: The subject of the verb 'went' must be in the subject form: 'Amadi and I'. 'Me' is an object pronoun, and 'myself' is reflexive.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
........ went to the stadium to watch a football match?

questions.e: 'If he arrived' (past form for a hypothetical) is a second conditional, so the main clause takes 'would' plus the base verb: 'would blame'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
If he arrived late, everyone ........ him?

questions.e: 'Found' reports a state at that past moment, so 'he was dead' fits. 'Had been dead' would need a time span, such as 'for hours'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
When they examined his body, they found that he ....... ?

questions.e: 'On end' is an idiom meaning continuously, without stopping, as in 'for days on end'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
The rain fell for days ......?

questions.e: In reported speech after the past 'said', the earlier action shifts to the past perfect: 'he had mislaid'. 'Had forgot' and 'he have lost' are ungrammatical.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Yesterday in the hall, Ola said that ...... his watch?

questions.e: 'Teachers' training' uses the plural possessive, the training of teachers in general. The apostrophe comes after the plural 's'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Government should invest more in ....... training?

questions.e: The collocation is 'a wealth of experience', meaning a great deal of it.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
The team has benefited from the coach's ....... of experience?

questions.e: 'Hardly any' means almost none, describing a nearly empty road. 'No any' is ungrammatical.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
There was ...... any traffic as he drove home?

questions.e: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it takes the -ing form: 'look forward to seeing you'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
I look forward to ....... you next week?

questions.e: Someone who cannot speak clearly and repeats sounds involuntarily is 'stuttering'. 'Gesticulating' means making gestures.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
The girl cannot speak with a clear voice; she is always ........?

questions.e: The correct phrase is 'commiserated with', meaning expressed sympathy to. 'Condoled' needs 'with' and is uncommon; 'greeted' doesn't convey sympathy.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
The politician ....... the family of the deceased?

questions.e: The phrasal verb is 'zero in on', meaning to aim at or focus closely on a target.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Our soldiers are starting to zero ....... the enemy?

questions.e: 'Says' is present, so the expectation is present ('expects'). A future arrival on 'this Friday' takes 'will arrive'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
My father has been away on a journey but my mother says she ....... he....... this Friday?

questions.e: 'The rest of the thieves' means the remaining thieves. Both 'the' and 'of the' are needed before a specific plural noun.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Kola was fined;....... thieves were given a jail sentence?

questions.e: Standard English says 'did not have the opportunity'. 'Was not chanced' and 'was not opportuned' are Nigerian non-standard forms.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
I....... to pursue my education?

questions.e: A negative question takes a non-assertive pronoun: 'Didn't anyone…?' 'Nobody' would create a double negative.
questions.s:
Choose the option that complete the gap(s).
Didn't ...... draw your attention to the entry requirements?

questions.e: In a relative clause, the relative pronoun (here an omitted 'that') already stands for the object, so 'it' must not be repeated: 'a language I can't speak well'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Kanuri is a language ..........?
o: that I can't speak it well
of which I can't speak it well

questions.e: In reported speech after a past verb, the question becomes a statement with 'whether/if', the tense shifts back, and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before'. Only C follows all these rules.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Last Tuesday, Ochonu asked me .........?

questions.e: After 'has', the past participle 'begun' is needed. The phrasal verb is 'sober up', meaning to become less drunk.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The young man has ..... to sober.......after being drunk?

questions.e: 'Split' is irregular and has the same form in the past participle: 'had split'. 'Splitted' and 'splited' are wrong.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
My mother had ........ the fire wood before it began to rain?

questions.e: 'Feuding' communities are in a bitter, prolonged quarrel. The idiom is 'take the law into their own hands'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The police officer warned the ....... communities against taking the law ...... hands?

questions.e: To 'come down with' an illness means to catch it, so he had come down with influenza.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Agbo could not travel as he had come ....... influenza?

questions.e: In a future time clause beginning with 'when', English uses the simple present: 'When he returns, tell him…'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
When he ....... from his journey, tell him I want to see him?

questions.e: The leaving happened before the past action of knocking, so the past perfect 'had already left' is required.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I knocked at his door, but he .......

questions.e: 'Few' (without 'a') means hardly any, which explains why the lecture was cancelled. 'A few' means some. 'Little' is used with uncountable nouns.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
....... of the students turned up, so the lecture was cancelled?

questions.e: After the article 'a', a noun is needed: 'complaint'. 'Complain' is the verb.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He brought a ...... against his neighbour?

questions.e: 'Capacity' is the amount a place can hold, which is the right word for how many guests a hotel can take.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The hotel lacks the ....... for accommodating so many guests?

questions.e: After 'would', the base form of the verb is needed: 'lose'. 'Loose' means not tight, and 'loss' is a noun.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
If you are not careful, you would ....... your money?

questions.e: The natural collocation is 'achieve perfection', meaning to reach it through effort.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
You must practice in order to ...... perfection?

questions.e: 'Intolerable' means unbearable, which describes a room you had to leave. 'Intolerant' describes people who won't accept others' views.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The condition of the room was so .....so i went outside?

questions.e: A negative statement ('You don't like…') takes a positive tag with the same auxiliary: 'do you?'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
You don't like Mathematics, ...... you?

questions.e: To 'write off' a debt is to cancel it, accepting that it won't be paid.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
They have had their debt written ...... by their creditors?

questions.e: A compound adjective of number plus noun uses the singular noun: a 'two storey' building, not 'two-storeyed'. Normally it is hyphenated (two-storey); 'story' is the American spelling.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Uncle Ochai now has enough money to complete his ......... building?

questions.e: 'By the end of this month' plus an ongoing action over 'years' needs the future perfect continuous: 'I will have been studying'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
By the end of this month, ...... for years in this school?

questions.e: 'Lay' (past form 'laid') means to put something down and takes an object, such as 'the picture'. 'Lay' as the past of 'lie' and 'lain' take no object.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He ........ the picture on the table?

questions.e: 'Would not' expresses refusal or unwillingness in the past, which fits a mean person declining to lend money. 'Could not' would mean he was unable.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He is really very mean. He ...... not lend me the money I wanted?

questions.e: An 'affront' is an insult to someone's pride or dignity. 'An affront to/on his dignity' fits.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
When the cashier told him to join the queue, he considered it ....... his dignity.

questions.e: The impersonal pronoun 'one' is used for people in general, and its possessive is 'one's': 'return one's greeting'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
If anyone greets you, it is only polite to return...... greeting?

questions.e: In standard usage, a student lives 'on campus', without an article.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Amina lives ....... campus?

questions.e: The rejections happened in a period up to now, and the acceptance 'would be a departure' from them. The present perfect 'have taken place' fits.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
An acceptance of the offer would be a departure from the several rejections that ....... ?

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'in accordance with', meaning in agreement with or following.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The officer acted in ....... the instructions?

questions.e: To 'detonate' a bomb is to make it explode. With no other context, it is the natural verb for what happens to a bomb.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The bomb was ......

questions.e: The adjective 'envious' takes the preposition 'of': 'envious of other people's achievements'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
If you want to succeed in life, don't be envious ......... other people's achievement?

questions.e: To value one thing 'above' another means to rate it as more important. Here honour is valued above life.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
They are taught to value honour ........ their lives?

questions.e: 'Consecutive' means following one after another without a break, so it means two nights in a row. 'Concurrent' means happening at the same time.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I missed the match though it was shown on television on two ...... nights?

questions.e: To 'recompense' someone is to compensate them for loss or harm. 'Indemnity' is a noun and can't follow 'to'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The company paid some money to Abu to .......him for losses he suffered during the
accident?

questions.e: A plan that 'falls through' fails to happen. A 'lifeline' is something that offers rescue or vital help.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Our plan for the trip fell ....... when the rich man did not give us a life.......?

questions.e: To 'amass' wealth is to gather a large amount of it, often greedily, which is what government frowns on.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Government has frowned upon politicians who are out to ...... wealth?

questions.e: 'You are putting…' uses the auxiliary 'are', so the negative tag is 'aren't you?'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
You are just putting the hat on ........ ?

questions.e: To 'cow' someone 'into submission' is to frighten them into obeying. It is the fixed collocation.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He was determined to ....... all position into submission?

questions.e: The verb 'persist' takes the preposition 'in': 'persisted in revealing'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I tried to discourage him, but he persisted ........ revealing the secret of his son.

questions.e: To be 'tuned in to' interests is to be aware of and responsive to them. 'People from all walks of life' means people of every background.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I am told that the market is ...... in to the interests of people from all ........ of life?

questions.e: To be 'in correspondence with' someone is to exchange letters with them, as pen pals do.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Uche has been in ...... with his pen pal for years?

questions.e: 'Despondent' means low in spirits and without hope, which is a natural reaction to being unable to pass.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Abba became ...... about his in ability to pass the examination?

questions.e: 'Not only' has to sit right before the first thing it introduces, which here is 'as a painter'; so the gap takes 'is gifted not only', balanced by 'but also as a sculptor'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Lemoti ....... as a painter, but also as a sculptor?

questions.e: To 'rattle off' is to recite something quickly and fluently from memory, like a list of dates.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He can recall the important dates in the nation's history, it is interesting to listen as he
rattles........?

questions.e: Reported speech after past 'asked' uses 'if' plus statement order, shifts tense back to 'had come', and changes 'yesterday' to 'the day before'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Last Monday his father asked me, ....... ?
o: if i had come some days before
if I had come the day before

questions.e: In reported speech, pronouns shift to the reporter's view: 'I' becomes 'he' and 'you' becomes 'her'. The tense moves back to 'was', giving 'that was the girl he told her about'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The boy told his mother...... ?
o: that was the girl he told her about
that was the girl I told you about her
that was the girl I told her about
that is the girl he told her about

questions.e: To 'pull through' is to recover from a serious illness or injury.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
His wife was badly injured in the fracas, but I think she will pull ....... ?

questions.e: The key treats 'a wide range of options' as plural in meaning (many options), so it takes the plural past 'were'. This is notional agreement, as with 'a number of'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
A wide range of options ....... made available to students in their final year last year?

questions.e: In 'one of the women who sell…', 'who' refers to the plural 'women', so it takes 'sell'. The main subject 'one' is singular, so it takes 'has'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
One of the women who ...... in the premises ...... been ordered to quit?

questions.e: Adverb-modified adjectives come before the noun modifier: 'more rapid' describes 'economic growth'. That gives 'more rapid economic growth'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The new trade agreement should facilitate ....... ?

questions.e: One is 'pleased with' someone's effort or work.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The principal said that he was pleased ...... my effort?

questions.e: Everyone leaving happened before Obi's past state ('still sat'), so the past perfect 'had left' is needed.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Long after everyone ....... the hall, Obi still sat inside?

questions.e: To 'sight' something is to see it, especially at a distance. 'Sited' means located, and 'cited' means quoted.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
When we looked up, we ...... the plane some miles away?

questions.e: 'Babies'' is the plural possessive, the dresses belonging to the babies. The apostrophe goes after the plural 's'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
They are the ...... dresses.

questions.e: 'Information' is uncountable and fits 'vital information'. The fixed phrase for passing news orally is 'by word of mouth'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Vital ...... is still spread ..... word of mouth in most villages in Africa?

questions.e: A 'legacy' is something handed down from the past. Western education is one of the legacies of colonial rule, and the plural fits 'one of the'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Western education is one of the ...... colonial rule.

questions.e: The son's confession cleared the others of blame, so they were 'exonerated'. 'Implicated' is the opposite.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The man was happy that his son confessed his guilt and so the others were .......?

questions.e: To 'proscribe' is to officially forbid or ban, which fits child trafficking. 'Prescribe' (recommend or order) is a sound-alike trap.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The federal Government has ....... child trafficking?

questions.e: The fixed expression is 'have no alternative but to', meaning have no other choice.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Based on the facts before me, I have no alternative ....... to hold you responsible?

questions.e: To 'circumvent' the law is to find a way around it. 'Circumspect' is an adjective meaning cautious.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Many people would always find reasons to ....... the law?

questions.e: The simple past fits a narrative of past events: 'When his tyre burst…'. 'Burst' doesn't change in the past, and 'bursted' is wrong.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
When his car tyre ......... on the way, he did not know what to do.

questions.e: 'Used to work' describes a past habit or state that no longer happens, contrasting with 'now he is a driver'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Lami's father ........ as a gardener when he was young, but now he is a driver.

questions.e: 'Whenever' means every time. Each time he switches on the light, the shadow disappears.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
........ he switches on the light, the shadow disappears?

questions.e: To 'ferret about' means to search around busily, which aroused suspicion. 'Ferret' adds -ed without doubling the 't'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The policemen became suspicious as the hoodlums ......in their office?

questions.e: A 'fortnight' is two weeks, from 'fourteen nights'. It is spelt 'fortnight'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
It is important that you clear the refuse in front of your house every ........?

questions.e: 'Needn't' is a modal here, so the tag repeats 'need' in positive form: 'need she?'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Suara needn't come with us, .......?

questions.e: To 'scour' a place is to search it thoroughly. 'Scourged' means whipped, and 'scouted' means explored.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Unoka .... the whole house to find his missing wristwatch.

questions.e: An embedded (reported) question uses statement word order, and the tense shifts back after 'asked': 'what time it was'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Ife asked me ....... ?
o: what is it by my time

questions.e: 'Eclectic' means drawing on a variety of methods or sources, which fits 'many ways to kill a rat'. It is spelt e-c-l-e-c-t-i-c.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
There are many ways to kill a rat, so we should be..... in our approach to the task ahead of
us?

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'in furtherance of', meaning to help advance something.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Audu took these actions purely ...... his own career?

questions.e: The correct spelling is 'pronunciation', with no 'o' after the first 'n', unlike the verb 'pronounce'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Here is Mr. Odumusu who teaches English ....... in our school?

questions.e: 'Instead of' is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund. The subject is understood: 'Instead of pleading, she lied.'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Instead of ......., she lied?

questions.e: Comparing three or more people requires the superlative: 'the naughtiest'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Of the three girls, Uka is the ........?

questions.e: To 'make up for' something is to compensate for it. Here that means catching up on lessons missed during the long absence.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I wonder how he will ......being absent from school for a long time.

questions.e: A 'carrier' is the rack on a bicycle or motorcycle where a passenger can sit. 'Career' means profession.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Please sit on the ....... ?

questions.e: To 'seize' a chance is to take it eagerly. 'Seize' is spelt with 'ei'. 'Cease' means stop.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
I want to .......this chance to acquaint you the latest development?

questions.e: An 'uphill' task is difficult and needs a lot of effort, like climbing a hill.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Getting a well paid job nowadays is an ...... task?

questions.e: To 'meddle in' someone's affairs means to interfere in matters that do not concern you; 'spy from', 'toy at' and 'complain into' are not correct English collocations.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The secretary has no right to ....... my affairs?

questions.e: 'Studiously avoided' means deliberately avoided, and what Bola dodged was answering the questions; 'parrying' already means avoiding, so it would be redundant.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Bola studiously avoided ....... the questions?

questions.e: The countable noun 'reason' needs an article, and 'a certain reason' suits a reason the speaker knows but is choosing not to reveal yet.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The school authority dismissed him for ...... but I won't tell you about it yet?

questions.e: 'Better as a singer' uses 'as' to mean 'in the role of'. 'Like' would compare him to a singer instead of describing his role.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
He was both a writer and a politician, but he was better...... a singer

questions.e: Job vacancies are made known through an 'advertisement'. 'Publicity' is general attention, and 'bulletin' would need an article.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
Vacancies in the company will be notified by...........

questions.e: The correct spelling is 'auxiliary', with 'i' before the final 'ary'. The other options are misspellings.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
He started his career as an..........teacher

questions.e: A vehicle that moves downhill with the engine off, using only momentum, 'coasts'. 'Taxied' is used for aircraft on the ground.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)\
The driver was short of petrol, so he..........down the hills with the engine switched off

questions.e: Once 'one' is the subject, the same pronoun must be kept throughout, including in the tag: 'how one behaves..., shouldn't one?'
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
One should be careful how......behaves in public, shouldn't.......

questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'first and foremost', meaning most importantly. The other options misspell 'foremost'.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
...........a good leader must have two characteristics

questions.e: 'About' before a number means 'approximately', so 'about three times' is correct. 'For about' and the 'like' options are not standard here.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
We visited his house...........three times

questions.e: The idiom is 'on the verge of', meaning very close to. Other prepositions are not used with 'verge' this way.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
She was............the verge of tears

questions.e: 'Infallible' means incapable of making mistakes. Since everyone errs, nobody is infallible. 'Imperfect' would contradict the meaning.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
Everyone makes mistakes occasionally, nobody is.........

questions.e: Adjectives usually follow the order opinion or state, then colour, then material: 'discarded black earthen pot'.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
The woman would not part with her..........pot

questions.e: A positive statement in the past simple takes a negative tag with 'did': 'We stood up..., didn't we?'
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
We stood up when the principal came in..........?

questions.e: The correct spellings are 'veterinary' and 'unravelled', with British English doubling the 'l'.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
This professor of...........medicine has......... the mystery of bird flu.

questions.e: 'Clothes' means garments to wear and fits 'some clothes'. 'Cloth' is fabric, and 'clothing' is uncountable and less natural here.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
Her mother brought her some.......

questions.e: Workers who lose their jobs because there is no work are 'laid off'. 'Laid up' means ill in bed, and 'laid out' means arranged.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
Many workers were............ as a result of the textile closure

questions.e: A 'fatal' accident is one that causes death, which matches 'the driver died'.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
The driver died in the .......... road accident

questions.e: 'Since' gives the reason, meaning 'because' or 'as', and one 'frowns at' or 'frowns upon' something one disapproves of. 'Although' would give the wrong logic.
questions.s: _______your parents frown _______our friendship, we shouldn't see each other anymore

questions.e: 'Though' introduces a contrast: she married him in spite of not trusting him. 'Since' would wrongly suggest a reason.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
...........she didn't trust him, she married him.

questions.e: In reported speech the question becomes a statement in the past tense, and the plural 'beliefs' needs 'they': 'what they were'.
questions.s:
Answer the following question below and choose the option that best completes the gap(s)
I wanted to know his political beliefs, so l asked him what........

questions.e: 'Averse' is always followed by 'to', as in 'averse to risk', meaning opposed to or disliking something.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
The girl says she is averse.....what others admire

questions.e: The correct spelling is 'onomatopoeia', with 'oeia' at the end. It means a word that imitates a sound.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Our teacher defined ......in his introductory lesson

questions.e: 'Devote oneself to' takes a gerund after 'to', so it is 'devoted himself to helping the poor'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
The philanthropist devoted himself......the poor

questions.e: 'But' links two contrasting ideas: liking apples and not liking oranges.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Tinu likes apples......she does not like oranges

questions.e: A ceremonial parade is a 'march past'. 'Pass' and 'match' are wrong spellings for this phrase.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
The students had a .....On Independence Day.

questions.e: 'Mind' is followed by the gerund (-ing form), so 'Do you mind waiting...?' is correct.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Do you mind......another hour or two?

questions.e: Soil that is completely soaked with water is 'saturated'. 'Satiated' means having eaten enough.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
The continuous rain has really .......the soil.

questions.e: 'Out of hand' means out of control, which suits how police would describe an unruly boy.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
The police described the boy as being.....hand

questions.e: A government formed by two or more parties together is a 'coalition' government. 'Collusion' is a secret, dishonest agreement.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
It was very easy for the two political parties to form a .......Government

questions.e: 'Encourage' is followed by an object and a to-infinitive: 'encouraged to carry out'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
All farmers were encouraged ......carry out fumigation on their farms

questions.e: The compound adjective 'fast moving' comes before the noun phrase 'luxury buses' in natural English order.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
There are lots of.....in a park

questions.e: The possessive pronoun that stands alone is 'theirs', written without an apostrophe, matching 'yours'.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Yours is to command.....is to obey

questions.e: Local laws made by councils are 'bye-laws' or 'by-laws'. The plural fits 'pass', and 'bye laws' is the only acceptable plural form among the options.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Local governments are authorized to pass

questions.e: To agree with a negative statement we use 'neither' with inversion: 'Neither have I.'
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Umar: I have never visted the dentist
Aliyu: ......?

questions.e: A third conditional, 'would have won', pairs with the past perfect 'if he had run fast' to describe an unreal past situation.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Usman would have won the race.....
o: only if he could run fast

questions.e: In 'from whoever offers it', the pronoun is the subject of 'offers', so the subject form 'whoever' is correct, with a singular verb.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
My father told me to take the money from .....it

questions.e: 'Matricide' is the killing of one's mother, from Latin 'mater', mother. 'Patricide' is the killing of one's father.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
Our teacher defined.......as the killing of one's mother

questions.e: We are confused 'about' something we do not understand. 'Confused with' means mistaking one thing for another.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best complete the gap (s)
