**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
Fierce dogs should be kept in the _______ during the day.

questions.e: After "a friend of", the possessive pronoun "ours" is used, and possessive pronouns take no apostrophe.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
We have known Rose for some years now, she is a friend of ____

questions.e: "Comprise" means "consist of", so it takes no "of"; the present tense "comprises" suits a committee that still exists.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
The new national security committee ____ retired military personnel.

questions.e: "Ran out of fuel" is the full phrasal verb, and since "of fuel" already follows the gap, only "ran out" is needed.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
His car ____ of fuel so he arrived late for the meeting.

questions.e: To "look up" a word is to search for it in a reference book such as a thesaurus or dictionary.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best complete(s) the gap.**
________ the word in the Thesaurus!

questions.e: "On time" means punctually, at the expected time; "in time" means early enough.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
Ade was told to finish the assignment ____ time.

questions.e: A particular, named city is introduced with the definite article: "The city of Abuja".
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best completes the gap(s)**
_________ is expanding rapidly.

questions.e: Colleagues called Mr Bepo "The Lekki Headmaster" because he humorously copied characters from the old TV drama Village Headmaster.
questions.s: The principal was nicknamed "The Lekki Headmaster" because...
o: He lived in Lekki during his time as a headmaster.
He humorously imitated characters from the Village Headmaster.
He introduced a new curriculum in the school.

questions.e: Calling the washing of corpses "cleaning dishes" replaces an unpleasant idea with a milder one, which is a euphemism.
questions.s:
What figure of speech is used in the expression "...wouldn't have to clean 'dishes', as folks
uncharitably say about washing corpses."

questions.e: "Foot-dragging" means deliberate delay or reluctance to act, here his slowness to decide on relocating.
questions.s:
“...his foot-dragging over the matter had pushed his marriage to the brink.” What does
"foot-dragging" mean as used in the novel?

questions.e: A passport officer told Bepo this after he paid extra to speed up his renewal: without paying he would still be queuing.
questions.s:
This question is based on Kabir Garba's The Lekki Headmaster
"Yes....That is what you paid the extra amount for. If you had followed the normal channel,
you would still be there with them."
To whom was this said?

questions.e: A prefect aspirant at Stardom must have spent at least two sessions in the school.
questions.s:
This question is based on Kabir Garba's The Lekki Headmaster
The contestant for the position of a prefect must have spent ... in the school.

questions.e: "No sooner" is always paired with "than": "No sooner had he left than...".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
No sooner had Tobi left the house _____ it began to rain.

questions.e: The fixed proverb is "What goes around comes around"; the singular subject "what" takes "comes".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
What goes around _____ around.

questions.e: "For about thirty minutes" shows an action that began earlier and is still going on, so the present perfect continuous "has been playing" fits.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The boy _____ the flute for about thirty minutes.

questions.e: "Each" is the singular subject, so it takes the singular verb "is", even though "answers" is plural.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Each of the answers ______ correct.

questions.e: "Each" is singular, so the auxiliary must be "has": "Each of the reports has been reviewed".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Each of the reports ______ been carefully reviewed by the committee

questions.e: "Incidence" means the rate of occurrence, which can increase; an "incident" is a single event.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The ____ of armed robbery has been on the increase.

questions.e: The past tense of the verb "advise" is "advised"; "advice" is the noun and "adviced" is not a word.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The doctor ____ him to take his medicine regularly.

questions.e: The correct spelling is "laudable", meaning praiseworthy, from the Latin for praise.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He was praised for the ______ achievement.

questions.e: "It is high time" + subject is followed by the past simple: "It is high time you stopped...".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
It is high time you _____ visiting that friend of yours.

questions.e: Adjectives follow the order opinion/quality, age, colour, purpose: "shiny new red lunch pack".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Put Chioma's meat in _____ pack.

questions.e: Comparatives like "better" are intensified with "far" (or "much"), not "very" or "too".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
As trained teachers, Joke teaches _______ better than Jumoke.

questions.e: The instruction concerns a future deadline, so "next week" is correct; "last week" is already past.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
The teacher asked the students to submit their assignments before the end of ____ week

questions.e: A third conditional (if + past perfect) takes "would have + past participle" in the main clause: "would have scored".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
If I had worked hard, I _______ very high marks in the exam.

questions.e: The tag repeats the auxiliary of the main clause in negative form; "had been" gives "hadn't it?"
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
It had been raining before the party started, _____

questions.e: The collective noun for sheep is a "flock"; "herd" is used for cattle.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
That Fulani man has a large _____ of sheep.

questions.e: A sailor away at sea is missed, so she is "longing for" him, i.e. yearning for his return.
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
She is ______ a sailor who is away at sea.

questions.e: "Scarcely" at the start inverts subject and auxiliary, and pairs with a past-perfect clause: "Scarcely had she entered when...".
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
Scarcely ______ she entered the room when the phone rang.

questions.e: "Presented" is past simple with no auxiliary, so the tag uses "did" in the negative: "didn't he?"
questions.s:
In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).
He presented a masterpiece at the conference, ___________

questions.e: The director fires questions at Bepo not to get answers but to rebuke him, so these are rhetorical questions.
questions.s:
**This question is based on Kabir Garba's The Lekki Headmaster**
'You again...Mr. Bepo? What business brings you out at this hour? Is this the students'
hostel you are supposed to be minding?'
**What figure of speech is used in the clauses?**

questions.e: The natural collocation for crying from deep pain or sorrow is to cry "bitterly"; "profusely" goes with sweating or bleeding.
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).**
The little girl cried....

questions.e: "Next" points to the future, so the noun clause subject should be "What will happen next".
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the best option that completes the gap(s).**
... is still unknown.

questions.e: The "as ... as" comparison takes the plain form of the adjective: "twice as big as mine".
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the best option that completes the gap(s).**
Her car is twice as... as mine.

questions.e: To have "a knack for" something is to have a special skill or tendency for it; "addiction" and "habit" take "to" or "of".
questions.s:
**In each of the following questions, select the option that best completes the**
**gap(s).**
Some candidates have ... for cheating in examinations.

questions.e: The tag repeats the modal from the main clause with reversed polarity: "couldn't have said" gives "could she?"
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).**
Mary couldn't have said a thing like that, ...

questions.e: An infinitive phrase as subject is singular, so it takes the singular active verb "calls for".
questions.s:
**In each of the following questions, select the option that best completes the**
**gap(s).**
To be alive after such a serious accident ... a celebration.

questions.e: Adjectives go in the order opinion, physical quality, age: "beautiful strong young lady".
questions.s:
**For this question, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).**
The ... lady is here.

questions.e: In a third conditional, the main clause uses "would(n't) have + past participle": "wouldn't have given".
questions.s:
**In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the**
**gap(s).**
If he had known, he wouldn't ... him her only copy of the book.

questions.e: A third conditional ('had not arrived ... would have starved') describes the opposite of what happened: the father did arrive, so the speaker did not starve.
questions.s: If my father had not arrived, I would have starved. This sentence means
o: My father did arrive and I didn't starve
I had to starve because my father didn't come
my father didn't arrive and I didn't starve
I should have starved but I didn't
I had starved before my father arrived

questions.e: An 'open secret' is supposedly secret information that is in fact widely known.
questions.s:
In the question below which of the following options express the **same idea** as the one in
quotes?:
'An open secret' means
o: a fact that is very secret
a secret told in the open air

questions.e: 'Witch-hunting' means unfairly persecuting people, and 'character assassination' means maliciously damaging someone's reputation.
questions.s:
After each of the following sentences, a list of possible interpretations is given. Choose the
interpretation that you consider the **most** **appropriate** for each sentence.
Employees have been urged to desist from witch-hunting and character assassination
o: entreated not to accuse individuals unjustly and malicious
informed to resist witch-hunters and character assassins
urged to desist from barbaric acts

questions.e: 'A means of' + gerund is the correct pattern: a means of improving.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word or phrase which **best fills the gap** in each sentence:
The dull students took correspondence course as a means .... his standard in the class

questions.e: The subject is 'knowledge', which is singular; 'as well as idioms and lexical items' does not make it plural. So 'is tested'.
questions.s:
In the question below choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which **best fill(s)** the gap:
Knowledge of figures of speech as well as idioms and lexical items .... in this section

questions.e: Here 'may not' expresses prohibition (not allowed), not possibility, so people are forbidden to pick flowers.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option (A-D) that best explains the information conveyed in
the sentence:
People may not pick flowers in this park.
o: people can pick flowers in this park
people may not wish to pick flowers in this park
people are prohibited from picking flowers from this park
people cannot pick flowers from this park

questions.e: 'Ought not to have told' criticises a past action that actually happened, so Tom told me but should not have.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option (A-D) that best explains the information conveyed in
the sentence:
Tom ought not to have told me
o: Tom did not tell me but he should
Perhaps Tom was wrong to have told me
Tom told me but it was wrong of him
It was necessary for Tom not to tell me

questions.e: 'Can't be swimming' expresses the speaker's strong belief that something is not happening, so it is likely he is not swimming now. It is not about ability.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option (A-D) that best explains the information conveyed in
the sentence:
He can't be swimming all day
o: it's possible he is not swimming now
It's very likely he is swimming now
He does not have the ability to swim all day
He would not like to swim all day

questions.e: 'Would make a mess of' here predicts an undesirable outcome, so Bolade will not cook the rice well.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option (A-D) that best explains the information conveyed in
the sentence:
Bolade would make a mess of cooking the rice.
o: it was typical of Bolade to make a mess of things
Bolade will not cook rice the rice well
Bolade does not like cooking rice

questions.e: 'If I were the captain' signals an unreal situation: I was not the captain, and so I did not lead the team to victory.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option (A-D) that best explains the information conveyed in
the sentence:
If i were the captain, i would have led the team to victory
o: I was not the captain but i led the tam to victory
I was the captain but i did not lead the team to victory
I was not the captain and i did not lead the team to victory
i was the captain and i led the team to victory

questions.e: 'Outlived its usefulness' means it is no longer useful. 'Between you and me' only signals that the opinion is confidential, so A captures the information.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
Between you and me, i would say the equipment has outlived its usefulness
o: I believe that the equipment is no longer useful to any of us
I believe that the equipment continues to be useful to either you or me
My idea of the usefulness of the equipment should remain known only to the two of us
My idea of the usefulness of the equipment is shared by both

questions.e: 'Wished he had started' expresses regret about a past event that did not happen, so Emeka regrets not starting school early.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
Emeka wished he had started school early
o: Emeka started school early as he wished
Emeka regretted not starting school early
Emeka could have started school early if he had wished

questions.e: Being 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' means facing two equally bad choices, i.e. being in a dilemma.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
He was between the devil and the deep blue sea
o: He stood between the devil and the sea

questions.e: Read as a defining clause, 'the boys who rioted' identifies only those boys who rioted, so only some boys rioted and those were suspended.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
The boys who rioted, were suspended by the principal
o: Only some of the boys rioted and they were suspended
All the boys rioted and were suspended
Many boys rioted and were suspended
A few boys rioted and were suspended

questions.e: 'Whoever would have thought' expresses surprise at an unexpected outcome, so people generally believed he would win.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
Whoever would have thought that he would lose the presidential election?
o: Everyone believed that he would lose the election,
It was commonly believed that he would win the election
He was supposed to lose the election
No one believed that he would win the election

questions.e: 'Wonderful' here expresses delight, so the news is very pleasing. It does not mean it caused wonder or was a miracle.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
It's wonderful that Musa is already out of hospital
o: The fact that Musa is out of hospital cause great wonder
The fact that Musa is out of hospital is a miracle
It is surprising that Musa is out of hospital
It is very pleasing that Musa is out of hospital

questions.e: 'Had Aminu been a dull student' is an inverted unreal condition; in reality he was not dull, so his failure surprised everyone.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence:
Had Aminu been a dull student, his failure wouldn't have surprised anybody
o: Aminu failed and it surprised everybody since he was dull
Aminu was not a dull student and so everybody was surprised that he failed
Because Aminu was a dull, student, everybody was surprised that he failed
Aminu had been a dull student, and so nobody was surprised that he failed

questions.e: To 'cross the bridge when one gets to it' means to deal with a problem only when it actually arises, i.e. decide at the appropriate time.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
The president of club said that he would cross the bridge on getting there
o: He was waiting for an opportunity to take a decision
When he got to the river he would build a bridge across it
He would take a decision at the appropriate time
When he got to the river he would cross at the bridge

questions.e: A 'death-blow' is something that ends or destroys a plan completely; his refusal to help caused the plans to fail.
questions.s:
In the question below select the option that best explains the information conveyed in **the**
**sentence**:
His refusal to help us, dealt a death-blow to our plans
o: because he did not help, our plans did not materialize
He helped and our plans materialized
He blew our plans to pieces
He supported our plans so it worked

questions.e: Without commas, 'the tailor' is a defining phrase that tells us which Mr Pam is meant, implying there are other people called Mr Pam. It says nothing about other tailors. The correct option is B.
questions.s:
In the question below, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence:
Here is Mr Pam the tailor
o: He is the only person known as Mr Pam, and he is a tailor
He is one of those known as Mr Pam, and he is a tailor
He is the only tailor, and he is Mr Pam
He is one of many tailors, and he is Mr Pam

questions.e: "Most of the time" means frequently, and a "menace" is a threat or danger, so their presence is frequently a threat. "Seldom a bother" reverses the meaning.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Most of the time, their presence is a menace?
o: Their presence is seldom a bother
Their presence is ussually of great concern
Their presence is frequently a threat

questions.e: The commas make "who is in the U.S.A." a non-defining clause, but the comparable reading in the key is that this is one of the speaker's sons, identified by being in the U.S.A., studying Engineering.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
My son, who is in the U.S.A., is studying Engineering.
o: My only son in the U.S.A is studying Engineering
One of my sons is in the U.S.A studying Engineering
My sons are in the U.S.A but only one is studying Engineering
My only son is in the U.S.A studying Engineering

questions.e: The proverb means that God's justice may seem slow, but it is thorough and complete, so every wrong is eventually dealt with in full.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The mills of God grind slowly, but they grind exceedingly small
o: God has a mill where every material in life is thoroughly ground
God may seem slow in action, but he adequately rewards every bit of injustice
The world is like a food factory where God take his time in grinding all raw materials properly
Even though God is never in a hurry, He achieves al things

questions.e: To "believe in" programmes is to accept and support them, so the speaker was among those who embraced them, not someone who created or rejected them.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
I was one of those who actively believe in his development programmes?
o: I was part of those who renounced the programmes
I was the originator of the programmes
I was one of the people who embraced the programmes
I was one of the great number who developed his programmes actively

questions.e: Not being interested in who rules means being indifferent about the rulers. The other options confuse the people with the rulers.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
People are not interested in who rules?
o: People who rules are not interested in the rule
The rulers are not indifferent about the people
People are indifferent about the rulers
People are ruled by the people they are interest in

questions.e: "Couldn't have attended" expresses the speaker's certainty that something did not happen, so it was impossible that Imona attended.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Imona couldn't have attended lectures yesterday
o: it was impossible that Imona attended lectures yesterday
It was possible that Imona didn't attend lectures yesterday
It was possible that Imona attended lectures yesterday
It was impossible that Imona didn't attend lectures yesterday

questions.e: A capacity crowd means the stadium was full. "In spite of the weather" means the people came despite bad weather, so the crowd defied the weather.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The stadium had a capacity crowd in spite of the weather?
o: The weather favoured the crowd at the stadium
The crowd defied the weather to fill the stadium
The stadium was not filled because of the weather
The crowd loved the weather at the stadium

questions.e: "Biennial" means happening once every two years, i.e. every other year. "Biannual" means twice a year.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The conference is biennial?
o: The conference is held twice every year
The conference is held twice in two years
The conference is held once every other year
The conference lasts for two years

questions.e: To "survive" a cabinet reshuffle means to keep one's post, so if only two survived, all the other ministers were removed.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Only two ministers survived the recent cabinet reshuffle?
o: In the recent changes in government, only two ministers were sacked
In the recent changes in government, all but two ministers remained alive
In recent changes in government, all but two ministers retained their posts
In recent changes in government, all but two ministers were sacked

questions.e: The second conditional ("If I left..., I would...") describes a hypothetical situation: if he left the country, his family would join him.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If I left the country, I would arrange for my family to join me?
o: He left the country and his family joined him
In the event of his leaving the country, his family would join him
He did not leave the country and his family did not join him
He may not leave the country

questions.e: "Mutual" hatred means each village hated the other, so they hated each other. "Themselves" would mean each hated itself.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
A state of mutual hatred existed for years between the two villages of Umunna and
Ogboma?
o: Umunna and Ogboma hated each other

questions.e: "Faked" means made as a false copy, and "beautifully" shows it was done well, so it was a skilful, deceptive replica.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The painting in the museum was beautifully faked?
o: The painting was a good deceptive replica
The painting was well-framed and displayed
The painting was deceptively decorated in the museum
The painting was carefully hung in the museum

questions.e: "Do you mind...?" asks if there is an objection, and "Yes, I do" means "I do mind", so Bola is clearly refusing the request.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Ade: Do you mind if i sit down here?
Bola: Well, yes I do actually.
o: Bola is reluctantly granting the request
Bola is willingly accepting the request
Bola is certainly rejecting the request
Bola is objecting to the request

questions.e: To "hold forth" is to talk at length on a subject, so the president gave a long speech on patriotism.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The president held forth for several minutes on the need for patriotism?
o: The president was silent for some minutes when patriotism was being discussd
The president whispered a few things about patriotism
The president spent time saying a few things about patriots
The president gave a rather long speech on the importance of patriotism

questions.e: A "slide" in price is a fall, and "reeling" means staggering or shaken, so the falling price is destabilising the industry.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The slide in the price of gold in the world market has left the industry reeling?
o: The gradual fall in gold price is making the industry unstable
The stablity in gold price is making the industry stagnant
The decline in gold price is making the industry redundant
The increase in gold price is making the industry to boom

questions.e: "Fabricated" means invented or made up, so publishing made-up untruths as facts is a misuse of press freedom.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Fabricated statements published as truths amount to an abuse of press freedom?
o: To make known what is not true is aggressive to press
Publishing formulated untruths is misused press freedom
Unplanned publicized untruths are a misuse of the freedom of the press
Press freedom is based on ,published untruths

questions.e: "At the eleventh hour" is an idiom meaning at the last possible moment.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The expected guests arrived at the eleventh hour?
o: The guest arrived at the last minute
The guest arrived at the expected time
The guests arrived at the eleven hours behind schedule

questions.e: In law, to "rest one's case" means to finish presenting one's arguments, so the counsel concluded her defence.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
After addressing the court for two hours, the defence counsel rested her case?
o: The defence counsel's was tried after speaking for two hours, so she took a break
The judge adjourned the defence counsel's case after listening for two hours
The defence counsel concluded her defence after speaking for two hours
The judge advised the defence counsel to rest after two hours of address

questions.e: Benjamin's statement shows he trusts Napoleon completely and believes whatever Napoleon says must be correct.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Benjamin exclaimed, 'If it is Napoleon who said it, it must be right'
o: Benjamin never believes what Napoleon says
Benjamin does not know what is right unless Napoleon says it
Napoleon always says what Benjamin believes to be right
Benjamin thinks that Napoleon always says the right thing

questions.e: "The last word in" something is an idiom for the best or most modern example of it, so the loaf was the best ever baked.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The manager said that the new loaf was the last word in bakery?
o: The loaf was the best ever baked
The loaf was the last to be baked
The loaf was the worst to have been baked
The loaf was the last in the baker's directory

questions.e: The reformists believe free and fair elections are impossible without constitutional changes, so such elections depend on legal reforms.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The reformists say elections cannot be free and fair unless a number of constitutional
changes are effected?
o: Free and fair elections deend on law reforms
free and fair and elections are the primary concerne of the reformists
Effecting consitutional changes is dependent on electoral reforms

questions.e: To "go under the hammer" means to be sold at auction, so many used items will be auctioned this weekend.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
Hundreds of used items will go under the hammer during the weekend?
o: Unserviceable goods will be publicly destroyed at the weekend
Impounded household items will be sold to the public before the weekend
Damage items will be sold next weekend
Many old items will be auctioned this weekend

questions.e: Although the overall picture (horizon) is unclear, the trouble spots have been identified, so the troubled spots are more clearly seen than the whole horizon.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The horizon may not be clear now, but the troubled spots have certainly been noted?
o: The horizon is dependent on the troubled spots
Clarity of the horizon is dependent on the perception of the troubled spots
The troubled spots are more perceptible than the horizon
Horizon, clarity of the troubled spots and clarity are remarkably noted

questions.e: "Intimidating" means frightening or making people feel nervous, so the crowd is frightening.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The crowd in the hall is intimidating?

questions.e: "If he were here" is an unreal condition: he is not present, so the occasion is less fun than it would be with him.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If he were here, it could be more fun.
o: He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun
He was being expected to supply more fun
There was not fun because he was not present
He was expected but did not show up to liven up the occasion

questions.e: A "jaundiced" view is negative, biased or unfavourable, often due to bitterness, so he takes an unfavourable position on their problems.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Though he is our elected representative he often takes a rather jaundiced view of our
problems.
o: He takes a rather hazy view of our problems
He takes an unfavourable position concerning our problems
He takes a rather forceful view of our problems
He takes a sickly view of our problems

questions.e: "Only" placed before "gave him a congratulatory card" limits what was given: all I gave James on that visit was a card.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
When I visited James I only gave him a congratulatory card on account of his promotion.
o: The only person I visited was James and nobody else
It was only James that I gave a congratulatory card to
All I gave James when I visited him was a congratulatory card
All I did when I visited James was given him a congratulatory card

questions.e: "No love lost between" two people is an idiom meaning they dislike each other.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The events of last Friday show that there is no love lost between the principal and the Vice-
Principal.

questions.e: "Inflammatory" remarks are provocative, intended to arouse anger or strong feelings, which is why they drew criticism.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The politician's inflammatory remarks were heavily criticised.
o: The politican's rude remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's provocative remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's bombastic remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's tribalistic remarks were heavily criticised

questions.e: An "idiosyncrasy" is a personal peculiarity; "chief" means main here, not a title. A "passion" for pounded yam is a penchant (strong liking) for it.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. 
Oche's chief idiosyncrasy is a passion for pounded yam.
o: Oche has a penchant for pounded yam

questions.e: "Must not" expresses prohibition: it is necessary that you do not attend. "Not necessary" would be "needn't" or "don't have to".
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. 
You must not attend the end-of-year party.
o: It is not necessary that you attend the party
It is necessary that you do not attend the party
You do not have to decide whether to attend the party or not
You have to decide whether to attend the party or not

questions.e: "Sycophancy" is excessive flattery to win favour, so a limit to it means people should know when to stop flattering.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. 
The man reasoned that there ought to be a limit to sycophancy.
o: there can be no favour beyond a reasonable point
sycophants need not talk all the time
people should know when not to use flattery
sycophants should know when to grant people's requests

questions.e: An "imp" is a mischievous or badly behaved child, like a small devil, so Adawo behaves badly.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. 
Adawo is an imp.

questions.e: If all the alternatives are negative, the solution must be one of those negative options, the least bad choice.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. 
The solution lies in choosing between various negative alternatives.
o: the solution can be found in one of negative options
the solution lies in choosing between the positive and the negative
the solution is a negative one

questions.e: "In a state of flux" means continually changing, so the organisation undergoes periodic changes.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The organization is constantly in a state of flux?
o: There are perodic changes in the organization
The organization is facing a difficult period
The organization is experiencing good times

questions.e: A "meteoric" rise is very rapid and dazzling, like a meteor, and it surprised people, so they were amazed at his rapid success.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
His meteoric rise to fame surprise everyone?
o: His rise to fame was only temporary
People were amazed at his rapid success
He rose to the top quite unexpectedly

questions.e: To be "pilloried" is to be publicly attacked and held up to ridicule, as people once were in the pillory.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
The politician was pilloried by the press for his inflammatory remarks?
o: The politician was snubbed by the press for his remarks
The politician was criticized by the press for his remarks
The politician was closely questioned by the press for his remarks
The politician was ridiculed by the press for his remarks

questions.e: "By leaps and bounds" means very quickly and in large amounts, so he got well very rapidly.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
After the successful operation, he recovered by leaps and bounds?
o: His well-bound wounds aided his recovery
He did a lot of keep-fit exercises

questions.e: "Taken bad" (or "taken ill") is an informal idiom meaning suddenly became sick.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explain the information conveyed in the sentence.
Audu was taken bad in the middle of the night?

questions.e: The second conditional describes something unreal or unlikely. In the key's reading, he did not go to London and so did not see the Queen.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If he went to London, he would see the Queen?
o: He did not go to London and did not see the Queen
He would like to see the Queen when he goes to London
When he goes to London he will see the Queen
He did not see the Queen when he went to London

questions.e: "Impassioned" means filled with strong feeling, so her father is an emotional man.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Ngozi has always considered her father to be an impassioned man?
o: Her father is a very strict man
Her father is a very lively man
Her father is an emotional man
Her father is a disciplined man

questions.e: "Hard currency" is money from a strong economy that is stable in value and widely accepted.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The manager paid us in hard currency?
o: We were paid in a strong and stable currency
We were paid in dollars and pound sterling
We were paid in new notes

questions.e: To "take issue with" someone is to disagree or argue with them, and "rebuked" means reprimanded.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The elders rebuked Olu for taking issue with his principal?
o: Olu was scolded for acting in collusion principal
Olu was reprimanded for arguing with his principal
Olu was blamed for issuing a statement denying his principal
Olu was cautioned for shouting at his principal

questions.e: To "throw one's weight around" is to behave arrogantly and use power unpleasantly; "humble beginning" means a simple background.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
In spite of his humble beginning, Audu now throws his weight around?
o: His noble brith notwithstanding, Audu is a corrupt man
From his poor background, Audu is now a rich man
Despite his obvious poverty, Audu is a proud man
Audu is arrogant despite his simple upbringing

questions.e: To 'play the devil's advocate' is to argue for an unpopular or opposing view just to provoke discussion, not because you believe it.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Everyone was ready to play the devil's advocate in the impeachment to encourage
discussion on it.
o: everyone was willing to speak against the impeachment to encourage discussion on it
everyone was willing to defend an unpopular point of view concerning the impeachment
everyone was willing to fight for the defenceless citizens no matter the consequences
everyone was willing to be an evil genius in the controversy

questions.e: A 'key figure' is a person whose role is central and essential. 'Figurehead' means the opposite: someone with a title but no real power.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Adamu's father is a key figure in that ministry
o: The ministry trusts Adamu's fatheras a central figure
Adamu's father as a figurehead in the ministry
Adamu's father's position is essential in the ministry
Adamu's father keeps the key to the minstry

questions.e: 'Drink-driving' means driving after drinking alcohol, or driving while drunk, and the law treats it as an offence. Option C is ungrammatical ('drunking').
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The government warns that drink-driving is punishable under the law?
o: a drunkard driving can be punished
driving while drunk is an offence
driving while drunking can be punished
drinking and driving is an offence

questions.e: 'Ostensibly' means apparently, or seemingly on the surface, possibly not in reality. So democracy is only apparently practised.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
In many countries, democracy is ostensibly being practiced?
o: democracy is indeed being inmany countries
many countries have democracy in practice
democracy is apparently practiced in many countries

questions.e: To 'reach a dead end' means no further progress is possible. The investigation into the suspects had stalled.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The investigators stated clearly that they had reached a dead end in their scrutiny of
suspects in the murder case?
o: the investigator did not know what to do with the suspects' murder
the investigators had evidence to sentence the suspects to death in the end
There was no further progress inthe investigation of the murder suspects
the end had come for the suspects in the murder case

questions.e: This third conditional describes an unreal past. In reality the rain did fall, and so the match was missed.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If the rain hadn't fallen, we wouldn't have missed the match?
o: The rain is falling, so we will miss the match
The rain fell, so we didn't watch the match
The rain didn't fall, so we didn't watch the match
The rain didn't fall, so we didn't miss the match

questions.e: 'Jawing away' is slang for talking non-stop, so the boy talked continuously in class.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The class was tired of the new boy jawing away all the time?
o: He was always chewing in the class
He was always making trouble for the class
He talked continuously in the class

questions.e: To 'pull together' means to work together and cooperate towards a common goal.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The new Headmaster hoped that his men would pull together?
o: He expected that the men would cooperate with him
He thought that the men would compose themselves at work
He was certain that they would resign en masse
He was certain that their condition would improve under him

questions.e: 'Pruned down' means reduced. The trader who paid in full did not have his order cut.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If the trader paid in full, his order was not pruned down.
o: The trader who made full payment did not have his order reduced
The trader who made some payment did not have his order delayed
Unless the trader paid in full his order would be rejected
As the trader did not increase his order, he did not need to pay in full

questions.e: A 'pawn' is someone used by others for their own ends. Saying the men were not pawns means they acted on their own idea.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The men were not pawns in someone else's political game.
o: The action they executed was their idea
The men used someone else's plan
They were used by someone's political game

questions.e: 'As suddenly as it began' means it ended just as abruptly, so it stopped almost immediately.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The crisis ended as suddenly as it began?
o: The crisis will not end suddenly

questions.e: Saying you won't complain about a 'lack of excitement' means the job has plenty of it, so the job is exciting.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
One thing I will not be complaining about in my new job is a lack of excitement?
o: The job is not too exciting
The job has been previously done

questions.e: To 'parry' questions is to skilfully avoid answering them directly, so the Governor evaded them.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The Governor parried all the questions put to him by the journalist?
o: The governor answered all the questions brilliantly
The Governor evaded all the questions
The Governor failed all the questions
The Governor mastered all the questions

questions.e: 'If I visited … I might go' is a hypothetical condition about a possible future visit. It means that if I go to England, I could go to Manchester City.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If I visited England, I might go to Manchester City.
o: When I go to England , I could go to Manchester City
Whenever I visit England, I must go to Manchester City
I did not go to England and could not go to Manchester
I could not visit Manchester City because I did not want to go to England

questions.e: To 'put one's foot down' is to act firmly and refuse to give way, which shows firmness of character.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The man puts his foot down whenever he is convinced of his action?
o: He desires to assert his will in the situation
He makes his mark whereever he goes
His attitude demonstrates someone who likes to oppress others around him

questions.e: A 'grey area' is something unclear or not well defined, so the regulations are not very clear.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
In our college, the regulations concerning resits are grey area?
o: The regulation have just been revised
The regulations have been often ignored
The regulations are not very clear

questions.e: 'Takes after' means resembles in character, and to 'fawn upon' someone means to flatter them to win favour.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Ogiri takes after his father, he fawns upon anyone with influence.
o: Like his father, Ogiri likes to flatter people with influence in society
Like his father, Ogiri hates influential people
Ogiri, who always follows his father, tries to act an influential man
Ogiri, who looks like his father, follows rich and influential people about

questions.e: 'You are to write' expresses an instruction or order. You have been told to write a report and hand it to the security office.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
You are to write a report and give it to the security office?
o: After writing your report, give it to the security office
You are writing a report, as the security office directed
The report you are writing should be given to the security office
You have been ordered to write a report, which you will give to the security office

questions.e: 'Vindictive' means wanting revenge, so the victors carried out vengeful acts against the defeated.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
After the war, the victors became increasingly vindictive?
o: Vengeful attacks were incessantly carried out on those who lost war
Friendly measures were taken to heal the wounds
Repressive measures were taken against those who lost the war
Those who won the war became treacherous

questions.e: To 'reel off' is to recite a list quickly and without hesitation, showing accurate knowledge of the names.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The prefect reeled off the names of all the students who broke the library?
o: The prefect gave a disjointed list of the students in the law library
The prefect omitted the names of the students who broke into the law library
The prefect submitted a complete list of the students who stole library books
The prefect gave an accurate list of the students who disobeyed library regulations

questions.e: 'I owe you far less than you owe me' means both have debts, but the listener's debt is much bigger.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
I owe you far less than you owe me?
o: My debt to you is greater than yours to me
Your debt is not much greater than mine
What we owe each other is approximately the same
I owe you something, but you owe me much more

questions.e: When a matter 'comes to a head', it reaches a critical point that demands action.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The dispute over land acquisition has come to a head?
o: The problem has reached crisis proportions
The problem has been referred to the headquarters
Because of the dispute, land acquisition has now been halted
The problem has now been solved

questions.e: 'Hardly … when' means one action followed the other almost immediately, so the bell rang just after he spoke.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
He had hardly spoken when the bell rang?
o: He found it difficult to speak, and then the bell rang
When the bell rang, he was still speaking
The bell rang very soon after he spoke
He spoke in a harsh manner and the bell rang

questions.e: To 'take something for granted' is to fail to appreciate it because you are used to it. So she isn't grateful enough.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
I think she takes her guardian's support for granted?
o: Her guardian has been helping her for a long time, and she is very grateful to him
She wants her guardian to grant her more support
She thinks her guardian will no longer support her as he has been doing
Her guardian has been helping her for a long time, but she does not show enough gratitude

questions.e: To 'fall in with' plans means to agree to or accept them.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The class has fallen in with the teacher's plans?
o: The class has ignored the plans
The class has rejected the plans
The class has accepted the plans
The class has modified the plans

questions.e: 'Could not have rewarded them more handsomely' means it was impossible to reward them better, so he rewarded them very generously. 'Handsomely' here means generously.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
He could not have rewarded them more handsomely.
o: He did not reward them very well
He rewarded them well, and he was also a good looking man
He spoke to them in a very generous way

questions.e: 'Look before you leap' is a proverb advising you to think about the possible consequences before acting.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
My advice to Tolu was: Look before you leap?
o: Tolu was advised to consider her opinons before reaching any decisions
Tolu was advised to consider the possible consequences before taking action
Tolu was advised to weigh her decisions by looking and leaping
Tolu was advised to leap only after looking

questions.e: 'Allegedly' means it is claimed but not proved. People accused the official of taking bribes.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The official had allegedly been bribed?
o: Some people accused the official of taking bribes
The official had been taking bribes without feeling any guilt
It was proved that the official had been taking bribes
The official accused some people of taking bribes

questions.e: 'Hardly ever' means almost never, and to 'hold with' means to agree with. So Emeka almost never supports my view.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Emeka hardly ever holds with my view on good governance?
o: Emeka sometimes opposes my idea of good governance
My view on what good governance is conforms with that of Emeka
Emeka never really supports my opinon of good governance
Emeka may never hold a view which conflicts with mine on good governance

questions.e: 'At least 30 kilometres' sets 30 as the minimum, so the distance is 30 km or possibly more.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The next village is at least 30 kilometers away.
o: The next village is 30 kilometres away, possibly less
The next village is approximately 30 kilometres away
The next village is only 30 kilometres away
The next village is 30 kilometres away, or possibly more

questions.e: 'Thanks to' means 'because of', so the phone call is the reason the visa was obtained.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Thanks to that phone call, I obtain the visa.
o: In spite of that phone call, I obtained the visa
It was because of that phone call that I obtained the visa
I am greatful to whoever phoned me, and I obtained the visa
If I had not receive that phone call, I would not obtained the visa

questions.e: To 'be up to something' means to be secretly planning something, usually mischievous or bad.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Ado and Abu are always together these days. They must be up to something?
o: They must have reconciled after their quarrel
They are probably planning something bad
They are capable of a praiseworthy achievement
They bear some responsibility for what has happened

questions.e: 'Needn't have bought' means the action was done but was unnecessary, so he bought the table, but it wasn't needed.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
He needn't have bought that table?
o: It isn't possible that he bought the table
He bought the table, but it wasn't necessary
He didn't buy the table because it wasn,t necessary
He doesn't need to buy the table

questions.e: 'Too cold for him to go out' means it was so cold that he did not go out.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
It was too cold for him to go out?
o: He had a bad cold, and did not go out
Although it was very cold, he still went out
As it was very cold, he did not go out
He was afraid to go out that day

questions.e: To 'adjourn' a meeting is to suspend it and resume at a later time or another day. It is not cancelled.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
He wants the meeting to be adjourned?
o: He wants the meeting to continue to the next day
He wants the meeting to commence another day

questions.e: 'Vociferous' means loudly vocal in expressing opinions. Being 'one of the vociferous few challenging' the appointment means he is among the people objecting to it.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
My father is one of the vociferous few challenging the company's appointment of the
manager?
o: my father is the one who shouts with a loud voice against the appointment of the manager
My father and others speak on behalf of the company against the appointment of the manager
My father is one of those objecting to the appointment of the manager
My father is agitated by the appointment of the manager

questions.e: The sentence describes a past practice: anyone who actually spoke a language other than English in the school paid ten naira. Merely intending to speak it didn't count.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
In those days in this school, everyone who spoke in a language other than English paid a
fine of ten naira?
o: Everyone of us paid a fine of ten naira because we did not always speak in English
Everyone would pay a fine of ten naira for wanting to use a language other than English
Those who spoke a language other than English on the premises paid a fine of ten naira
Those who intended to speak other language on the school premises were required to pay ten naira

questions.e: A 'vexed issue' is one that has been much discussed and argued about, so the officer added his voice to that debated problem. 'Vexed' here doesn't mean angry.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The officer has discussed the vexed issue of incessant power failure?
o: In anger the officer explained the problem of constant power failure
The officer added his voice to the much discussed problem of power cut
The officer's explanations angered those failures who have suffered the effects of frequent power failure
The officer told the people not to be angered by the frequent power cut

questions.e: To 'steal the show' is to attract the most attention or praise. Here Ado did so in a joint effort.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
It was our collective idea but Ado was doing everything to steal the show.
o: Ado was not part of the planning but he tried rub us of the benefit of it
We planned the show together but Ado was trying to abort it
It was a joint project but Ado is trying to attract the most attention
We collated the idea for the show but Ado was trying to steal the programme

questions.e: To 'pop along' somewhere informally means to go there quickly for a short visit.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
As we watched, he just popped along to the shop for some bread?
o: He has walked slowly to the shop
He stole some bread from the shop but we could not stop him
H e broke into the bread shop before our very eyes
He went quickly to the shop for some bread

questions.e: 'In all ramifications' means in every respect, so his tenure was a total, huge success.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
In all ramifications, Chief Adeyemi was a successful principal of the school?
o: He was partly a failure and partly a success
Everyone admitted that he was largely successful during his tenure
He was not totally successful in the school
His tenure witnessed a huge success

questions.e: 'Hold-up' here means a delay that kept the speaker waiting. The keyed reading is that service was slow. (In other contexts, 'hold-up' can also mean an armed robbery.)
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
I couldn't buy the biscuit because of the hold-up in the supermarket.
o: There was nobody to attend to me

questions.e: Having an 'itching palm' means being greedy for money, especially by taking bribes.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Musa will not do the job well because he has an itching palm?
o: He has rashes in his palm
He is always looking for something to touch
He is always ready to accept bribe
He is tapping people on the back

questions.e: 'Conspicuous by his absence' means his absence was very noticeable. His absence from lectures was glaring.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Emeka was always conspicuous by his absence when it came to attending lectures.
o: That Emeka always attended lectures at school
Emeka absence from lectures was all too glaring
It was obvious that Emeka was not present at lectures
What made Emeka conspicuous was is occasional absence from school

questions.e: 'Friendly fire' is fire from one's own side in a war that accidentally hits one's own troops.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
He was injured by a friendly fire?
o: He was wounded in a war by a friend of his who fired a shot mistakenly
He was injured by a gun shot that was fired by a friend
He was hit in a war by a war weapon fired by his own side
It was a war and he was hit by a bomb fired by an unknown soldier

questions.e: 'On occasions' means only occasionally, not often. The speaker dislikes that Kola visits so rarely.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Kola visits us on occasions, and I don't like that?
o: I do not like Kola because he visits us only when an event is being celebrated
I hate the fact that Kola only visits us when something is being celebrated
That Kola does not visit us often is something I object to
Kola seldom visits us and that is because he is a fair-weather friend

questions.e: 'Lying in third place' means being in third position in a race or competition. It has nothing to do with lying down.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
At the time I arrived, Olu was lying in third place?
o: Olu's third position coincided with my arrival
When I arrived, Olu was sleeping in the space reserved for him
It was a competition and Olu was in third position when I arrived
On my arrived at the competition, Olu went to sleep

questions.e: The sentence means people don't care who governs them, so they are not concerned about who rules.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
People are not interested in who rules?
o: People are not ruled by the leaders they want
People are not concerned about who rules them
The rulers are not concerned about the people
People who rule are not intersested in the ruled

questions.e: Having 'no axe to grind with' someone means having no grievance or grudge against them, so the witness had no hatred for the brothers.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The witness said he had no axe to grind with his brothers?
o: He had no hatred for the brothers
He had no axe and therefore stole the matchet
He had no axe and therefore borrowed their matchet
He had no vested interest in the brothers.

questions.e: To have one's 'tail between one's legs' means to be ashamed and humiliated, typically after a defeat.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The footballers moved with their tails between their legs?
o: They moved happily because they won the match
They were unhappy because they had been despised by their opponents
They were ashamed because they had been defeated
They moved with their tails between their legs

questions.e: To 'talk one's way out of' something is to use persuasive words to avoid an obligation or difficult situation.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The headmaster managed to talk his way out of having to give a speech.
o: He delieverd a speech despite the difficulty
He managed to give a speech out of a difficult situation
He managed to get himself out of a difficult situation
He managed to talk on his way

questions.e: To 'cross the Rubicon' is to take a step that cannot be undone, so we are irrevocably committed.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
As regards the matter, we have crossed the rubicon

questions.e: To be 'full of oneself' means to be very conceited and self-important.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Uche is full of himself?

questions.e: 'Debutants' are first-time participants, and being 'up … by three goals to nil' means leading or winning by that score. So, playing for the first time, they won 3–0.
questions.s:

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

o: She was sad because her husband was absolutely drunk
She was apprehensive that her husband would drink as soon as he recovered fromdrunken stupor

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

o: He was expected but did not show up to make the occasion lively

questions.e: 'Unforeseen circumstances' are unexpected events, so the meeting was shifted for unexpected reasons.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The secretary said that the postponement of the meeting was due to unforeseen
circumstances?
o: The date of the meeting was shifted as a result of unexpected reasons
The meeting's date was off for strange reasons
The meeting was called as a result of obstacles hitherto unknown

questions.e: A 'bird's-eye view' is a view from high above, so the hunter sees the animals from a high position.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The hunter has a bird's eye view of the animals.
o: He views animals from a high position
He views the bird on the tree with one eye
He watches animals and bird's closely

questions.e: 'Wasn't too different from what had been expected' means her result was about as expected, even though she came last.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Even though Susan was the last in the examination, her result wasn't too different from

o: She had not been serious with her studies

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Mrs. Adamu does all her work with more haste, less speed.
o: She accept whatever she does with more haste and speed
She approaches whatever she does hurriedly

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

o: Her uncle refused to help her

questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The plan to upgrade the dispensary to a general hospital did not materialized?
o: The plan did not meet the required specifications
The arrangement did not work out as wished

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Okon's company took a hit last year?

His company was badly damaged last year
His company was established last year

o: only my son is in lagos studying english
my only son is in lagos studying english

Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
If I went to the village I would visit the King.
o: If i go to the village, i will visit the king

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the
information conveyed in the sentence.

the vice chancellor does not enjoy the people's criticism of his administration

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the
information conveyed in the sentence.

o: she was convicted for the charge
she was blamed and charged to court
her case was resolved by the court

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the
information conveyed in the sentence.

o: the landlord gives orders to people
the landlord is respected by his tenants

the management expected the company to issue more than one billion shares

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the
information conveyed in the sentence.

I wouldn't have responded to his rude talk, if l were you

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the
information conveyed in the sentence.
He could not speak out because he had a feet of clay.

Answer the following question below and select the option that best explains the

LEXIS, STRUCTURE AND ORAL FORMS

sentence.

you need a brush from Spain

LEXIS, STRUCTURE AND ORAL FORMS

Amaka would pass for a beauty queen

LEXIS, STRUCTURE AND ORAL FORMS

LEXIS, STRUCTURE AND ORAL FORMS

later in life, Bolu will become an M.C
Bolu may not be the M.C

questions.s: Bridget denied that she wasn't there. This means that
o: She confessed that she wasn't there
She owned up not to be there

questions.e: The third conditional describes the opposite of reality: he did not speak up, so he was given.
questions.s: If he had spoken up, he wouldn't have been given. This means that
o: he spoke up and was given
he wasn't given because he spoke up
he didn't speak up and wasn't given
he was given because he didn't speak up

questions.e: 'To know one's onions' is an idiom meaning to know one's subject or job thoroughly.
questions.s:
**Choose the correct interpretations of the statement given, for questions below**
I know my onions
o: I know my job very well
I am clever because of experience
I am aware of my position

questions.e: Calling a place 'the Mecca' of something means it is a place many people are drawn to visit, as pilgrims go to Mecca.
questions.s:
Choose the correct interpretations of the statement given, for questions below
America is the Mecca of the world
o: America is the commercial garden of the world
America is a beautiful place in the world
America is a place where people like to visit
America accepts assorted races throughout the world

questions.e: Having 'itchy feet' is an idiom for a restless desire to travel or move from place to place.
questions.s:
Choose the correct interpretations of the statement given, for questions below
All the Nigerian footballers have itchy feet
o: the footballers use their feet to steer

questions.e: In the novel's chat language, KOTL stands for 'kiss on the lips'.
questions.s:
**This question is based on Bolaji Abdullahi's Sweet Sixteen**
 
KOTL means ___________

questions.e: A 'swan song' is a person's final performance before death or retirement, so this was the actor's last appearance.
questions.s:
**After each of the following sentences, a list of possible interpretations of all or part**
**of the sentences is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most**
**appropriate for each sentence.**
 
The appearance which the famous actor made last month was his swan song. This meant
that_________
o: the actor sang beautifully during the play
the play was postponed because of the actor's non-appearance
the play was the actor's last appearance before he died
the last play was the actors best performance

questions.e: 'Not letting the grass grow under one's feet' means not wasting time and acting promptly.
questions.s:
**After each of the following sentences, a list of possible interpretations of all or part**
**of the sentences is given. Choose the interpretation that you consider most**
**appropriate for each sentence.**
 
Muiz does not let the grass grow under his feet. This means that Muiz _________
o: does not waste time in doing things
cuts the grass in his field regularly

questions.e: 'By no means a small feat' means it was not easy at all, so Omar's achievement was difficult.
questions.s: Omar's achievement was by no means a small feat. This means that?
o: Omar's achievement was not as difficult as it seems
His accomplishment was not by a small feat

questions.s: I only visited Chidi. This means that
o: I didn't do anything asides visiting Chidi
I didn't go with anyone to visit Chidi
I visited Chidi and his friends

questions.e: An account 'in the red' is overdrawn, holding less than zero; banks traditionally showed debts in red ink.
questions.s: My account with the bank is in the red. This means that my account is

questions.e: 'If he were here' describes an unreal situation: he was absent, so the occasion was not as much fun as it could have been.
questions.s:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence.
If he were here, it could be more fun.
o: He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun
He was expected but did not show up to liven up the occasion
There was no fun because he was not present
He was being expected to supply more fun

questions.e: A 'jaundiced view' is a biased, negative or unfavourable attitude, not a literally sickly one.
questions.s:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence.
Though he is our elected representative, he often takes a rather jaundiced view of our
problems.
o: He takes a rather hazy view of our problems
He takes an unfavourable position concerning our problems
He takes a rather forceful view of our problems
He takes a sickly view of our problems

questions.e: Omar sees passing his SSCE as no small feat because he passed very well at his first attempt.
questions.s:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.
why did Omar say he passed his SSCE by no means a small feat?
o: because he failed other subjects but passed maths and English
because he registered with one of the miracle centers
Because he passed excellently on his first attempt

questions.e: 'At daggers drawn' is an idiom for being bitterly hostile to each other, so they were always angry with each other.
questions.s:
From the list of words in A to D, choose one that best describes the sentence.
James and Henry were at daggers drawn when I knew them. This means that they
o: were always angry with each other

questions.e: Choosing 'between negative alternatives' means the answer is one of several unfavourable options.
questions.s:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence.
The solution lies in choosing between various negative alternatives.
o: The solution lies in choosing between the positive and negative
The solution can be found in one of the negative options
The solution is a negative one

questions.e: "In spite of" means the bad weather did not stop people; a capacity crowd means the stadium was full, so the crowd defied the weather to fill it.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The stadium had a capacity crowd in spite of the weather.
o: The stadium was not filled because of the weather
The crowd defied the weather to fill the stadium
The crowd loved the weather at the stadium
The weather favoured the crowd at the stadium

questions.e: "Biennial" means happening once every two years, i.e. every other year. Don't confuse it with "biannual", which means twice a year.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
The conference is biennial.
o: The conference lasts for two years
The conference is held once every other year
The conference is held twice every year
The conference is held twice in two years

questions.e: To survive a cabinet reshuffle is to keep one's post. If only two survived, every other minister lost their job, i.e. all but two were sacked.
questions.s:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
Only two ministers survived the recent cabinet reshuffle.
o: In recent changes in government, all but two ministers retained their posts
In the recent changes in government, all but two ministers remained alive
In recent changes in government, all but two ministers were sacked
In the recent changes in government, only two ministers were sacked

questions.e: "Gospel truth" is an idiom for something absolutely and completely true, so the information is completely true.
questions.s:
Choose the interpretation that you consider most appropriate for each sentence.
What I told you is the gospel truth. This means that the information is
