questions.e: "Building castles in the air" means daydreaming about a wonderful future that is unlikely ever to happen.
questions.s:
**In the following question, select the option that best explains the information**
**conveyed in the sentence.** 
He was building a castle in the air.
o: He was imagining a terrible future
He was imagining a possible future as a famous architect
He was imagining a wonderful and rather impossible future

questions.e: To play the devil's advocate is to argue the unpopular or opposing side of a case, often just to test the argument.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
Jude appears to sometimes enjoy playing the devil's advocate.
o: Jude seems to enjoy acting as the devil in films
Jude seems to enjoy playing the game
Jude seems to enjoy advancing the unpopular side of an argument
Jude seems to always enjoy appearing differently

questions.e: To "hold one's own" is to cope well and stand firm in a situation, which shows self-confidence.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
Yerima always holds his own in any situation he finds himself.

questions.e: The "cynosure of all eyes" is the person everyone is looking at, the centre of attraction.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
Titi was the cynosure of all eyes at the party.
o: She was the centre of attraction
She was eager to leave the party

questions.e: To let a case "stand over" is to adjourn it to a later date, so the lawyer wants it postponed.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
Let this case stand over for the present, the lawyer pleaded.
o: The case should be discussed immediately
The case should be struck out
The case is pending in court

questions.e: "Helping the police with their investigation" is a polite newspaper way of saying a suspect is being questioned at the police station.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
The paper stated that the driver of the lorry was helping the police in their investigation.
o: joining the police in their investigation
being questioned at the police station
helping the police to drive around
helping the police who were injured

questions.e: "It is not in my place" here means it is not my habit, so the speaker is simply not used to keeping late.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
It is not in my place to keep late, no matter what happens.
o: I am not used to keeping late
I am a habitual latecomer to any event
I do not get to anywhere later than expected
I do not really care whether I get to an event late or not

questions.e: "Neck and crop" means completely or entirely, so Tayo cut himself off totally from his old friend.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
Tayo had to separate himself neck and crop from his old friend.
o: He became scared of his old friend
He became suspicious of his old friend
He completely severed from his old friend
He completely forgave his old friend's offences

questions.e: "Burning the midnight oil" means working or studying late into the night.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
One of the prerequisites for success in examination is burning the midnight oil.
o: needs to study late into the night
one should burn all the candles
one needs to study at will

questions.e: "Improbable" means unlikely to happen, so the sentence means snow in June is highly unlikely, not impossible.
questions.s:
**Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
It is highly improbable that it will snow in June.
o: It is highly unlikely that it will snow in June
It is possible that it will snow in June
It will never snow in June
The snowfall will probably be high in June

questions.e: A "herculean task" is one that needs great effort, matching the idea that driving in Lagos is difficult.
questions.s:
**Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
Driving in Lagos is a difficult task.
o: It is an easy task to drive in Lagos
It is a difficult task driving Lagos
It is a herculean task driving in Lagos
It is not a difficult task to drive in Lagos

questions.e: To be given "a free hand" is to be allowed to act freely without interference, so he can run the business his own way.
questions.s:
**Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
I am given a free hand to run this business.
o: I am allowed to do my own business
I alone can choose my executives

questions.e: To "keep one's fingers crossed" is to hope for a good outcome, so they should remain hopeful the gratuity will be paid.
questions.s:
**Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.** 
The government has promised to pay our gratuity, we need to have our fingers crossed.
o: We should be united in purpose

questions.e: "A stone's throw" is an idiom for a very short distance, so Adeola lives very close to the church.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentences.**
Adeola lives a stone's throw away from the church.
o: He lives where stones are thrown to the church
He lives a long distance from the church
He lives not too close to the church
He lives very close to the church

questions.e: "Speak of the devil" is said when the person being talked about suddenly appears; it says nothing about his character.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentences.
Here he comes, speak of the devil.
o: He is scared of seeing the devil
He is the representation of the devil
He appears as he is being discussed

questions.e: To win "hands down" is to win very easily, without much effort.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentences.
Moses won the contest hands down.

questions.e: To "back up" someone's argument is to support or endorse it.
questions.s:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentences.
I decided to back up my friend's argument at the meeting.

questions.e: The two sentences describe two connected actions with no contrast, so they are joined with "and": travelling and returning next week.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.**
She is travelling to Abuja. She'll return next week.
o: She is travelling to Abuja to return next week
She is travelling to Abuja but returning next week
She is travelling to Abuja to returning next week
She is travelling to Abuja and returning next week

questions.e: If our field is bigger than yours, it follows that your field is not as big as ours; the other options change the meaning or drop "field".
questions.s:
**Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence**
Our school field is bigger than yours.
o: Your school is bigger than ours
Your school is not bigger than ours
Our school field is as big as yours
Your school field is not as big as ours

questions.e: To "call it a day" is to stop working for the day.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence**
The manager told his workers to call it a day.
o: They were told to continue working
They were told to intensify their efforts
They were told to stop working
They were told to pause for a few minutes

questions.e: To be "equal to the task" is to be capable of handling it, so the teacher saw her students as hardworking and able.
questions.s:
**Choose the option that explains the information conveyed in the sentence**
The teacher believed her students were equal to the task.
o: The students were young and weak
The students were hardworking and dedicated
The students were not adequately prepared
The task was very difficult to carry out

questions.e: The proverb means the market is so busy and crowded that one person's absence is never noticed.
questions.s:
The Yoruba proverb "The Oyingbo market never finds out a certain person did not even turn
up" means

questions.e: "Red tape" means excessive official procedures and formality, so red-tapism is excessive bureaucracy found everywhere.
questions.s:
This question is based on Kabir Alabi Garba's The Lekki Headmaster.
"Red-tapism is found everywhere" means
o: Red tape worm is found everywhere

questions.e: An argument that "holds water" is sound; excuses that don't hold water are not logical or believable.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
Tom's excuses don't hold water.
o: The excuses are not logically sound
The excuses are acceptable by a few
The excuses explain the situation well

questions.e: "Hush money" is a bribe paid to keep someone quiet or gain an advantage, so he bribed his way into the job.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
He got a job by paying hush money.
o: He bribed to get the job
He was induced to get the job
He paid exorbitant fee to get the job
He was paid for the job

questions.e: To "throw in the towel" is to give up or admit defeat, so the chairman is telling members not to give up.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
The chairman of the association tells his members not to throw in the towel.
o: They are not to give up
They should be ready for a trip

questions.e: To "tighten one's belt" is to spend carefully and live frugally, so despite his wealth he is careful with money.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
Despite his wealth, Mr Oluboye is known for tightening his belt.
o: He is very careful with his spending
He refuses to wear a belt at all

questions.e: Calling something "a load of crap" is slang for saying it is nonsense or worthless, so they thought the lecture was stupid.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
The students felt the lecture was a load of crap.
o: The students believe the lecture was too long
The students refused to listen to the lecturer
The students thought the lecture was stupid
The students did not attend the lecture

questions.e: To "put a spoke in someone's wheel" is to deliberately hinder their plans.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
The boy accused his friend of putting a spoke in his wheel.
o: He accused his friend of making jest of him
He accused his friend of spoiling his bicycle wheel
He accused his friend of destroying his move of getting a new wheel
He accused his friend of thwarting the execution of his plan

questions.e: A "slave driver" is a boss who works people very hard, as shown by having to work two weekends in a row.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
My boss is such a slave driver, I had to work two weekends in a row.
o: He is a business owner who is very rich
He is a leader who is considerate
He is a taskmaster who overworks employees
He is a manager who is friendly

questions.e: "Cinema, tonight?" is a suggestion, and "Maybe another time" politely declines it while leaving the door open for later.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
"Cinema, tonight?" he asked. "Maybe another time", she replied.
o: He asked her if she will go to the cinema and she vehemently declined it
He suggested taking her to a cinema tonight and she said probably another time
He suggested going to the cinema with her and she agreed
He asked to take her to a cinema tonight and she accepted

questions.e: A "man of letters" is a learned person devoted to literature, i.e. a great literary figure, not someone who writes many letters.
questions.s:
For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the
sentence. 
Peter is a man of letters.
o: He likes to read a lot
He is a great literary artist

questions.e: To "go back to the drawing board" is to start again from the beginning after a plan has failed.
questions.s:
**For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed.**
The coach resolved to go back to the drawing board after their third loss.
o: The coach told the players to study the diagram.
The coach decided to start all over again.
The coach asked the players to copy the notes.
The decided to do the selection again.

questions.e: Explanation (no official key): 'Either ... or' presents two alternatives, of which only one will happen, so if Ada attends the party, Adio will not. Options A and C assert one outcome, and D reverses the logic. Best answer: B.
questions.s:
**In each of the following questions, choose the option that best explains the**
**information conveyed in the sentence.**
Either Adio or Ada will attend the party.
o: If Ada attends the party, Adio will not.
Ada will attend the party but Adio will not
If Adio does not attend the party, then Ada will not attend.

questions.e: To have "a bee in one's bonnet" about something is to be obsessed with it, so he is excessively fond of Aloe Vera products.
questions.s:
**For this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed**
Gbenga has a bee in his bonnet for Aloe Vera products.
o: He painted his car bonnet in attractive colours.
He loves bees made from Aloe Vera products.
He has an excessive love for Aloe Vera products.
The bonnet of his car was damaged by Aloe Vera bees.

**sentence**:

You were asleep so you did not hear the sound

Research

boat

Air

underlined.
Pleasure

Caliph

questions.s: Choose the word that does not have the same vowel sound as the others.

Church

underlined letter(s).
business

Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the
underlined letter(s).
